# Management-Governance Module — TTWO (Synthesis)

## Abstract

Take-Two's leaders are long-tenured and candid about numbers already printed, but they are not aligned stewards of shareholder capital. Five years of capital allocation netted minus $14.6m of free cash flow while the share count rose 61.7%, book value per share fell 42.5%, and $6,665.1m — 84.7% of all goodwill ever recorded — was written off. Pay rewards size, not return on capital; insiders own 0.95%, all granted, and sold $85.2m with zero buys. The biggest signal is structural: $79.5m a year leaves for the CEO's own firm, which supplies him and the President. Audit, contingency and forensic specialists never ran, so those readings are unproven rather than clean. Verdict: misaligned or weak stewardship.

---

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation *(CLAUDE.md §8)*

- **Strongest bear point:** capital allocation, rebuilt from filings rather than inherited — five years of free cash flow netting to **minus $14.6m** while the share count rose **61.7%**, book value per share fell **42.5%** ($32.90 → $18.91), EBITDA per share fell **26.7%** even as absolute EBITDA rose 17.4%, and **$6,665.1m was written off = 84.7% of all goodwill ever recorded** against the Zynga deal at ≈$9,168m (2.3× the pre-deal capital base, 43.2% dilution, $3,248.9m of new debt, $516.1m of cash interest = 91.5% of four years' operating cash flow) [`02`, 02-001 to 02-010, 02-020; `FY26 10-K, Note 9`; `FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Stock Performance Graph`].
- **Strongest bull point (the steelman, and it is real):** the formal governance machinery is better than the verdict implies and the company is not hiding anything findable. Board **90% independent** with all key committees 100% independent, a Lead Independent Director convening eleven independent-only sessions, **one share one vote, 99.6% float, no promoter, no bloc, no pledge anywhere in the record**, **zero** company-level enforcement in five years, **12/12 10-Qs and 4/4 10-Ks on time with zero NT filings in the issuer's entire history**, say-on-pay at **95%**, **4.66% RPT/say-on-pay dissent**, **zero** loans, guarantees, royalties or promoter-linked customers, and **0 of 54 network subjects classified `disclosable-and-omitted`** [`05`; `07` §4; `09`; `12` 12-001, 12-005].
- **Single killer risk specific to stewardship:** **capture, not leakage** (§24 Filter 6 is tested and *not* tripped — there is no controlling owner). The CEO and President are supplied by contract from the CEO's own firm at **$79.5m a year to 2029-03-31**, priced with **no disclosed benchmarking, no peer set and no performance thresholds**, with **no disinterested-shareholder vote**, policed by a board of **12.6-year average tenure** including an audit-committee chair at 12.7 years, and funded through the one plan shareholders pushed back hardest on (**22.40% against, 2025**) with no disclosed board response to that vote.
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** the deal-making that produced the write-down has been **dormant roughly 2.5 years** (business acquisitions $(2.6)m FY2026, **nil** in H1 FY2027) and FY2026's goodwill test passed with no impairment; the **FY2026 operating-cash-flow recovery to +$624.3m** and EBITDA doubling to $788m is one delivered year of inflection; **relative TSR against the NASDAQ-100 over three years, paying zero below the 40th percentile, carries 50.1% of the CEO vehicle's equity at target** — a genuine per-share test with a real floor; and the insider-selling inference is **not proven**: there was **no insider sale between 2026-08-18 and today's launch**, and the two largest CEO sales came *after* the FY26 10-K had already disclosed the November date.

## 3. Reconciliation

Five genuine disagreements. In each case the premise is tested, not inherited, and where a cap's factual premise is false it is **released with the evidence named**; where coverage really is thin the cap **stays**.

**1. Incentive alignment — triage cap of 50 vs `03`'s recommendation of 70. RULING: the cap's premise is FALSE; released and reset at 70, which does not bind.**
The triage's trigger is "No proxy / compensation disclosure." That condition is not satisfied. `03` sourced **audited** `FY26 10-K Note 3` (counterparty, term to 2029-03-31, $3.3m annual fee, $13.2m maximum bonus, $16.6m / $10.2m / $6.5m consulting expense) and `Note 16` (unit counts, grant-date values, metric families, measurement windows); the **actual award agreements were filed WITH the 10-K** as `Ex. 10.8 (TSR)` and `Ex. 10.9 (RCS)` with their **complete Annex A vesting grids in the pool** (40/50/75th percentile → 0/50/100/200%; RCS 3/6/9% → 50/100/200%); and `03` read the **real DEF 14A on EDGAR** (`ttwo-20260727.htm`) for say-on-pay 95%, the clawback's reach to ZMC, and double-trigger-only vesting. That is real, audited, citable pay structure. The residual gap is narrower and genuine — **no Summary Compensation Table, no CD&A weights for the named executives, no primary-source pay ratio, no compensation peer group** — so the cap is **reset to 70, sized to that residual**, rather than removed. `03`'s evidence-built **53** sits below 70, so **the cap does not bind and the composite is unchanged either way** (a literal cap of 50 would move the component three points and the Governance Score by 0.33).

**2. RPT & leakage risk — triage floor of 40 + Confidence 80, which `09` refused to apply. RULING: `09`'s refusal was CORRECT.**
The floor's trigger is "No related-party note / RPT disclosure (A5 not quantifiable)." That premise is false on direct evidence: `FY26 10-K Note 3 — MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT` **is** a related-party note in the audited financial statements, quantified **three years deep**, and the real DEF 14A's "Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions" section names the arrangement and the $275,000-per-month base fee. The triage looked for a note titled "related party" (ASC 850's usual heading); the disclosure sits under its own heading. **A5 IS quantifiable, so the row does not engage.** The practical point `09` makes and I adopt: the derived **44** happens to sit above 40 anyway, but it matters that the number is **derived from evidence, not set by a cap**, because the same false premise also carried a Confidence cap that must not travel. **The Confidence cap of 80 from that row is released too**; the binding Confidence ceiling is `12`'s 75, for a different and real reason.

**3. A2-01…A2-05 and A10-03 recorded "Not Available" by triage. RULING: the gap is CLOSED and the triage record is superseded.**
`05` obtained the real **DEF 14As (2026-07-27 and 2025-07-28)** plus **Item 5.07 voting-results 8-Ks for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual meetings** and answered **25 of 25 owned items (14 Green, 6 Amber, 2 Red, 3 genuine N/A)**. Committee composition, independence, financial expertise, meeting counts, chair rotation and three years of resolution-by-resolution vote counts are all now on the record. No cap on the board read survives. One qualifier `05` imposes on itself travels with it: **the decisive evidence is primary but OUT OF POOL** (read on EDGAR 2026-11-19), and three sub-prongs stayed unreadable even with web access — **private auditor sessions, D&O insurance, and the special-meeting / written-consent ownership thresholds**.

**4. Legal-database sweep caps — the triage recorded its own web lookups as unreachable; `07` and `12` both report access WAS available. RULING: the blanket cap is NOT inherited as written; narrower, evidence-sized caps bind instead.**
The triage's "web/legal-database sweep did not run → People & network integrity max 65 / Legal risk floor 40 / Confidence max 70" and its stricter discovery variant ("People max 60 / Confidence max 75") both rest on "all network hosts denied this run." That was true for the triage and false for `07` and `12`, which reached EDGAR, SEC litigation releases, SEC IAPD, USPTO, OpenSanctions, court aggregators, dated media and the company's own site. So the **A17-01 "loop did not run" cap of 60 does not apply on that ground — the loop DID run** (Phase 1 on 6 of 7 recipes, Phase 2 on 3 entities, which is how the barred founder was found at all). What survives is narrower and real:
- **People & network integrity max 60** — but on a *different* and correctly-evidenced trigger: **declared breadth overflow including Tier-A-controlled entities** (26 hop-1 candidates against a 25-entity limit; six named overflows, four of them Tier-A-controlled). `07`'s uncapped sum of 65 is capped to 60. The coverage-limited sweep cap of 65 is also live and less restrictive.
- **Legal & regulatory risk floor 40** — **retained**, because the coverage genuinely is thin where it matters most: **five primary systems were unreachable** (Law.com paywalled, Trellis 403, UniCourt 405, PACER, state/Chancery e-filing) and the axis A9-10 turns on is exactly the one that did not run. `12`'s own evidence rows build to **25**; the reported **40** is the floor. **The 15-point gap is our access, not a finding against the company**, and the master synthesizer must carry it that way.
- **Confidence max 75** — `12`'s own cap, retained as the binding ceiling.
The triage's **A17-01 "Insufficient Data, explicitly NOT Red"** call is upheld and the distinction preserved: source unavailability is a coverage gap, never the Red band.

**5. `05`'s shareholder friendliness of 70 against its own two Red items. RULING: 70 stands, and the tension is stated rather than averaged.**
The honest reading is that **form and substance diverge**. The formal machinery genuinely earns a low-strong score: 90% independent, all key committees 100% independent, a Lead Independent Director convening eleven independent-only sessions, eleven board meetings, a skills matrix with no gap, annual elections with majority voting and a resignation policy, no pill, no classified board, one share one vote, no supermajority, special-meeting and written-consent rights retained, every resolution across three meetings passed, no director below 90.1% support, and the one pay item that drew 13.9% dissent in 2024 engaged on and fixed to 95.3% by 2026. The two Reds are both about **the same thing**: the board policing the ZMC agreement is not an arm's-length counterparty to the man who has chaired it for eighteen years — combined Chair/CEO (A1-02) and four long-tenured independents including the audit chair (A1-04). `05`'s own verdict word is **"adequate," not "strong,"** and that is what the 70 means: the lower end of the 61–80 band. It is not averaged away — it is carried into the Governance Score at an 0.11 weight against a Capital allocation of 31 at 0.14, which is why the composite lands at 52 / Weak rather than anywhere near the shareholder-friendliness score itself.

**One non-disagreement worth recording, because it could easily be mistaken for one.** `01` did **not** emit RF-MGT-005 (nothing was routed from `business-model/01`, which states "none found, hard or soft … nothing soft to route") while `07` **did** emit it at High on a different item it discovered itself (the Zelnick civil claim). Both are correct on their own facts and they do not conflict: `01` tested the *routed* trigger and `07` tested the *substance* of §24 Filter 1. The flag fires, the cap applies, and `01`'s record stands unamended.

## 5. Stewardship Summary

**(a) Promises and per-share value.** They deliver on the one number they choose to guide and nowhere else: **six-for-six on their own final annual Net Bookings guidance FY2021–FY2026**, against GAAP diluted EPS kept in **1 of 4** years (missed by $16.06 and $21.08) and operating cash flow in **3 of 6** (worst a −99.7% miss, $350m guided and $1.1m delivered). Capital allocation then destroyed per-share value on arithmetic that is not close: **minus $14.6m of five-year free cash flow, share count +61.7%, book value per share −42.5%, EBITDA per share −26.7% while absolute EBITDA rose 17.4%, and $6,665.1m written off = 84.7% of all goodwill ever recorded** — with the company's own five-year scorecard putting $100 at **$111.77 against $169.11 for the NASDAQ Composite**. The best use of capital was debt reduction, and even that carries a qualifier: **the FY2026 $1,150.0m repayment was funded by selling equity at $225.00, not by operating cash.**

**(b) Do incentives and ownership point at per-share value or at size?** At size, with one real exception. The cash bonus (to **$13.2m**) pays on **absolute Adjusted EBITDA**; the second equity metric pays on **Recurrent Consumer Spending, a revenue slice, on whichever of two grids pays more**; a third of the units at target are time-based with no metric; and **nothing anywhere pays on return on capital, earnings per share or cash flow per share while return on capital ran −4.3% / −3.1% / −4.2% / −0.8% across FY2023–FY2026 and −1.0% on the latest twelve months.** The exception is genuine and should not be buried: **relative total shareholder return against the NASDAQ-100 over three years, paying zero below the 40th percentile, carries 50.1% of the CEO vehicle's equity at target.** Ownership points nowhere useful: **0.95% aggregate, CEO plus ZMC 0.72%, every share granted, none bought, $85.2m sold across thirteen open-market sales with zero purchases.**

**(c) Are minority holders protected, and is management candid when results are bad?** Protected in form, exposed in substance. One share one vote, 99.6% float, no promoter, no bloc, **no pledge anywhere in the record**, no poison pill, annual elections with majority voting, every resolution passed across three meetings, and **0 of 54 network subjects classified `disclosable-and-omitted`**. Against that: a **$79.5m-a-year contract supplying the two most senior executives, priced with no disclosed benchmarking, peer set or performance thresholds, with no disinterested-shareholder vote**, policed by a board of 12.6-year average tenure including an audit-committee chair at 12.7 years, and funded through the one plan shareholders pushed back hardest on (**22.40% against, 2025**, with no disclosed response to that vote). On candor the split is sharp and it is the tell: in its worst reported quarter management led with the line it missed and quantified the variance, and disclosed both GTA VI slips against their own superseded dates — yet the **Q1 FY2027 release called a quarter with Net Bookings −3%, recurrent spending −1% and a GAAP loss 186.6% wider "excellent… positive trends"**, and the **legal note of three consecutive filings names zero cases** while the public record holds a **$44.9m adverse IBM verdict against Zynga**, a **five-week UK blacklisting trial with judgment pending today**, and **at least one apparent federal securities class action** that appears in no filing.

**(d) The single most important reason not to trust this team with shareholder capital — and the honest counterweight.** The reason: **they have spent the last five years converting shareholders' ownership into scale that did not earn a return, and the pay structure does not ask them to stop.** $9,856.7m of acquisition consideration and $2,476.7m of capitalised development, funded by $5,196.7m of new debt and $1,449.3m of new equity rather than by the business, against four consecutive years of negative return on capital and a bonus that pays on absolute EBITDA. The counterweight, stated because it is real: the deal-making has been **dormant roughly 2.5 years**, FY2026's goodwill test passed, FY2026 operating cash flow recovered to **+$624.3m**, there has been **no insider sale since 2026-08-17** including through today's launch, and **nothing the engine could reach suggests these particular people are dishonest** — nineteen years of unqualified audit opinions, zero company-level enforcement in five years, and a clean sweep on every person-level axis that was reachable. The live integrity item is **one unresolved, un-adjudicated private civil claim against the chief executive in his personal investment capacity, whose pleadings nobody in this run could read**. That is a monitoring-and-cap finding, not a walk-away — and not a clean bill of health either.

**On the ZMC management agreement (A5-05 Amber, A5-10 Amber, A1-02 Red, A6-01 Red, RF-SHR-001):** Was any benchmarking or peer analysis performed before the $79.5m price was approved, and will it be disclosed? Is the arrangement recurring or does it end at 2029-03-31, and what replaces it? Is it material to earnings and cash — yes: 1.19% of revenue, 9.09% of total G&A, **20.6% of all stock compensation**. Is the disclosure adequate — quantified in Note 3, but the approval policy, benchmarking and performance thresholds are **not readable**. Is it company-specific or sector-wide — **company-specific**; no peer in the sector supplies its CEO by contract from the CEO's own private-equity firm. Does it affect minority holders — yes, through the equity plan they voted **22.40% against**. Is management's explanation credible — there is no explanation to assess, only an assertion of arm's length, and **an assertion is not evidence**.

**On the legal note (A9-10 Amber, A9-11 Amber, 06-012 Red):** **One paid primary-docket pull is the single highest-value next request** — the federal securities class actions over the GTA VI delay disclosures, and the Glasgow Employment Tribunal register for *IWGB v. Rockstar Games UK*. **On incentives (A6-01 Red, A6-04 Amber, A6-05 Amber, 03-010 Red):** Will any returns-based or per-share metric (ROIC, EPS, FCF per share) enter the plan? ## 7. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **The stewardship verdict is "Misaligned or weak stewardship," and the single strongest piece of evidence is arithmetic, not narrative:** five years of free cash flow netting to **minus $14.6m** while the share count rose **61.7%** and **$6,665.1m — 84.7% of all goodwill ever recorded — was written off**, with the company's own five-year table putting $100 at **$111.77 against $169.11 for the NASDAQ Composite**. `02` rebuilt this from the filings rather than inheriting `business-model/11`'s quick-read.
- **Non-Negotiable Gate: PASS, coverage-limited.** No hard disqualifier (`business-model/01` verbatim: *"No disqualifier triggered." · "Any disqualifier triggered: N" · "No lock applies."*); **0 Critical red flags**; **0 current controllers/CEOs/CFOs/chairs graded Disqualifying**; no confirmed material undisclosed legal matter. **One conditional trigger stays live:** confirm a filed securities class action on a court docket and find it still absent from the next periodic filing → RF-CMP-001 fires, candor caps at 50, Governance risk floors at 60, **and the gate must be recomputed**. Do not treat the PASS as settled while that docket is unpulled.
- **Capital allocation destroyed per-share value and the pay structure did not ask it to stop.** BVPS −42.5% ($32.90 → $18.91), EBITDA per share −26.7% while absolute EBITDA rose 17.4%, revenue +89.9% against revenue per share +18.5%, four consecutive years of negative return on capital. Two qualifiers travel with it: the M&A pattern has been **dormant ~2.5 years** and FY2026's goodwill test passed; and the "best use of capital," the $1,150.0m debt repayment, was **funded by selling equity at $225.00, not by operating cash**.
- **Incentives and ownership do NOT align management with minority holders — with one genuine exception.** Cash bonus on **absolute Adjusted EBITDA** (to $13.2m); second equity metric on **Recurrent Consumer Spending**, on whichever of two grids pays more; **nothing on return on capital, EPS or cash flow per share**. The exception: **relative TSR vs the NASDAQ-100 over three years, zero below the 40th percentile, carries 50.1% of the CEO vehicle's equity at target** — better than most. Ownership: **0.95% aggregate, 0.72% for CEO + ZMC (~$291m), every share granted, none bought, $85.2m sold with zero buys.** **The Summary Compensation Table reports the CEO at $403,019 while his firm received $66.8m (proxy basis) / cost $79.5m (audited basis) — anyone reading the standard table understates his economics by roughly two orders of magnitude.**
- **The people read.** 23 subjects: **19 Clean, 1 Minor concerns, 0 Material concerns, 3 Disqualifying**. The riskiest live subject is **Strauss Zelnick**, graded **Minor concerns on his own record** for an **unresolved, un-adjudicated** civil fraud / California-securities claim (LA Sup. Ct. 24STCV20137, stayed to arbitration 2025-02-04) plus a pro se Delaware derivative action. **The three Disqualifying grades belong to the founder and two former officers, all permanently SEC-barred, with every link terminated in 2007 — dated base-rate context on the issuer's own enforcement history, NOT a live finding; RF-NET-003 was tested and explicitly does not fire.** §24 Filter 1 is **open**: RF-MGT-005 fires at High, capping Disclosure candor at 60 and conviction at "no rating above Watchlist." It is a conviction cap, **not a gate failure**.
- **The checklist read.** **114/179 answered (63.7%) — 64 Green · 43 Amber · 7 Red · 65 not available.** The seven Reds: **A1-02** (combined Executive Chairman/CEO), **A1-04** (four IDs past ten years including the audit-committee chair at 12.7), **A6-01** (pay rising 34.1% through four loss years), and **A16-03 / A16-04 / A16-06 / A16-18** — all four of those **historical only, links terminated 2007**. **The binding Checklist Risk is RPT & leakage risk at 44**: max(44, 40 substituted, 40 substituted, 40) = **44**, so the two substituted 40s do not move the composite — but they were entered, not dropped, because unknown is not safe.
- **The biggest governance risk is capture, not leakage, and it is High severity.** **$79.5m a year leaves for the controller's own firm — $16.6m cash consulting expense ($3.3m base fee at $275,000/month plus a bonus at/near its $13.2m cap) plus $62.9m of non-cash stock compensation on RSUs granted to ZMC** — which is 20.6% of all stock comp for two of 12,909 people, 1.19% of revenue, $205.2m over three years, 100% controller-linked. It is priced with **no disclosed benchmarking, peer set or performance thresholds**, carries **no disinterested-shareholder vote**, is policed by a board of **12.6-year average tenure**, and is funded through the one plan shareholders voted **22.40% against** with no disclosed response to that vote. **Carry the build with the total every time, and never treat the $16.6m, $66.8m and $79.5m figures as interchangeable.**

## 8. Simple Summary

- **Promises: half kept.** They hit their own sales target six years out of six — and missed their own profit target in three of the last four years and their own cash target in three of six, once by 99.7%.
- **Capital destroyed value per share.** Over five years the business threw off **minus $14.6m of spare cash** while the number of shares grew **61.7%**. Book value per share fell **42.5%**. Of every dollar of goodwill the company ever recorded, **84.7% has been written off**.
- **Pay rewards getting bigger, not earning a return.** The cash bonus (up to **$13.2m**) pays on total profit before interest, tax and write-offs — a size measure. **Nothing in the pay plan pays on the return earned on the money invested**, which has been negative four years running. The one good part: half the chief executive's shares only pay if the stock beats the NASDAQ-100 over three years.
- **Insiders own almost none of it and have been selling.** Together they own **0.95%** of the company. Every share was given to them; essentially none was bought. In twelve months they sold **$85.2m** across thirteen sales and bought **nothing**. The two most senior executives are supplied to the company by a private firm the chief executive owns and runs, which was paid **$79.5m** last year — while the standard pay table shows his pay as **$403,019**.
- **Minority shareholders are protected on paper, exposed in practice.** One share one vote, no controlling owner, no shares pledged, nine of ten directors independent, every shareholder vote carried. But the **$79.5m contract has no published price comparison and shareholders never vote on it**, and the board approving it has sat together for **12.6 years on average**.
- **Candor is split.** They own a miss once the number is printed — and the written release called a quarter with sales down 3% and a loss 186.6% wider "excellent." **The legal section of three filings in a row names no case at all**, while the public record holds a **$44.9m court loss**, a five-week UK employment trial with judgment due, and an apparent shareholder lawsuit that appears nowhere in the filings.
- **No hard disqualifier was flagged.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`: *"No disqualifier triggered… No lock applies."* The company's founder was convicted and permanently barred — **but that was 2007 and every link ended then**; nobody running the company today has an adverse record on anything we could check.
- **Useful, with three holes you must know about.** **The audit specialist, the contingent-liabilities specialist and the accounting-forensics specialist never ran — the run's budget ran out.** Fifty-three checklist items are **unanswered, not clean**, including the audit-fee test and the whole fraud-detection battery. **Those tests were not run; they were not passed.**

Accounting standard, currency, fiscal year — these travel with every number this module quotes: **US GAAP**, **USD** (millions in the financial statements), fiscal year ends **March 31**. So "FY2026" means the year ended Mar-31-2026, and "Q2 FY2027" means the quarter ended Sep-30-2026 — a US 10-Q is a **standalone three-month period**, not a cumulative half-year, so no cumulative-basis restatement is needed (CLAUDE.md §27).

## Language is not a data gap (CLAUDE.md §27)

Every document in this pool is in English, so no translation was required and no source was discounted for language. Recorded for completeness: had a home-language filing been present it would have counted as **present at the full source tier its type earns**, with figures transcribed verbatim and labels translated — never marked "missing", "not extractable in English", or "opaque". The only genuine reading gap in this pool is the DEF 14A export whose content is empty, and that is handled above as absent content, not as a language or extraction issue.

## External data (frameworks/EXTERNAL_DATA.md)

**No external data in this pool.** `<DATA_PATH>/external/` does not exist; no manifest row carries `external: true`; no `.source.json` provenance object is present. Nothing to list, nothing to tier, no freshness line to flag — and therefore no external document moved the sufficiency verdict, which is the correct outcome in any case: external data is enrichment and never fills a filing, transcript, or deck slot in the sufficiency rule.

The company's own risk factor says it out loud: "Our continued success will depend to a significant extent on our senior management team and **our relationship with ZMC Advisors, L.P.** … Our Executive Chairman/Chief Executive Officer and President **are partners of ZMC**" [`FY26 10-K, Item 1A — We depend on our key management and product development personnel`]. The agreement provides an annual management fee of **$3.3m** and a maximum annual bonus of **$13.2m**, and the company recorded consulting expense of **$16.6m / $10.2m / $6.5m** in FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024 plus stock-based compensation on restricted stock units granted to ZMC of **$62.9m / $56.2m / $52.8m** — **$79.5m combined in FY2026** ($16.6m + $62.9m), or **1.19%** of FY2026 net revenue of $6,656.4m [`FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — Stock-Based Compensation`; revenue per `FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`]. Pricing that arrangement is agent `03`'s (pay) and agent `09`'s (related party); what it means **here** is that continuity in the CEO and President seats is a **contract-renewal question with a stated end date of 2029-03-31**, not an employment relationship — and the agreement itself (Ex. 10.26, filed with the 8-K of 2022-05-05) is **not in the pool**, so its termination, renewal and performance conditions are unreadable.

## 3. Stated Strategy & Targets

Management's stated strategy is unchanged and plainly written: "**Our strategy is to create hit entertainment experiences, delivered on every platform relevant to our audience through a variety of sound business models**", resting on three named pillars — "**creativity, innovation, and efficiency**" — and on a stated aim to "**Increase Scale and Profitability**" by "launching new intellectual properties; growing our core franchises through high-quality, fresh sequels, relevant brand extensions, and robust live services; and expanding our intellectual property portfolio and talent base **through strategic acquisitions and partnerships**" [`FY26 10-K, Item 1 — Strategy Overview` and `Item 1 — Increase Scale and Profitability`]. Capital returns are explicitly not part of it: "We have never declared or paid cash dividends… We currently anticipate that all future earnings will be retained to finance the growth of our business **and pay down our outstanding debt**" [`FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Dividend Policy`], and "During the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026, 2025, and 2024, **we did not repurchase shares**" against a board authorisation of up to 21.7m shares, of which 11.7m have been bought cumulatively and 10.0m remain available [`FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Share Repurchase Program`].

The explicit, checkable targets standing today, all issued **2026-11-09**: FY2027 **Net Bookings $8,000–8,200m** (reiterated, unchanged from the Q1 outlook), FY2027 **GAAP net revenue $7,980–8,180m** (raised), FY2027 **GAAP diluted EPS $0.57–0.75**, FY2027 **capital expenditure approximately $290m**, FY2027 **net cash from operating activities over $1,000m**, and — the one balance-sheet target — "to be in a **net cash position by the end of the fiscal year**"; plus Q3 FY2027 **Net Bookings $3,350–3,500m** and **GAAP diluted EPS $1.30–1.44** [`TTWO 2Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-11-09, "Outlook for Fiscal Year 2027"` and `"Fiscal Third Quarter Ending December 31, 2026"`; `Q2 FY27 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-11-09, prepared remarks (Goldstein)`]. Longer-dated and non-numeric but still checkable: "we expect to **sustain this new level of scale** and generate strong cash flows for the next several years" [`Q1 FY27 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-08-07, prepared remarks`] and continued "**pursuing accretive M&A**" [`Q2 FY27 Earnings Call transcript, 2026-11-09, prepared remarks (Slatoff)`]. **The number that disagrees, named (CLAUDE.md §3).** A reader shown only §4.1 would conclude this team hits its numbers. §4.2 is the series that says otherwise, and it must be addressed by name rather than averaged away. The FY2024 and FY2025 GAAP misses were **$2,342.1m and $3,545.2m of goodwill impairment** — non-cash write-offs attributable to "one of our reporting units", recognised in the two years after the May-2022 Zynga acquisition, which the company itself re-cites as an acquisition consequence: "potential impairment charges incurred to write down the carrying amount of intangible assets generated as a result of an acquisition, such as the Goodwill impairment charge of approximately $3,500 we recognized during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025" [`FY25 10-K, MD&A — Goodwill impairment`; `FY26 10-K, Item 1A`]. Two things follow and both matter: the misses are **not exogenous** — they are the accounting recognition of this same team's own capital allocation; and they are **non-cash**, so they do not by themselves prove operating underperformance. What *does* prove operating underperformance is the cash column beside them — operating cash flow of $1.1m, $(16.1)m and $(45.2)m in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 against guidance of $350m, $90m and $(200)m [`FY26 10-K` and `FY25 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows`; `CIQ Estimates export, Guidance tab`]. The adjudication, plainly: **the top-line promise was kept every year; the cash promise was missed in three of six, once by 99.7%; and the GAAP promise was missed by multiples in the two years the acquisition was written down.** Agent `02` owns the capital-allocation verdict on that acquisition; this agent records its consequence for management credibility.

### 4B. Two pool-integrity corrections this agent is obliged to record

Both bear on findings in this report, so they are stated here rather than left to be rediscovered. Neither contradicts triage `00`'s central point — the proxy really is absent and that really does block compensation, audit fees and AGM voting — but two declared gaps are narrower than recorded.

1. **The ZMC / ZelnickMedia arrangement IS quantified in the audited notes.** Triage `00` records "**No RPT note**" and "RPT quantification **not assessable**", and `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` records "Its dollar amount is not quantified anywhere in this pool." The FY2026 10-K in fact carries **Note 3 — Management Agreement**, with: the counterparty (ZMC Advisors, L.P.), the effective date (2022-05-23), the term (through **2029-03-31**), the annual management fee (**$3.3m**), the maximum annual bonus (**$13.2m**, performance-conditioned), consulting expense recorded in General and administrative expenses of **$16.6m / $10.2m / $6.5m** for FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024, and stock-based compensation on restricted stock units granted to ZMC of **$62.9m / $56.2m / $52.8m** [`FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — Stock-Based Compensation`]. It is not labelled a related-party note and Item 13 is still incorporated by reference to the absent proxy — so the audit-committee approval policy, the benchmarking, and the performance thresholds remain unreadable — but the **economics are disclosed and dated**. Agent `09` should quantify from Note 3 and must **not** record the arrangement as unquantified; agent `03` should read Note 3 before concluding that no pay data exists at all. `business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance.md` already found and used this note ($79.5m combined FY2026 cost, 1.19% of revenue), which corroborates the read.
2. **Some committee seats ARE identifiable, as a vendor lead rather than a clean roster.** Triage `00` records "**Not a single committee seat is identifiable from this pool**". The CIQ Board Members export's **"Job Functions"** field in fact names committee roles for 9 of the 10 directors — for example Tolson "Member of Audit Committee, **Chairman of Audit Committee**"; Sheresky "**Chairman of Compensation Committee**"; Moses "Member of Audit Committee, Member of Compensation Committee, **Chairman of Corporate Governance Committee**"; Srinivasan "**Chairman of Executive Committee, Lead Director**"; Siminoff and Viera "Member of Audit Committee"; Gordon board-only [`CIQ Board Members export (tab: Board Members), Job Functions field`]. The field is **not** a clean current roster: it mixes current and prior roles (Dornemann carries both "Chairman of Compensation Committee" and "Lead Director", a seat the same export elsewhere says he held "until September 2023"), it is a tier-4 vendor field rather than a filing, and it gives no meeting counts, no independence determination and no financial-expert designation. Agent `05` should treat it as a **corroborating lead** for A2-01/A2-05 — enough to say the committees exist and who chairs them, not enough to grade composition — and should not record committee membership as wholly unavailable.

## 5. Management Read

**Tenure and stability are exceptional and not in question: one CEO for 15.9 years, one CFO for 19.4 years, one President for 13.5 years, and no Section-16 officer or director departure in nine years** — the opposite of the churn this test screens for, though the *completeness* of that departure record is capped by the pool holding no 8-K and no TTWO material-event history at all. **The record splits sharply by which promise you measure.** On the metric management chooses to headline — Net Bookings — it met or beat its own final annual guidance in **six consecutive years, FY2021 through FY2026**, the strongest single fact in this report. On the lines it does not headline it missed repeatedly and by large margins: GAAP diluted EPS kept in only **1 of 4** years FY2023–FY2026 (missed by **$16.06** in FY2024 and **$21.08** in FY2025, behind **$2,342.1m and $3,545.2m** of goodwill write-offs on its own acquisition), operating cash flow kept in only **3 of 6** including a **−99.7%** miss in FY2023 (guided $350m, delivered $1.1m), and capex overran its own guidance by about **20%** in two of six years.

**The single biggest management signal is negative, and it is a product promise, not a financial one:** *Grand Theft Auto VI* slipped from "**Fall of Calendar 2025**" to "**May 26, 2026**" to "**November 19, 2026**" — roughly **13–14 months across two revisions**, both disclosed in the filings against the company's own prior dates rather than quietly re-based [`FY25 10-K, Item 1`; `FY26 10-K, Item 1`]. The whole FY2027 case — Net Bookings of $8,000–8,200m, operating cash flow over $1,000m, a swing to a net cash position — rests on that one title, which launched **today, 2026-11-19**, with pre-orders described as "far in excess of our initial expectations" and **not quantified anywhere in this pool**. So the position is blunt: this is a stable, long-tenured, candid team with a near-perfect record on the number it guides, a poor record on cash and GAAP earnings, one year of delivered operating improvement (returns still negative at **−0.8%** in FY2026 and **−1.0%** on the latest twelve months), and an unverifiable launch carrying the next twelve months. Competence at hitting a self-chosen top-line target is proven; competence at converting it into returns on capital is not.

## management-governance / 02_capital-allocation-scorecard.md

_Source: `02_capital-allocation-scorecard.md`_

# Capital-Allocation Scorecard — TTWO

**Jurisdiction / regime:** United States, SEC domestic filer (Form 10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A), US GAAP, reporting currency **USD**, fiscal year ends **March 31** — "FY2026" means the year ended March 31, 2026 [FY26 10-K, cover page]. All figures below are **USD millions** unless marked per share. Share counts in millions.

**Window scored:** FY2022–FY2026 (five fiscal years), extended to the six months ended September 30, 2026 where the 10-Q adds a fact. The governance triage recorded a 10-year capital-allocation history as present in the pool, so the "no multi-year history" partial-data rule does **not** apply and the single-period cap is **not** used.

**Definitions used (CLAUDE.md §15).**
- **FCF = CFO − purchases of fixed assets.** Note the company-specific wrinkle: TTWO's *capitalised game-development spend* ($688.9m in FY2026) sits **inside operating activities**, not in investing [FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. So reported CFO is already net of its largest growth outlay, and fixed-asset capex is the only investing capex to subtract. Where the vendor's own "Levered Free Cash Flow" ($1,447.8m FY2026; $787.6m LTM Sep-26) is quoted it is flagged as a **vendor-defined, after-interest** figure that is not the §15 FCF — the sidecar labels it that way itself [`ciq_facts.json` `levered_fcf_m` — CIQ Financials→Cash Flow, LTM Sep-30-2026 — vendor export].
- **Net debt (strict)** = total debt − cash equivalents. The vendor's $1,237.8m is a **broad / CIQ basis** (nets liquid investments and includes ~$0.4bn of lease liabilities in total debt) [`ciq_facts.json` `net_debt_m`]. Filing-based strict net debt at Sep-30-2026 is **$1,370.4m** (borrowings $2,519.8m − cash and cash equivalents $1,149.4m) [Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets].
- **Invested capital** = total debt + book common equity ("Total Capital") [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization — vendor export].
- **ROIC** = return on invested capital, i.e. the profit earned on each $100 of capital put into the business.

**Reading-check status (hard limitation, carried forward).** This extract generation carries **no `numeric_reading_check` on any source or any sheet** (`manifest.json` — zero occurrences of the key; zero warning tokens). **Every reading below is therefore unchecked, and none of it may be described as reading-verified.** No warning token, source/extract reference or LF-line span exists to preserve, because none was emitted. Confidence scores in the findings table are set accordingly. One genuine extraction gap was found and is treated as a reading gap, not as a company finding: see finding 02-027 (the Gearbox purchase-consideration component table).

**Other data limits stated up front.**
1. **No DEF 14A content.** The proxy export is an empty shell ("This filing has no tabular data to export") [`Take-Two_Interactive_Software_Inc_-_Form_DEF_14A(Jul-27-2026).xls`]. The board's capital-allocation oversight, stock-ownership guidelines, and 10b5-1 plan status are **not proven from available data**. The scorecard itself does not depend on it — the cash-flow statements and both 10-Ks are present.
2. **No FY2022 10-K in the pool.** FY2022 CFO, capex, cash acquisitions and the FY2022 "repurchase" line are **vendor-sourced (tier 5)**, not filing-confirmed, and are labelled every time they appear.
3. **No TTWO material-event history.** There is no 8-K, no S-4 and no merger press release in the pool, and the CIQ "Key Developments" export is **Alphabet Inc.'s, not TTWO's** [`Alphabet Inc NasdaqGS GOOGL Key Developments.xls` — wrong issuer, not read as TTWO evidence]. So the *announced* rationale and any quantified synergy target for Zynga and Gearbox are not readable here. The deal **outcomes** are fully readable from the 10-Ks.
4. **Pre-order volumes for *Grand Theft Auto VI* are unquantified anywhere in the pool.** The launch happened today (2026-11-19). Its outcome is **not proven**.
5. **The valuation module has not run.** Intrinsic-value buyback discipline is therefore not assessable from this module (see §3).

## 1. Uses of Capital (3–5 years)

**Reporting currency: USD.** Cumulative FY2022–FY2026 (five fiscal years ended March 31, 2026).

Cumulative **CFO** over the window is **$822.1m** — the denominator for the percentages below. That small number is the whole story of this table: the money spent did not come from the business.

**Where the money actually came from (sources, same five years).** CFO $822.1m + debt issued $5,196.7m (FY23 3,248.9 + FY24 1,348.9 + FY25 598.9) + equity issued for cash $1,449.3m (FY22 19.7 + FY23 65.4 + FY24 39.4 + FY25 77.3 + FY26 1,247.5) + divestiture proceeds $32.7m = **$7,500.8m** [FY25 10-K and FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows; FY2022 line vendor export]. On that base: acquisitions 47.3%, debt repaid 51.5%, capex 11.2%, buybacks 3.5%, dividends 0.0% — summing to 113.5%. The 13.5% gap is **not** a hidden use of capital: it is the fall in cash and short-term investments from $2,552.1m (Mar-31-2022) to $1,989.3m (Mar-31-2026) [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization — vendor export] plus movements between cash, bank time deposits and marketable securities, which shuffle money between near-cash forms rather than deploy it. The sources-and-uses bridge is therefore **approximate**, and is labelled as such.

**The single most important number in this section: five-year free cash flow.** On the §15 basis (CFO − purchases of fixed assets):

| Year | CFO | − Fixed-asset capex | = FCF | Source |

| FY2025 | (45.2) | 169.4 | **(214.6)** | FY26 10-K |
| FY2026 | 624.3 | 162.8 | **461.5** | FY26 10-K |
| **Cumulative** | **822.1** | **836.7** | **(14.6)** | — |

Five years of free cash flow nets to **minus $14.6m** — effectively nothing — while $9,856.7m of acquisition consideration was committed and the share count rose 60.3%. H1 FY2027 is worse again: CFO of **$(173.5)m** against $83.7m a year earlier, with $372.4m of capitalised development and $163.3m of fixed-asset capex [Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows] — the pre-launch build for *Grand Theft Auto VI*.

### Serial-acquirer + opportunity-cost test (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 4)

The upstream quick-read (`business-model/11_capital-allocation-governance`) scored this signal 75 and carried RF-CAP-004 into the triage. This module is the dedicated deep-dive and **supersedes** that quick-read. I rebuilt the test from the filings rather than inheriting it. **It trips, and it trips on arithmetic, not on style.**

**Frequency and size.** Two material deals in four fiscal years. Zynga's ≈$9,168m build compares with the company's own **total capitalization of $4,059.9m** (total debt $250.2m + book equity $3,809.7m) at March 31, 2022 — **about 2.3x the entire pre-deal capital base** [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization — vendor export]. The 50.0 shares issued were **43.2% of the 115.8 shares outstanding before the deal**.

**Debt-funded.** $3,248.9m of long-term debt was issued in FY2023, taking total debt from **$250.2m (Mar-31-2022) to $3,682.1m (Mar-31-2023)** and later to a peak of **$4,122.3m (Jun-30-2024)** [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization and Cash Flow — vendor export; FY25 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. A debt-funded deal at roughly twice the company's own pre-deal capital base is precisely the condition Filter 4 names.

**Outcome, in the company's own numbers.** $6,665.1m of acquisition-related write-downs — **84.7% of every dollar of goodwill the company has ever recorded**. The company itself ties the charge to the deal: "potential impairment charges incurred to write down the carrying amount of intangible assets generated as a result of an acquisition, such as the Goodwill impairment charge of approximately $3,500 we recognized during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025" [FY26 10-K, Item 1A]. **One qualifier must travel with that attribution:** the FY2026 10-K attributes the goodwill impairments to "one of our reporting units" **without naming it**; the FY2025 10-K separately attributes the *intangible* impairments to the Zynga acquisition. So the Zynga attribution is explicit for the intangibles and strongly implied but **not named in the filing** for the $5,887.3m of goodwill.

**Opportunity cost, charged (not just the deal's own loss).** Three charges, each cited above and each a real cost of the deal rather than a footnote to it: (a) a **label sold** — Private Division and its title rights, at an $11.4m loss, for $32.7m; (b) **focus and people removed** — studios shut, two titles' development terminated, several rounds of layoffs, all under the cost programme that followed; (c) **$516.1m of cash interest over four years, equal to 91.5% of the CFO those four years produced** — money that existed as an obligation only because the deal was part-financed with debt. Bare "synergies / strategic fit" language was credited nowhere above.

**The moderating fact, stated plainly.** The deal-making has stopped. Business acquisitions were $(2.6)m in FY2026 and **nil** in the six months to September 30, 2026 (against $(2.0)m a year earlier) [FY26 10-K and Q2 FY27 10-Q, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. No new material transaction is disclosed in either FY2027 10-Q or either FY2027 earnings release. Goodwill was **not** impaired in FY2026 and the FY2026 test passed: "our qualitative and quantitative assessments indicated that it is more likely than not that the fair value of our reporting units exceeds their carrying amounts" [FY26 10-K, Note 9]. The pattern has been dormant for roughly two and a half years.

**Verdict: RF-CAP-004 confirmed on the historical record, dormant on current conduct.** The M&A discipline component is capped per the MODULE_RULES rejector table, and the serial-acquirer pattern is **named as the most material capital-allocation signal** — not because deals are still happening, but because the write-down it produced is still the largest single fact in this company's capital history and still sits on the balance sheet as $1,061.9m of residual goodwill and $1,631.2m of acquired intangibles.

## 3. Buyback Scorecard

**Module boundary (stated as required).** This module runs **before** valuation. **Intrinsic-value discipline is not assessable from this module** — the valuation module has not run, and no fair-value range exists to judge a buyback price against. Everything below is judged only on observable evidence: net share-count change, price versus the actual trading range, whether leverage rose, whether stock-comp dilution was offset, and whether insiders benefited disproportionately.

| Year | Amount Spent | Currency | Shares Bought | Implied Avg Price | Share-Count Change | Offset SBC Dilution? | Price-Discipline Evidence | Judgment | Source |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | 264.1 | USD m | **Not disclosed in pool** | **Not determinable** | 115.4 → 115.8 (+0.4%) | No | Share price traded $123.08–$192.91 across the four quarters of FY2022; no per-trade price is in the pool | **Insufficient Data.** No FY2022 10-K exists in the pool, so whether this line is an open-market repurchase or RSU tax-withholding cannot be established | CIQ Financials_Annual → Cash Flow "Repurchase of Common Stock" and Historical Capitalization — vendor export |
| FY2023 | **0.0** | USD m | 0 | n/a | 115.8 → 169.3 (**+46.2%**) | **No** | Program idle through the year the share count rose 46% | **Red** | "During the fiscal years ended March 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, we did not repurchase shares of our common stock" [FY25 10-K, Item 5] |
| FY2024 | **0.0** | USD m | 0 | n/a | 169.3 → 171.4 (+1.2%) | **No** | Program idle; 2.1 shares of restricted stock issued net of forfeitures | **Red** | FY25 10-K, Item 5; FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity |
| FY2025 | **0.0** | USD m | 0 | n/a | 171.4 → 177.4 (+3.5%) | **No** | Program idle; 2.4 restricted shares + 0.4 ESPP + 0.6 options + 2.8 Gearbox shares issued | **Red** | FY26 10-K, Item 5; FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity |
| FY2026 | **0.0** | USD m | 0 | n/a | 177.4 → 185.7 (+4.6%) | **No** | Program idle **while the company sold 5.5 shares at $225.00**; Jan/Feb/Mar-2026 monthly repurchase table shows nil in every month with 10.0 shares still available | **Red** | FY26 10-K, Item 5 (Summary Table); FY26 10-K, Note 12 |
| H1 FY2027 | **0.0** | USD m | 0 | n/a | 185.7 → 187.2 (+0.8%) | **No** | Only equity cash flow is a $(1.9)m RSU tax payment and $32.3m of stock issuance | **Red** | Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows |

**Four facts that settle this section.**

1. **The program exists and has been left idle.** "Our Board has authorized the repurchase of up to 21.7 shares… As of March 31, 2026, we had repurchased a total of 11.7 shares… and 10.0 shares of our common stock remained available" [FY26 10-K, Item 5]. Treasury stock has been **frozen at 23.7 shares / $(1,020.6)m from March 31, 2022 through September 30, 2026** — independent confirmation that no shares were added [FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity; Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets].
2. **Average price paid — stated, with its basis.** No year-by-year average price is disclosed and none is computable for FY2023–FY2026 because the numerator and denominator are both zero. The only computable figure is the **cumulative implied cost of all treasury shares ever bought: $1,020.6m ÷ 23.7 shares = $43.06 per share** [FY26 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets — undated, multi-programme cumulative basis, not attributable to any single year]. Against today's $216.61 [`ciq_facts.json` `current_price` — CIQ Comps→Financial Data, as-of 2026-11-19], historic repurchases were made far below the current price — but that tells you about a decade-old programme, not about conduct in the window scored here. For FY2022, **the average price is not determinable.**
3. **A vendor-mapping error that must not travel (§5).** The CIQ cash-flow export shows "Repurchase of Common Stock" of $108.1m (FY23), $94.1m (FY24) and $2.9m (FY26). Those three figures reconcile **exactly** to the 10-K's own line "**Tax payment related to net share settlements on restricted stock awards**" — $108.1m, $94.1m and $2.9m [FY25 10-K and FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. They are shares withheld to pay employees' taxes when restricted stock vests, **not buybacks**, and the filings say in terms that no shares were repurchased in those years. Anyone reading the vendor line as a buyback would record $205.1m of returns to shareholders that did not happen.
4. **Dilution was not offset — it was compounded.** Shares outstanding went **115.8 (Mar-31-2022) → 185.7 (Mar-31-2026) → 187.2 (Sep-30-2026), +61.7%** [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization — vendor export; `ciq_facts.json` `shares_outstanding_m`]. Weighted-average basic shares rose 170.1 (FY24) → 175.1 (FY25) → 183.9 (FY26) [FY26 10-K, Note 12]. Compensation-related issuance alone over FY2024–FY2026 was roughly **8.7 shares** (restricted stock net of forfeitures 2.1 + 2.4 + 2.5; ESPP 0.4 + 0.4 + 0.3; options 0.6) against stock-compensation expense of $335.6m, $324.0m and $305.3m [FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. **None of it was offset.** Of the FY2026 $305.3m of stock compensation, **$62.9m (20.6%) was granted to ZMC Advisors L.P.**, the outside firm that supplies the CEO and President [FY26 10-K, Note 3 and Note 16; per agent `03`].

**The one genuinely favourable price-conduct fact, and it belongs on the other side of the ledger.** On **May 22, 2025 the company issued 5.5 shares at a price to the public of $225.00, raising $1,192.8m net** [FY26 10-K, Note 12], and used it to retire $1,150.0m of notes. That price is **3.9% above today's $216.61** and was struck within 5% of the highest quarterly close in the company's history ($237.50 at the May-2025 pricing date) [CIQ Financials_Annual → Historical Capitalization, Share Price series — vendor export]. Issuing stock high is the mirror image of buying it low, and it is price discipline on the issuance side — it is credited. But it also means the plain description of this company over the window is that it was a **net seller of its own equity** to continuing holders, not a buyer.

**Leverage and insider context.** The share-count increase did not coincide with rising leverage — total debt fell from the $4,122.3m peak to $2,911.4m (vendor basis, incl. ~$0.4bn of leases) at Sep-30-2026, and total debt / EBITDA from 8.77x (FY2025) to 3.64x (LTM Sep-26) [CIQ Financials_Annual → Ratios and Historical Capitalization — vendor export; `ciq_facts.json`]. Insiders were sellers across the same stretch: **net insider selling of $85.2m across 13 open-market sales with zero buys**, insider ownership **0.95%** of which the CEO + ZMC hold 0.72%, **all granted, none bought** (agent `04`). Among those sales, ZMC Advisors L.P. sold 148,711 shares at $227.40–231.01 on 2026-06-01 [CIQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading — vendor export]. No buyback existed for insiders to tender into, so this is **not** a mechanism-abuse finding — but the company and its insiders were on the same side of the trade, selling, while no capital was returned to continuing holders.

## 4. Dividends & Organic Reinvestment

| Metric | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Payout ratio | **0.0%** — no dividend has ever been paid | "We have never declared or paid cash dividends" [FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Dividend Policy]; Total Dividends Paid nil FY2017–FY2026 [CIQ Financials_Annual → Cash Flow — vendor export] |
| Dividend coverage (FCF) | **Not applicable** — nothing to cover. For scale: five-year cumulative FCF was **$(14.6)m**, so any payout would have had to be debt- or equity-funded | §1 FCF table [FY25 10-K, FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows] |
| **Documented dividend policy exists? Followed for ≥4 years? (A10-01)** | **Yes / Yes — Green.** A policy is set out under its own heading: "We currently anticipate that all future earnings will be retained to finance the growth of our business and pay down our outstanding debt. We do not expect to declare or pay any cash dividends in the foreseeable future. The payment of dividends in the future is within the discretion of our Board and will depend upon future earnings, capital requirements and other relevant factors." Followed without deviation for **at least 10 consecutive years** (FY2017–FY2026) and, on the company's own statement, for its entire history. **No payout exceeds FCF and nothing is debt-funded** — the red band cannot fire | FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Dividend Policy; CIQ Financials_Annual → Cash Flow, "Total Dividends Paid" row, FY2017–FY2026 columns — vendor export |
| **Incremental ROIC (Δ NOPAT / Δ invested capital)** | **−25.9% (pre-tax basis)** — Mar-31-2022 → Mar-31-2026: Δ operating income = $(79.5) − $545.0 = **$(624.5)**; Δ invested capital = $6,469.2 − $4,059.9 = **+$2,409.3**; **−624.5 ÷ 2,409.3 = −25.9%** | CIQ Financials_Annual → Income Statement ("Operating Income") and Historical Capitalization ("Total Capital") — vendor export |

**Reading the incremental return honestly.** Three qualifiers travel with the −25.9%. (a) It is a **pre-tax operating-income** basis, not NOPAT — tax expense was a credit in two of the four loss years, so a tax-effected figure is not meaningfully computable and a NOPAT version would be negative either way. (b) The vendor's "Operating Income" **excludes** the goodwill impairments and asset write-downs (they sit in unusual items); including them makes the number **worse**, not better — on an all-in pre-tax basis (EBT including unusual items, $465.4m → $(197.8)m) the incremental return is **−27.5%**. (c) It is a two-point measurement across a period in which capital first ballooned and then was written down; the intermediate path is worse again (Mar-2022 → Mar-2023: Δ operating income $(1,121.2)m ÷ Δ capital $+8,469.6m = **−13.2%**). **Every version of the calculation says the same thing: each extra dollar of capital put into this business since March 2022 is associated with less operating profit, not more.**

**The level, not just the increment.** ROIC by year: 9.0% (FY2022) → **−4.3% (FY2023) → −3.1% (FY2024) → −4.2% (FY2025) → −0.8% (FY2026) → −1.0% (LTM Sep-30-2026)** [`ciq_facts.json` `multi_year_trajectory` — CIQ Financials_Annual → Ratios — vendor export]. **Four consecutive full fiscal years of negative return on capital, with the latest twelve months still negative** — independently corroborating agent `03`'s finding, which also established that **nothing in the pay structure pays on return on capital**. The trend inside that is improving (−4.2% → −0.8%), and that qualifier travels.

**Organic reinvestment — where the real money went, and what is riding on it.** Capitalised game development absorbed **$2,476.7m over FY2023–FY2026**. Put against the cash the operations generated before that spend — CFO of $564.1m plus the $2,476.7m that was deducted inside it = **$3,040.8m of gross operating cash** — development took **81.4% of everything the business produced**. Fixed-asset capex of $162.8m ran at **0.98x** depreciation of $166.4m, i.e. pure maintenance, with FY2027 capex guided to $200.0m [FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows; FY26 10-K, MD&A — Capital Expenditures].

The resulting asset and its concentration: capitalised software development and licences of **$2,277.5m non-current at March 31, 2026**, of which **$2,149.7m (94.4%) relates "to titles that have not been released"** [FY26 10-K, Note 7]. It grew again to **$2,494.9m at September 30, 2026** after a further $372.4m of H1 FY2027 spend [Q2 FY27 10-Q, Note 7 and Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows]. The asset has been impaired in two of the last three years — **$109.9m (FY2024), $77.5m (FY2025), $(1.0)m (FY2026, a net recovery)** — with the FY2024 and FY2025 charges tied to the cost-reduction programme and to "a decision not to proceed with further development of certain interactive entertainment software products" [FY26 10-K, Note 7]. Two technical notes travel with the balance: government production grants have **reduced** the carrying amount by $233.2m cumulatively, and the FY2026 amortisation-and-impairment line of $412.8m is net of a $27.9m stock-compensation portion [FY26 10-K, Note 7].

**Judged against the *Grand Theft Auto VI* record, as instructed.** The title slipped roughly **13–14 months across two disclosed revisions**: the FY2025 10-K recorded it as "expected to launch in Fall of Calendar [2025]" and then "Rockstar plans to release Grand Theft Auto VI on May 26, 2026" [FY25 10-K, Item 1 and Item 7]; the FY2026 10-K moved it to November 19, 2026 [FY26 10-K, Item 1 and Item 7]; the Q2 FY2027 10-Q confirmed it [Q2 FY27 10-Q, Item 2]. It **launched today, 2026-11-19**. What is **proven**: the slip, the two revisions, the $2,149.7m of unreleased-title cost sitting on the balance sheet, the $372.4m of further H1 FY2027 spend, the H1 FY2027 CFO of $(173.5)m, and the CEO's statement ten days before launch that "we do track awareness and anticipation, and everything is trending very positively" [Q2 FY27 earnings call, 2026-11-09, Q&A]. What is **not proven**: anything about the outcome. **Pre-order volumes are unquantified anywhere in this pool**, no units, bookings or sell-through figure exists, and the delay is the only hard reinvestment datum the window supplies. A reinvestment programme that has consumed 81.4% of gross operating cash, produced negative returns on capital for four years, and parked 94.4% of its asset in one unreleased title is a **concentrated bet whose result is simply not yet in evidence** — and the honest read is that it must be scored on the record so far, not on the launch.

**One watch item that would flatter the cash line.** A $215.0m uncommitted accounts-receivable purchase facility was opened May 19, 2025 and was **unused** in FY2026; by the company's own stated accounting, proceeds if drawn "will be reflected as cash provided by operating activities" [FY26 10-K, Note 2]. Drawing it would lift reported CFO without the operations producing more cash.

## 4A. Distribution Conduct (A10-05)

**There was no buyback and no dividend in the window.** FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 each had zero repurchases [FY25 10-K and FY26 10-K, Item 5] and no dividend has ever been paid [FY26 10-K, Item 5]. **Total capital returned to shareholders over the five years scored: $0 in FY2023–FY2026, and a vendor-recorded $264.1m in FY2022 whose basis cannot be confirmed.** Over the same five years the company *took in* $1,449.3m of equity from shareholders. The A10-05 conduct test therefore has very little to bite on, and is graded on that narrow basis.

| Test | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism rationale stated (dividend vs buyback, who benefits)? | **Yes — Green, narrow basis.** The 10-K states the choice and the reason: "all future earnings will be retained to finance the growth of our business and **pay down our outstanding debt**", and separately that the repurchase programme "does not require us to repurchase shares and may be suspended or discontinued at any time". The stated rationale is consistent with what actually happened — $1,150.0m of debt repaid in FY2026 — and is coherent given five-year cumulative FCF of $(14.6)m. **However:** zero capital-allocation commentary appears in **either** FY2027 earnings call or **either** FY2027 earnings release — the words buyback, repurchase, dividend, capital allocation, pay down and deleveraging appear **nowhere** in the Q1 FY2027 (2026-08-07) or Q2 FY2027 (2026-11-09) transcripts or the Q2 FY2027 release, including the prepared remarks. So the policy is disclosed in the annual filing but is not being discussed with shareholders in the current year | FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Dividend Policy and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities; FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows; Q1 FY27 earnings call 2026-08-07 and Q2 FY27 earnings call 2026-11-09 (full transcripts incl. Presentation section — searched, nil); TTWO 2Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-11-09 (searched, nil) |
| Promoter participation in any buyback (tender/open-market) | **Not Applicable — none possible.** No buyback or tender occurred in the window, and there is **no promoter or controlling shareholder**: Delaware-incorporated, NASDAQ-listed, largest holder BlackRock, Inc. at 16,249,491 shares (8.7% of 187.2 outstanding). Insider ownership is 0.95% in total (agent `04`). The related conduct fact, recorded but **not** an A10-05 trigger: ZMC Advisors L.P. — the firm that supplies the CEO and President — **sold** 148,711 shares at $227.40–231.01 on 2026-06-01, part of net insider selling of $85.2m across 13 open-market sales with zero buys | FY26 10-K, cover page; `ciq_facts.json` `top_institutional_holders`; CIQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading — vendor export; agent `04_ownership-and-insider-behavior` |
| Buyback timing vs promoter pledge / stake changes | **Not Applicable** — no buyback, no promoter, and share pledging/encumbrance disclosure does not exist in this regime (there is no US equivalent of the SEBI SAST pledge filing for a company with no controller) | FY26 10-K, cover page; MODULE_RULES Jurisdiction-Aware Source Mapping |

**A10-05 verdict: Green (narrow basis).** A documented rationale exists, it matches the cash flows, and no mechanism was used in a way that could favour an insider — because no mechanism was used at all. This is **not** a finding that distribution conduct is good; it is a finding that the specific abuse A10-05 tests for did not occur. The substantive criticism of the distribution record — $0 returned, $1,449.3m raised, a 61.7% larger share count, and a 10.0-share authorisation left idle — is scored in §3 and in the buyback-discipline component, not here.

## 5. Capital-Allocation Read

**Capital allocation has destroyed per-share value, and the arithmetic is not close.** Since March 2022 the company has put roughly $9,856.7m of acquisition consideration and $2,476.7m of capitalised game development to work, funded almost entirely by $5,196.7m of new debt and $1,449.3m of new equity rather than by the business — which produced **minus $14.6m of cumulative free cash flow over five years**. The results, per share: **book value per share fell 42.5%** ($32.90 at Mar-31-2022 to $18.91 at Mar-31-2026), **EBITDA per share fell 26.7%** ($5.79 to $4.24) even as *absolute* EBITDA rose 17.4%, **basic EPS went from $3.62 to $(1.62)** with four straight loss years, and **revenue grew 89.9% while revenue per share grew 18.5%** — dilution ate roughly four-fifths of the growth. Tangible book value per share is now **negative $6.55**, against a peer-set median of **+$3.20**, and **8 of the 10 peers carry net cash while TTWO carries net debt** [CIQ Comps → Financial Data, as-of 2026-11-19 — vendor export]. The market's own scorecard agrees: $100 invested on March 31, 2021 was worth **$111.77** at March 31, 2026, against **$169.11** in the NASDAQ Composite and **$176.74** in the S&P 500 — **57.3 and 65.0 percentage points behind** [FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Stock Performance Graph].

**Best use of capital: debt reduction, with one qualification.** $3,864.9m repaid over five years took total debt from a $4,122.3m peak down to $2,911.4m and leverage from 8.77x to 3.64x total debt / EBITDA, with interest cover of 5.3x, all-fixed-rate maturities and the nearest wall at $600m in 2027 [CIQ Financials_Annual → Ratios and Historical Capitalization; `ciq_facts.json` `debt_maturity_wall`, `interest_coverage_x`]. The qualification is that the FY2026 $1,150.0m repayment was funded by **selling equity at $225.00**, not by operating cash — undoing a financing mistake by issuing stock, which was at least done at a good price (3.9% above today's $216.61).

**Worst use of capital: the Zynga acquisition.** $9,168m committed, 43.2% dilution of the pre-deal share base, $3,248.9m of debt taken on, and **$6,665.1m written off — 84.7% of all the goodwill the company has ever recorded** — plus the opportunity cost charged above: a label sold at a loss, studios closed, two titles' development terminated, and $516.1m of cash interest equal to 91.5% of four years' operating cash flow.

**The single biggest capital-allocation signal is the serial-acquirer pattern (RF-CAP-004, confirmed on independently rebuilt numbers).** Two material deals in four years, the larger at about 2.3x the company's own pre-deal capital base and part debt-funded, followed by write-downs of 84.7% of all goodwill ever recorded. CLAUDE.md §24 calls this close to a disqualifier, and the evidence here supports the filter rather than merely inheriting the quick-read's conclusion. Two facts pull the other way and must travel with it: the deal-making has been **dormant for roughly two and a half years** (business acquisitions $(2.6)m in FY2026, nil in H1 FY2027, no new material transaction disclosed), and FY2026 brought no goodwill impairment with the recoverability test passed. What is *not* yet evidence either way is *Grand Theft Auto VI*, launched today, carrying $2,149.7m of unreleased-title cost — a bet whose outcome is unquantified in this pool and which cannot be scored as an allocation result until it reports.

**Conclusion: value-destructive / size-driven.**

I tested the filter on independently rebuilt filing evidence rather than inheriting it, and **confirm it** (02-003, 02-004, 02-007, 02-008, 02-031). The cap is a **ceiling, not a floor**: the evidence-built score of **31** sits below it, so the cap **does not bind** and no part of this score is the product of the cap. The Governance-risk floor of 60 belongs to the synthesis (`99`), not to this agent. No partial-data cap applies — the triage recorded a 10-year capital-allocation history as present, and the five-year scorecard was built from it, so the single-period cap is **not** used.

**Scores NOT produced here (module boundary).** No fair value, no price target, no scenario probabilities, no risk/reward, no rating, no position size. Those belong to the valuation module and the master synthesizer.

## 0. The declared data gap is narrower than triage recorded — and that changes this agent's cap

Triage `00` and the handoff to this agent recorded "**No compensation disclosure**" and capped Incentive alignment at 50, because the pool's DEF 14A export is a hollow vendor file ("This filing has no tabular data to export") and FY26 10-K Items 10–14 are incorporated by reference to that absent proxy. That is accurate about the *proxy export*. It is not the whole picture, and three sources carry real, citable pay structure:

1. **`FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`** (audited) quantifies the arrangement through which the CEO and President are paid: the counterparty, the term, the annual fee, the maximum annual bonus, the consulting expense recorded, and the stock-compensation expense on units granted to that counterparty. Agent `01` already corrected the record on this point (finding 01-021).
2. **`FY26 10-K, Note 16 — Stock-Based Compensation`** (audited) gives the unit counts by award type, the grant-date values, and the *metric families* behind each award type — relative Total Shareholder Return and Recurrent Consumer Spending — with the measurement windows.
3. **The actual award agreements were filed WITH the FY26 10-K**, not incorporated by reference: `Ex. 10.8 — Form of Global Restricted Stock Performance Unit Agreement (TSR)` and `Ex. 10.9 — … (RCS)` are marked "Filed Herewith" in the exhibit index and their **Annex A vesting tables are complete in the pool** — the percentile grid, the growth grid, the payout percentages. Only the company-specific numbers are blanked (`<<Target number of awards granted>>`, `March 31, 20[__]`).

On top of that, I reached the **real DEF 14A on EDGAR** (`ttwo-20260727.htm`, filed 2026-07-27) and read its proxy-summary and governance-practice text directly, plus the readable **FY2022 DEF 14A** for the bonus-metric structure. Those are primary documents, web-retrieved, cited and dated as such.

**What is still genuinely missing:** the Summary Compensation Table itself (so the CFO's and President's base/bonus/equity split is unread), the Compensation Discussion & Analysis metric *weights for the named executive officers*, the CEO pay-ratio section, the compensation peer group, and the director-fee table. The EDGAR fetch returned only the front of the document and would not reach those sections.

**Cap position for `99`.** The Score Cap Rules trigger is "No proxy / compensation disclosure." That condition is **no longer factually satisfied**: compensation disclosure exists, is audited, and is readable, and the award agreements' vesting mathematics are in the pool verbatim. I score on the evidence and reach **53/100**. If `99` applies the original cap literally, the figure becomes **50** — a three-point difference that changes nothing in the composite. My recommendation is a **relaxed cap of 70**, sized to the residual gap (no Summary Compensation Table, no CD&A weights, no pay ratio from the primary source, no peer group), with the reasoning shown here so the decision is auditable rather than inherited.

## 1. Compensation Structure

**Reporting currency: USD. Period: fiscal year ended 2026-03-31 (FY2026), with FY2025 and FY2024 comparatives.** All 10-K figures are in millions as the financial statements present them.

The structurally unusual fact comes first: **the CEO and the President are not paid as employees.** Under the 2022 Management Agreement, effective 2022-05-23 and running through 2029-03-31, **ZMC Advisors, L.P.** supplies "financial and management consulting services" to Take-Two, and under that contract "Strauss Zelnick continues to serve as Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, and Karl Slatoff continues to serve as President" [`FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`]. Zelnick founded and runs ZMC. So the money for the top two seats leaves Take-Two as a fee to a firm the CEO owns, not as a salary to a person.

| Executive | Base | Annual Bonus | Long-Term Incentive | Cash vs Equity Mix | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| **CEO (Strauss Zelnick) — paid through the ZMC management agreement, jointly with the President** | **$3.3m/yr** fixed management fee for the term (= **$275,000 per month**) | **Maximum $13.2m/yr**, "based on the Company achieving certain performance thresholds" — thresholds NOT stated in the 10-K | Time-based, market-based (relative TSR) and performance-based (RCS) restricted stock units granted to ZMC. FY2026 **stock-compensation expense $62.9m** (FY2025 $56.2m, FY2024 $52.8m) | **Cash ≈ 21% / equity ≈ 79%** on the FY2026 expense basis: cash-route consulting expense $16.6m of the $79.5m total; equity $62.9m. Of the cash leg, only $3.3m is fixed — fixed pay is **4.2%** of the $79.5m total | `FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — Stock-Based Compensation (ZMC Non-Employee Awards)`; the $275,000/month figure from `Web: FY2026 DEF 14A (filed 2026-07-27), Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions — via 07_people-integrity-dossiers.md, retrieved 2026-11-19` |
| **CEO — as the Summary Compensation Table reports him** | — | — | — | **Total $403,019** for FY2026 (FY2025 $106,457). This is what Take-Two pays him *directly*; his economics arrive through ZMC | `Web: aggregator restatement of the FY2026 DEF 14A Summary Compensation Table (gloom.sh), retrieved 2026-11-19 — tier 10, unverified` |

Her underlying employment agreement is Ex. 10.14–10.17, incorporated by reference and not in the pool |
| **President (Karl Slatoff)** | Covered by the same ZMC agreement as the CEO — not separately disclosed in the audited note | Same | Same | Same pool of ZMC awards | `FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement` |

### 1A. Reconciling the three different numbers for the same arrangement (handoff item)

Three figures for the ZMC arrangement are in circulation across this module. They are not in conflict; they measure different things, and here is the arithmetic.

| Figure | What it actually measures | Basis | Source |
|---:|---|---|---|
| **$275,000 per month = $3.3m/yr** | The **fixed base management fee only** — one component | Contractual rate | `Web: FY2026 DEF 14A, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions`, via `07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` — and independently corroborated by the audited note's "annual management fee of $3.3" [`FY26 10-K, Note 3`] |
| **$16.6m (FY2026)** | The **cash-route consulting expense recorded in General and administrative expenses** — the base fee plus the performance bonus actually earned and any other cash components | US GAAP expense recognised | `FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement` (the identical figure agent `07` reported from the proxy — same number, both documents) |
| **$79.5m (FY2026)** | **Total accounting cost of the arrangement** = $16.6m cash-route expense **+ $62.9m stock-based compensation expense** on units granted to ZMC. Arithmetic: 16.6 + 62.9 = 79.5 | US GAAP expense recognised | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — ZMC Non-Employee Awards`; computed by agent `01` (finding 01-021) and `business-model/11` |
| **$66.818m (FY2026)** | The proxy's own **"total compensation paid to ZMC in fiscal 2026"** figure, from CD&A page 37 ("Detailed ZMC"). Almost certainly a *cash-plus-grant-date-fair-value* basis rather than an expense basis — my own target-basis reconstruction from Note 16 lands at **≈$64.8m** (cash $16.6m + time-based 74k units × $226.28 + target market-based 112k × $225.09 + target performance-based 37.5k × $168.76 = $16.6m + $16.7m + $25.2m + $6.3m), which is within 3% of the proxy's figure | Cash + grant-date fair value (inferred) | `Web: search-engine restatement of FY2026 DEF 14A, CD&A p.37 "Detailed ZMC", retrieved 2026-11-19 — unverified; I could not read p.37 directly`. **Inference, not from filings** for the basis attribution |

**Verdict on the reconciliation:** the $3.3m fee is *inside* the $16.6m, which is *inside* the $79.5m. The $66.818m is the same economics measured on a grant-value rather than an expense basis. Nothing is double-counted and nothing contradicts; the only residual uncertainty is the exact composition of the proxy's $66.818m, which I could not read at source. The gap between the Summary Compensation Table's **$403,019** for the CEO and the **$66.8m–$79.5m** his firm received is not an error either — it is what happens when an executive is supplied under a contract rather than employed, and it is the single most important thing to know about reading this company's pay tables.

**Note the trend in the cash leg.** The consulting expense ran $6.5m (FY2024) → $10.2m (FY2025) → $16.6m (FY2026): **+155% in two years**, against net revenue up 24% over the same two years ($5,349.6m → $6,656.4m) [`FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`]. The maximum cash available is $3.3m fee + $13.2m bonus = $16.5m, so FY2026's $16.6m means the performance bonus was earned at or very near its cap.
