## 2. Performance Metrics

Three award types, two real metrics. Both metric mechanics are fully disclosed, because the award forms themselves were filed with the FY26 10-K.

| Plan | Metric | Weight | Per-Share/Returns or Size-Based? | Source |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| **Annual bonus (cash)** — ZMC agreement, max $13.2m/yr | "Certain performance thresholds" — **not identified in the 10-K**. The readable FY2022 proxy names the annual-incentive metric as **Adjusted EBITDA** (FY2022 grid: threshold $473.3m / target $591.6m / maximum $887.4m; FY2022 actual $827.2m) | Effectively **100%** of the cash bonus on the FY2022 structure; the FY2026 weighting is unread | **SIZE-BASED.** Absolute profit in dollars. It rises if the company gets bigger even when the return on the capital used to get there is poor, and it is blind to share count | `FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement` (the $13.2m cap and the undisclosed thresholds); `Web: FY2022 DEF 14A, Compensation Discussion & Analysis, retrieved 2026-11-19` (the Adjusted EBITDA grid — **four years stale for the current structure**) |
| **LTIP — market-based RSUs** | **Relative Total Shareholder Return**: Take-Two's TSR percentile rank against the companies in the **NASDAQ-100 Index**, measured over **three years**, using 30-trading-day average prices at both ends. Payout grid: **below 40th percentile = 0%**, 40th = 50%, 50th = 100%, **75th or above = 200%** (capped), straight-line in between | **50.1%** of the FY2026 units granted to ZMC on a target basis; **60.1%** on a maximum basis (see the mix note below) | **PER-SHARE / RETURNS-BASED.** This is the genuinely good part of the structure: it pays on what a shareholder actually earned, relative to a wide market index, over a long window, and pays nothing at all below the 40th percentile | `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — Stock-Based Compensation (ZMC Non-Employee Awards)`; `FY26 10-K, Ex. 10.8 — Form of Global Restricted Stock Performance Unit Agreement (TSR), Annex A` |
| **LTIP — performance-based RSUs** | **Recurrent Consumer Spending (RCS)** — defined in the award form as "certain net bookings generated by the Company… virtual currency, add-on content, microtransactions, NFTs, game related subscriptions… but would not include full-game digital downloads", measured over **three years**, on **two grids, whichever pays MORE**: (a) *absolute* RCS growth — below 3% = 0%, 3% = 50%, 6% = 100%, **9%+ = 200%**; (b) *relative* RCS as a share of three-year-average total net bookings — below 45% = 0%, 45% = 50%, 50% = 100%, **55%+ = 200%** | **16.8%** of FY2026 ZMC units on a target basis; **20.1%** on a maximum basis | **SIZE-BASED.** RCS is a slice of revenue. Grid (a) pays for revenue growth; grid (b) pays for revenue *mix*. Neither contains a share count, a return on capital, or a cash-flow test. The "greater of the two" rule means the award pays on whichever revenue story looks better after the fact | `FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY26 10-K, Ex. 10.9 — Form of Global Restricted Stock Performance Unit Agreement (RCS), Annex A` |
| **LTIP — time-based RSUs** | None. Vests on dates (June 1, three successive years) if the recipient is still there | **33.1%** of FY2026 ZMC units on a target basis; **19.8%** on a maximum basis | **NEITHER** — retention, not performance | `FY26 10-K, Note 16 — ZMC Non-Employee Awards` |

**The mix, with its basis stated (§15).** Note 16's ZMC table prints FY2026 grants of 74 thousand time-based, **224** market-based and **75** performance-based units, and footnotes that the market- and performance-based figures are the **maximum** number eligible to vest, with target = 50% of maximum. So the two bases are:

- **At target:** 74 + 112 + 37.5 = **223.5k units** → time 33.1%, relative TSR 50.1%, RCS 16.8%. **66.9% of the CEO vehicle's equity is performance- or market-conditioned.**
- **At maximum:** 74 + 224 + 75 = **373k units** → time 19.8%, relative TSR 60.1%, RCS 20.1%. **80.2% conditioned.**

Both are quoted wherever the mix appears below. Never mix them.

**Two things worth naming.** First, the CEO vehicle's equity is *more* TSR-weighted than the broad employee pool's. Company-wide FY2026 grants (employees and ZMC together, at 100% of target) were 1.2m time-based, 0.6m market-based and 1.0m performance-based — so for employees the dominant performance metric is RCS, while for ZMC it is relative TSR [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`, the three non-vested-activity tables]. Second, **no metric anywhere in this structure pays on return on capital, earnings per share, free cash flow per share, or cash conversion.** Return on invested capital (ROIC — the profit earned on each dollar of capital put into the business) has been **negative for four consecutive fiscal years**: −4.3% (FY2023), −3.1% (FY2024), −4.2% (FY2025), −0.8% (FY2026) [`CIQ Financials→Ratios, annual columns Mar-31-2023 → Mar-31-2026`, vendor data]. Nobody's pay is affected by that.

## 3. Pay vs Performance

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **CEO total pay (latest)** | Two numbers, two bases, both correct: **$403,019** as the Summary Compensation Table reports Zelnick personally, and **$66.818m** (proxy basis) / **$79.5m** (audited accounting basis) paid to his firm ZMC for supplying both him and the President. $79.5m = **1.19%** of FY2026 net revenue of $6,656.4m, and **10.1%** of FY2026 EBITDA of $788m (vendor figure). ZMC's $62.9m is **20.6%** of the company's entire $305.3m pre-tax stock-compensation expense — one two-person vehicle taking a fifth of the equity cost of a 12,909-person company | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`; `CIQ Financials→Income Statement, FY2026 EBITDA` (vendor); `Web: FY2026 DEF 14A CD&A p.37 restatement, retrieved 2026-11-19 — unverified`; `FY26 10-K, Item 1 — Human Capital` (headcount) |
| **Pay vs peers (if available)** | **One peer sourced, so this is a single comparison and not a peer median.** Electronic Arts' CEO total compensation was **$30,529,835** for its FY2025 on a Summary Compensation Table basis, with an EA pay ratio of 260:1 on median employee pay of $117,302; EA revenue is a similar scale to Take-Two's. Against that: Take-Two's ZMC arrangement costs **$66.8m–$79.5m for the top two seats plus the firm's services**, i.e. roughly **$33.4m per executive** on the proxy basis — in line with the one peer — but **2.2× that single peer's CEO figure in aggregate**. The two sides are on different bases (one SCT total for one person vs a contract covering two people and a firm), so the aggregate multiple is a flag to investigate, not a measured excess | `Web: Reuters/TradingView report of the Electronic Arts FY2025 DEF 14A, retrieved 2026-11-19 — unverified`. **No compensation peer group could be read from the TTWO proxy** |
| **Pay-for-performance alignment** | **The direction of travel is wrong.** The 10-K's own five-year performance graph: $100 invested on 2021-03-31 was worth **$111.77** in Take-Two at 2026-03-31, against **$169.11** in the NASDAQ Composite, **$176.74** in the S&P 500 and **$137.38** in the RDG Technology Composite — last of all four, by 57 percentage points against the NASDAQ. Over the same stretch the company reported GAAP net losses in **four consecutive years**: −$1,124.7m (FY2023), −$3,744.2m (FY2024), −$4,478.9m (FY2025), −$298.2m (FY2026). The ZMC cost went **$59.3m → $66.4m → $79.5m** across FY2024–FY2026, **+34% in two years**, and the cash leg **+155%**. *Adjudicating the numbers that disagree (§3):* FY2026 genuinely improved — the loss narrowed from −$4,478.9m to −$298.2m, EBITDA more than doubled from $380m to $788m, and revenue rose 18%, so FY2026's pay rise is not pay for failure. The red condition is the **FY2024 and FY2025 pair**, where losses deepened in both years while ZMC's cost rose. And the metrics did bite somewhere: company-wide **0.7m performance-based (RCS) units were forfeited** in FY2026 and forfeitures reversed **$49.1m** of expense, pushing the cost-of-revenue stock-comp line to **negative $27.9m** — these are not awards that always pay | `FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Stock Performance Graph (5-year cumulative total return, March 2026)`; `CIQ Financials→Income Statement, annual Mar-31-2023 → Mar-31-2026`; `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16` |
| **Say-on-pay support (%)** | **95% of votes cast in favour at the 2025 annual meeting** — well above the 70–80% dissent line, so no board response was owed and none is missing | `Web: FY2026 DEF 14A (filed 2026-07-27), Proxy Summary / governance practices — read directly on EDGAR, retrieved 2026-11-19` |
| **Did the relative-TSR gate actually bind?** | **Cannot be measured from this pool, and the available proxy is basis-mismatched.** In FY2026, 0.7m market-based units vested company-wide with essentially zero forfeitures, and all 0.5m of ZMC's vesting units vested with **0.0 forfeited**. The 10-K's March-to-March graph implies Take-Two returned +34.8% over the three years to 2026-03 versus +24.6% for the NASDAQ Composite — which would justify vesting — **but that is the wrong index (the award uses the NASDAQ-100, the graph uses the Composite) and the wrong window (the award measures from a June 1 reference date on 30-day averages)**. Both bases are mismatched, so this is an approximation, not the measured outcome, and it is not used as evidence of outcome here | `FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY26 10-K, Ex. 10.8, Annex A`; `FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Stock Performance Graph` |
| **What the metrics reward vs what management actually delivers (handoff item)** | Agent `01` found management **six-for-six on its own Net Bookings guidance (FY2021–FY2026)**, but GAAP EPS met in only **1 of 4 years** and operating cash flow in **3 of 6**. Line that up against the pay metrics: the bonus pays on **Adjusted EBITDA**, the big equity slug pays on **relative TSR**, and the rest pays on **RCS net bookings**. **Two of the three metrics are bookings-and-EBITDA-family measures — exactly the family management hits — and nothing at all pays on GAAP earnings per share, operating cash flow, or return on capital, the measures it misses.** That is not a coincidence to be admired; it is what the metric choice does | `management-governance/01_management-and-track-record.md §3` (promise record); metrics per `FY26 10-K, Note 3`, `Ex. 10.8`, `Ex. 10.9`, and `Web: FY2022 DEF 14A CD&A` |

### 3C. Equity dilution and who pays for the pay (A6-04, and the minority-holder lens)

Shown separately because it is where compensation touches the minority holder's per-share claim directly.

- **Burn rate.** FY2026 grants, all three types at 100% of target: 1.2m + 0.6m + 1.0m = **2.8m units**, against **185,666,663 shares outstanding** at 2026-05-11 → **1.51% annual burn**. Inside the <2% green band [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY26 10-K, cover page`].
- **Overhang.** Unvested units at 2026-03-31, at 100% of target: 2.9m + 1.1m + 4.1m = **8.1m**, plus **11.2m** still available under the 2017 Plan = **19.3m = 10.4%** of shares outstanding — just over the <10% green line, hence Amber. Including the ESPP's 7.2m available shares the figure is **26.5m = 14.3%**; that basis is labelled because an employee purchase plan at 85% of market is not the same instrument as a free grant [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`].
- **No offset.** The board has authorised buybacks of up to 21.7m shares with 10.0m still available, and the company **repurchased nothing in FY2024, FY2025 or FY2026** [`FY26 10-K, Item 5 — Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities`]. So three straight years of roughly 1.5%-a-year grant dilution landed on existing holders with no buyback to absorb it.
- **Share count.** Weighted-average basic shares **170.1m (FY2024) → 175.1m (FY2025) → 183.9m (FY2026)**, +8.1% over two years. *Attribution, honestly:* management states the FY2026 jump of 8.8m shares was "**primarily due to our May 2025 underwritten public offering** of common stock, as well as normal stock compensation activity", so most of the latest year's dilution is a capital raise, not pay, and I do not charge it to compensation. The FY2025 step (+5.0m, no offering) is the cleaner compensation-driven read [`FY26 10-K, Item 7 — Net loss and Loss per share`; `FY26 10-K, Note 12 — Loss Per Share`].
- **Pricing.** No discount grants and no options: awards are restricted stock units priced at the grant-date closing price (time-based grants valued at $227.49 per share for employees and $226.28 for ZMC in FY2026), and market-based awards are Monte-Carlo valued. The only discounted instrument is the ESPP at 85%, a standard broad-based employee feature [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`].
- **Director pay.** Non-employee directors receive **restricted stock and stock grants, not options** — the plan's director forms are a "Form of Non-Employee Director Restricted Stock Agreement" (Ex. 10.10) and a "Form of Non-Employee Director Stock Grant Agreement" (Ex. 10.11), with **no director option form in existence**. The fee amounts live in the unreadable director-compensation table [`FY26 10-K, Exhibit Index, Ex. 10.10–10.11`].

---

## 4. Incentive Alignment Read

The pay rewards getting bigger and getting the share price to beat an index — not earning a return on the capital it takes to do either. The cash bonus (up to $13.2m a year) pays on **absolute Adjusted EBITDA**; the second equity metric pays on **Recurrent Consumer Spending**, a slice of revenue, on whichever of two grids pays more; and nothing in the structure touches return on capital, earnings per share, free cash flow per share or cash conversion — while ROIC has been negative for four straight years and GAAP earnings per share was missed in three of the last four. The genuinely good part is real and should be said plainly: **relative Total Shareholder Return against the NASDAQ-100 over three years, paying zero below the 40th percentile, carries the single largest weight in the CEO vehicle's equity (50.1% at target, 60.1% at maximum)** — that is a per-share test with a long window and a real floor, and it is better than most.

The single biggest incentive signal is structural, not metric: **the CEO is a contractor, not an employee.** His firm, ZMC Advisors, received $66.8m (proxy basis) or cost $79.5m (audited accounting basis) in FY2026 for supplying him and the President — 20.6% of the company's entire stock-compensation expense for two of its 12,909 people — while the Summary Compensation Table reports his pay as **$403,019**. Anyone who reads this company's pay through the standard table will understate the CEO's economics by roughly two orders of magnitude, and the $3.3m base fee is contractually fixed to 2029-03-31 regardless of anything. Set against five-year total shareholder return of **+11.8% versus +69.1% for the NASDAQ Composite** and four consecutive years of GAAP losses, with the cash leg of that fee up **155% in two years**, the magnitude is not matched by the delivery. The counterweights are genuine and are not averaged away: say-on-pay support of **95%**, a clawback policy that expressly reaches ZMC, double-trigger-only change-of-control vesting, no options and no repricing, 1.51% annual burn, and median employee pay rising **18.7%** — within a point of the executive rise, so the classic divergence flag does not fire.

**Conclusion: mixed.** One per-share metric doing most of the equity work, sitting on top of a size-based cash bonus, a revenue-based second equity metric, a magnitude at the top of the thin peer evidence available, and a delivery record the pay did not follow down.

## Incentive Alignment Score

| Component | Score | Max Score | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Returns / per-share metrics | 13 | 25 | One genuine per-share metric, carrying the largest single weight: **relative TSR vs the NASDAQ-100 over three years, zero below the 40th percentile — 50.1% of ZMC's units at target, 60.1% at maximum** [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `Ex. 10.8, Annex A`]. Against it: the cash bonus (up to $13.2m) pays on **absolute Adjusted EBITDA** [`FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `Web: FY2022 DEF 14A CD&A`], the second equity metric pays on **RCS, a revenue slice, on whichever of two grids pays more** [`Ex. 10.9, Annex A`], a third of the units at target are time-based with no metric, and **nothing anywhere pays on return on capital, EPS, or cash flow per share while ROIC ran −4.3% / −3.1% / −4.2% / −0.8% across FY2023–FY2026** [`CIQ Financials→Ratios`] |
| Metric clarity and weights | 13 | 20 | Unusually clear where it is disclosed: the actual award forms were **filed with the 10-K**, so the full vesting mathematics is readable — TSR percentile grid (40/50/75 → 0/50/100/200%), RCS absolute grid (3/6/9% → 50/100/200%) and relative grid (45/50/55% → 50/100/200%), with straight-line interpolation and 200% caps [`Ex. 10.8 / Ex. 10.9, Annex A`]; unit counts and the target-vs-maximum basis in Note 16. Deductions: the company-specific target levels are blanked in the forms, the **annual bonus thresholds are not in the 10-K at all** ("certain performance thresholds"), the CD&A weights for the named executives are unread, and the RCS "greater of absolute or relative" rule means the effective bar is the lower of two bars |
| Pay-for-performance alignment | 7 | 20 | Five-year cumulative return **$111.77 vs $169.11 (NASDAQ Composite), $176.74 (S&P 500), $137.38 (RDG Tech)** — last of four [`FY26 10-K, Item 5`]; GAAP net losses four years running (−$1,124.7m / −$3,744.2m / −$4,478.9m / −$298.2m); ZMC cost **+34.1% in two years**, cash leg **+155%** [`Note 3`; `CIQ Income Statement`]. Mitigants scored, not ignored: FY2026 genuinely improved (loss narrowed to −$298.2m, EBITDA doubled to $788m), **$49.1m of expense was reversed on forfeitures** and 0.7m RCS units forfeited company-wide [`Note 16`], and say-on-pay ran **95%** [`Web: FY2026 DEF 14A, read on EDGAR`]. But ZMC itself forfeited **0.0** units in FY2026 |
| Long-term orientation | 11 | 15 | Both performance metrics measure over **three years**; time-based units vest over three annual dates; the management agreement runs to **2029-03-31**; equity is **~79%** of the CEO vehicle's cost and fixed pay only **4.2%**; retirement eligibility requires age 55 + 10 years or age 60 + 5 years with six months' notice [`Note 3`; `Note 16`; `Ex. 10.8 / 10.9, §3`]. Deductions: 200% maximum payouts on both performance metrics, and the "greater of" RCS rule |
| Pay magnitude vs peers/performance | 4 | 10 | **$66.8m (proxy basis) / $79.5m (accounting basis)** for the top two seats = **1.19% of net revenue**, **10.1% of EBITDA**, and **20.6% of the company's entire stock-compensation expense** for two of 12,909 people [`Note 3`; `Note 16`]. Against the single sourced peer (EA CEO **$30.53m**, FY2025), ~$33.4m per executive is in band but the aggregate is 2.2× on mismatched bases [`Web: Reuters/TradingView on EA FY2025 DEF 14A`]. The reported **467:1** pay ratio would sit above the 200× line but rests on a self-contradicting tier-10 source, and the one peer runs 260:1. **No peer set — relative pay only partially assessed.** Pay rose through two consecutive years of deepening losses |
| Minority-holder alignment | 5 | 10 | For: burn **1.51%** inside the <2% line, no options, no repricing, no discount grants beyond a standard 85% ESPP, a clawback policy expressly reaching **ZMC**, **double-trigger only** change-of-control vesting, say-on-pay **95%**, and median employee pay **+18.7%** — within a point of the executive rise [`Note 16`; `Ex. 97.1`; `Web: FY2026 DEF 14A, read on EDGAR`]. Against: overhang **10.4%** above the <10% line (14.3% including the ESPP), **zero buybacks in three years** against ~1.5%-a-year grant dilution with 10.0m shares authorised, and a structure in which the Summary Compensation Table reports the CEO at **$403,019** while his firm received **$66.8m** — pay that is nearly invisible in the table a non-specialist reader would use |
| **Total** | **53** | **100** | Mixed band (41–60). **Cap note for `99`:** the Score Cap Rules trigger "No proxy / compensation disclosure" is no longer factually satisfied — audited Note 3 and Note 16 plus the filed award forms and the partially-read EDGAR proxy carry real structure. If `99` applies the original cap literally the figure becomes **50**; my recommendation is a **relaxed cap of 70**, sized to the residual gap (no Summary Compensation Table, no CD&A weights, no primary-source pay ratio, no peer group). Either way the composite outcome is unchanged |

# Ownership & Insider Behavior — TTWO

**Jurisdiction (CLAUDE.md §27).** Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated US issuer listed on NasdaqGS. The local-equivalent sources for this agent are therefore the DEF 14A beneficial-ownership table, Form 4 (Section 16) insider filings, and Schedule 13D/13G — **not** an Indian shareholding-pattern filing. India/SEBI constructs (promoter group, SAST pledge declaration, ASM/GSM surveillance, the 75% promoter cap, minimum public shareholding) have **no counterpart in this regime**; each is answered as Not Applicable with the reason and, where one exists, with the US analogue tested in its place.

**Evidence binding.** Every pool read resolved through the frozen generation `0af638492ecb0521db2676c79d75e6940c7227bb9f192567527b8a57eb43203d` (raw snapshot + `manifest.json`, `corpus.txt`, `ciq_facts.json`, `relationships.json`). The extractor was not run; live `data/TTWO/` and `analyses/TTWO_2026-11-19/_pool_extracts/` were not read. `data/TTWO/` below is a citation label only.

**Numeric reading check — UNCHECKED (carried forward from triage `00`).** This generation carries **no `numeric_reading_check` field on any source or sheet**, and `corpus.txt` carries no labelled extractor reading-warning annotation. There is therefore **no literal warning token, no source/extract reference and no LF-line/column span to preserve**, and no amount is currently marked not-proven on reading-warning grounds. But a missing check means **unchecked, not clean**. One figure in this report is explicitly quarantined on that basis: the intraday price/volume panel in the CIQ Public Company Profile (Section 4A), whose flattened two-column layout is ambiguous — it is reported as an unverified reading and is **not permitted to anchor any verdict or red flag**.

**Three data limits stated before any number is used.**
1. **The pool's DEF 14A export is hollow.** `Take-Two_Interactive_Software_Inc_-_Form_DEF_14A(Jul-27-2026).xls` contains one cell: "This filing has no tabular data to export." So the authoritative beneficial-ownership table, its pledging footnotes and the stock-ownership guidelines are **absent from the pool** [triage `00`, §3; FY26 10-K, Items 12–13 (incorporated by reference)]. Ownership below is rebuilt from Form 4 and holder-history exports, and the proxy's own figures were retrieved from the web and are labelled unverified.
2. **The pool's insider-transaction export excludes part of the record.** Its own report criteria read `Types: All Transactions (Excluding Automatic and Derivatives)` [CIQ Public Ownership → Insider Trading export, report-criteria header]. Automatic (pre-scheduled plan) transactions and derivative transactions — including option exercises — are therefore **not in it**. The holder-history file independently shows director holdings falling by amounts this export does not explain (Gordon 61,930 → 47,187 shares across Dec-31-2025 → Sep-30-2026, against only +1,474 shares of acquisitions in the transaction export; Siminoff 13,908 → 11,569 against +1,560). **Insider selling in this report is a floor, not a total.**
3. **No TTWO material-event history exists in the pool.** There is no 8-K, and the "Key Developments" export is **Alphabet Inc.'s (GOOGL)**, mis-filed [triage `00`, §5]. Agent `01`'s qualifier travels with this report: departure and event detection here is **Form-4-only**, so "no event found" means "none found in the Form 4 record", not "none occurred". This is the binding reason the single most decision-relevant timing test below cannot be closed.

**Scope boundary.** Agent `07` found a live, unresolved, un-adjudicated civil fraud / California-securities claim against Strauss Zelnick personally (LA Superior Court **24STCV20137**, filed 2024-08-09, stayed pending arbitration 2025-02-04) and a pro se Delaware Chancery derivative action (**2025-0816**), firing RF-MGT-005 at High [`07_people-integrity-dossiers.md`, Zelnick dossier]. That is `07`/`12` territory and is **not re-adjudicated here**. The only ownership-relevant question it raises is whether his TTWO shares are encumbered as security in that dispute: **no pledge, charge, margin arrangement or collateral assignment is disclosed anywhere in this pool or in the web-retrieved proxy** (Section 3). No ownership implication is proven.

Judged as a share of the company, it is 0.72%, and **none of it was bought.** The only cash conviction purchase in the entire Form 4 record is director Paul Viera's $10.0m buy in August 2018. ### 2D. Net insider activity and the timing tests

**Net insider activity: net selling, one-directional.** Thirteen open-market sales for **$85.2m** against **zero open-market purchases**. The controller side alone (Zelnick personally plus ZMC) sold **318,711 shares for $72.4m** — 85% of the total. Officers sold $11.8m; non-executive directors $1.0m. On the all-types basis the vendor reports net −167,943 shares [`ciq_facts.json` `insider_net_activity`].

**Separating the three kinds of selling, as required.** Open-market discretionary-looking sales: 376,847 sh / $85.2m (2A). Issuer withholding on vesting: 88,422 sh (2B). Option exercises and any plan-flagged ("automatic") sales: **not in this export at all** — its report criteria exclude them — so the true gross figure is higher and is recorded as Insufficient Data, not as zero.

**Whether any of these ran under a pre-set Rule 10b5-1 plan: not proven from available data.** The plan-adoption checkbox and date live on the Form 4 cover itself, which is not in this pool; the vendor export carries no plan field. The web-retrieved proxy confirms only that the company's Securities Trading Policy "includes requirements for Rule 10b5-1 trading plans" [`Web: TTWO PRE 14A, 2026-07-17, Securities Trading Policy, retrieved 2026-11-20 — unverified`]. **No intent is inferred from any sale.** Two observable facts cut the other way and are stated for balance: the CEO's three sales fall 3–5 days after a public disclosure event (2026-05-21 10-K signing; 2026-08-07 Q1 call), the classic shape of trading-window-compliant selling; and the June-1/June-2 cluster (ZMC, Goldstein, Emerson) lands on the annual vesting date disclosed in the 10-K [FY26 10-K, Note 16].

**The GTA VI test, answered explicitly — and NOT PROVEN.** *Grand Theft Auto VI* launched **today, 2026-11-19**, after slipping about 13–14 months across two disclosed revisions, and the whole FY2027 outlook rests on it. The pool fixes the revisions only to filing dates: the FY25 10-K (signed 2025-05-20) printed "**Fall of Calendar 2025, is now planned for release on May 26, 2026**" [FY25 10-K, Item 1, p.215 of extract]; the FY26 10-K (signed 2026-05-21) printed "**planned for release on November 19, 2026**" [FY26 10-K, Item 1]. **The announcement date of the second slip is not in this pool** — there is no 8-K and the Key Developments export is Alphabet's. Consequence, stated plainly:
- The CEO's **2026-03-02** sale of 60,000 shares ($12.9m) falls **inside the undated window** in which the second delay became public. Whether it preceded or followed that announcement **cannot be determined from available data**. It is recorded as an open question, not as a finding.
- The **2026-05-26** ($15.6m) and **2026-08-10** ($10.1m) sales both fall **after** 2026-05-21, by which date the November date was in the audited annual filing. Those two sales therefore came **after**, not before, the bad news.
- Between **2026-08-18 and 2026-11-19 — the 13 weeks running into the launch, and the period covering the weak Q2 FY27 print of 2026-11-09 (net bookings "to $1.67 billion… below our forecast"; recurrent consumer spending "down 9%… compared to our guidance of a 5% decline") — there was not one insider sale of any kind in the Form 4 record.** That is evidence against, not for, informed selling ahead of the miss.

**Conclusion on RF-OWN-003 / RF-MKT-001: NOT TRIGGERED, on the evidence available.** No sale is shown to precede an adverse announcement whose date the pool can fix, and the quarter immediately before the known adverse print is clean. The finding is recorded as **Insufficient Data on the one undated sale**, with the missing 8-K / material-event history named as what would close it — never as a red flag fired on a date nobody can produce.

- The **SEBI SAST graded thresholds** that this module's A3-02 band names — 25% of promoter holding as the warning line, 50% of holding or 20% of total capital as the detailed-declaration trigger, invocation as Critical [SAST Reg 28(3), Reg 31] — are **India-specific and have no US counterpart**. There is no promoter group here to measure against, and no US rule requires a standing pledge-percentage disclosure.
- The **US analogue** is the DEF 14A beneficial-ownership footnote (which must disclose shares pledged as security) plus the company's anti-pledging policy. The pool's proxy export is hollow, so that footnote is **not readable in the pool**. Retrieved from the web, the FY2026 proxy lists among its governance practices **"Strong anti-hedging, anti-pledging and insider trading policies"** [`Web: TTWO DEF 14A (ttwo-20260727.htm) / PRE 14A (ttwo-20260717.htm), 2026-07-27 / 2026-07-17, Compensation & Corporate Governance Highlights, retrieved 2026-11-20 — web-sourced, unverified`].

No pool filing shows any pledge, so **neither fires** — and equally, the favourable anti-pledging statement is web-sourced and therefore carries confidence 2, not a clean bill from a filing. The honest verdict is **Green on a zero-pledge record, with confidence capped because the document that would carry the footnote is missing from the pool.**

## 5. Ownership / Insider Read

**Skin in the game is large in dollars and small in share, and none of it was bought.** The CEO and his firm ZMC hold 1,342,568 shares — about $291m at $216.61, roughly 15× his own ownership requirement — but that is 0.72% of the company, every share of it arrived as a grant under a related-party management agreement, and the only cash conviction purchase in the whole Form 4 record is a director's $10.0m buy in August 2018. Aggregate insider ownership is 0.95% and fell 11.7% in nine months.

**The insider signal is one-directional selling into the biggest catalyst the company has ever had.** Thirteen open-market sales for $85.2m in twelve months, **zero** purchases, with the controller side taking $72.4m of it — and the pool's export excludes automatic and derivative transactions, so that is a floor. But the inference people will reach for is **not proven**: the last insider sale was 2026-08-17, there was none in the 13 weeks into today's launch or before the weak 2026-11-09 print, and the two largest CEO sales came *after* the audited 10-K had already disclosed the November date. The one sale that cannot be cleared is 60,000 shares on 2026-03-02, inside the undated window of the second delay — and the reason it cannot be cleared is that this pool contains no 8-K and the material-event export is another company's.

**The biggest risk to minority holders is not control or pledging — it is that the people running the company own almost none of it and are contracted from outside it.** One share one vote, 99.6% float, no dual class, no controlling bloc, no pledge anywhere in the record and an anti-pledging policy in the proxy; Filter 6 has no subject because there is no controlling owner. What replaces that risk is structural rather than abusive: executive leadership sits in a private firm on an agreement running to 2029 that shareholders do not vote on annually, which collected $16.6m of fees plus $62.9m of stock compensation in FY2026 and is also the largest insider holder. That channel's economics belong to `09`; what belongs here is the consequence — the controller's upside comes from grants and fees, not from shares he bought, and in the last twelve months he has been converting those grants to cash rather than adding to them.

## 1B. Board Process & Renewal (A1-08 … A1-17)

| Test | Finding | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skills matrix — per-director mapping, gaps (A1-08) | **Disclosed as a matrix with per-director mapping.** At least **12 named competency categories**, each mapped to named directors, with counts: Corporate Governance & Sustainability 10, Executive Leadership 10, Consumer & Marketing Insight 9, Entertainment & Media Expertise 9, Strategy and Growth 9, Financials & Investment Experience 7, Human Capital Management 7, Technology 7, Global Business Operations & International 6, **Risk Management 6**, Education Experience 3, Regulatory & Governmental 2. **No core competency maps to nobody** — finance/accounting (7, plus two designated audit-committee financial experts), the company's own industry (9), risk (6) and technology/cyber (7) are all covered | **Green** | `DEF 14A filed 2026-07-27, Board Skills and Qualifications matrix (pp.15–16)` — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| ID resignations, 3 years — reasons held up? (A1-09) | **Zero independent-director exits in three years.** The identical ten directors stood and were elected at the **2024, 2025 and 2026** annual meetings; both the FY2025 and FY2026 10-K signature pages carry the same ten names. The only board-level change is a **leadership rotation, not a departure** — Dornemann handed the Lead Director role to Srinivasan in **September 2023** and kept his seat. No mid-term exit, no exit citing concerns, nothing to test for reasons that do not hold up | **Green** | `Item 5.07 8-Ks: ttwo-20240918.htm, ttwo-20250918.htm, ttwo-20260917.htm` — EDGAR 2026-11-19; `FY26 10-K` and `FY25 10-K, Signatures pages` |
| Reappointments/removals — evaluation-based? against dissent? (A1-10) | **Merit-based on the disclosed process, and no resolution was pushed through against significant dissent.** Directors are elected by a **majority of votes cast** in uncontested elections, with a **resignation policy**: a director failing the standard must promptly tender a resignation to the Corporate Governance Committee, which recommends acceptance or rejection to the full board within 90 days. Across three meetings the **worst director result was 9.86% against** (Sheresky, 2024) — nowhere near the 20% line. No dissenting director was removed or dropped; no seat changed hands at all | **Green** | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Vote Required / Majority Voting and Director Resignation Policy`; three Item 5.07 8-Ks — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| Board evaluation — method + outcomes, or recycled boilerplate? (A1-11) | **Methodology disclosed AND consequences visible.** Annual board and committee self-evaluations by questionnaire, **plus biennial individual interviews of each director conducted by an outside third party**; results feed board composition and performance. The consequences are traceable, not asserted: the **Lead Director role rotated in September 2023**, a **new Technology Risk Committee was created in October 2025**, and the proxy names "active process of evaluating and rotating committee leadership positions" as a standing practice. Externally facilitated on a cycle is the UK Code norm and this meets it | **Green** | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Board Evaluation; Corporate Governance Highlights` — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| Diversity & refreshment — median tenure, additions (A1-12) | **Diversity floors met, refreshment real but slow.** 30% women, 30% ethnically diverse, 50% diverse overall; no seat filled by controller kin. **Five new independent directors in nine years (50% of the board)**, the two most recent in **May 2022 — 4.5 years ago, inside the five-year test**. But **median independent-director tenure is 9.7 years** against a Green band of <9, and **average tenure 12.6 years** with three directors at 19.7. Neither band is met: the Green band fails on median tenure, the Red band (median >12y AND no new independent voice in five years) fails on both limbs | **Amber** | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Board Composition / Diversity / Refreshment`; tenure arithmetic from §1A |
| Succession planning (A1-13) | **Process disclosed; the bench is not, and the structure makes this the board's hardest unanswered question.** The **Corporate Governance Committee** works with management to maintain a succession plan for key team members, with annual full-board discussion, and "Annual Succession Planning oversight" is a named governance highlight. What is NOT disclosed is any named internal successor — and the CEO (**69**) and the President are not employees at all: both are **supplied to the company by ZMC Advisors, L.P. under the 2022 Management Agreement, which runs only through 2029-03-31** [`FY26 10-K, Note 3`]. Succession here is therefore a **contract-renewal decision with a stated end date**, and the agreement itself (Ex. 10.26, filed with the 8-K of 2022-05-05) is not in the pool, so its renewal and termination mechanics are unreadable. The 10-K's own Power of Attorney names only Zelnick and Goldstein, with no third name behind them | **Amber** | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Corporate Governance Committee / Succession Planning` — EDGAR 2026-11-19; `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Power of Attorney, 2026-05-21` |
| Permanent / age-exempt seats — shareholder renewal within 5y; 75+ NED special resolution (A1-15) | **No permanent seats exist, and every seat is renewed annually — well inside the five-year test.** "All members of the Board of Directors stand for election on an annual basis"; the board is **not classified or staggered**; there is no non-retiring or nominee seat, and **no promoter to hold one**. India's requirement of a special resolution for a non-executive director aged 75+ has **no US equivalent**; applied by analogy to the two directors over 75 — **Dornemann (80)** and **Gordon (76)** — both were put to shareholders in September 2026 and carried **96.2%** and **99.8%** of votes cast respectively. The gap worth naming: **no retirement-age policy is disclosed**, so age-based refreshment rests entirely on the annual vote | **Green** (local-equivalent standard applied; the 75+ special-resolution limb is Not Applicable by regime) | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Corporate Governance Highlights / Election of Directors`; `Item 5.07 8-K ttwo-20260917.htm` — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| ID appointment/removal minority gate — public-majority carried? vacancies ≤3 months? (A1-16) | **The US equivalent of the minority gate is satisfied.** LODR Reg 25(2A)'s special-resolution-plus-public-majority test exists to stop a promoter outvoting the float; **TTWO has no promoter and no control block**, so every vote cast IS a public/minority vote and the two tests collapse into one. Every one of the ten directors carried a **majority of votes cast** in 2024, 2025 and 2026, with the weakest result **90.1% for** (Sheresky, 2024) and the 2026 range **93.1%–99.8% for**. A resignation policy backs the standard. **No vacancy arose at all**, so the ≤3-month refill test never engaged | **Green** (local-equivalent standard applied) | Three Item 5.07 8-Ks; `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Majority Voting` — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| IDs-only meeting held; D&O cover where mandated (A1-17) | **Executive-session prong: emphatically met.** "During fiscal 2026 the independent directors met in executive session (outside the presence of management) on **eleven occasions**" — one per board meeting, against a Green band of ≥1 a year. The Lead Independent Director convenes them and sets their agenda. **D&O prong: Insufficient Data.** Neither the FY2026 nor FY2025 proxy section read discloses whether directors' and officers' liability insurance is in force, and there is **no US mandate** (the mandatory-D&O rule is India top-1000). Delaware indemnification plus the September 2026 officer-exculpation charter amendment imply protection exists but do not evidence an insurance policy | **Green** on the session prong; **Insufficient Data** on D&O (no mandate to breach) | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Executive Sessions` — EDGAR 2026-11-19; D&O absence recorded from the same document |

## 2. Tenure & Refreshment

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Average director tenure | **12.6 years across all ten** (proxy's own: "average tenure ~12 years"); **median independent-director tenure 9.7 years**. Distribution: three at 19.7 yrs (Dornemann, Moses, Sheresky — all March 2007), one at 12.7 (Tolson), one at 9.7 (Srinivasan), one at 8.5 (Viera), one at 7.2 (Hernandez), two at 4.5 (Gordon, Siminoff). The CEO has 19.7 years on the board and 15.9 as CEO | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Board Composition` — EDGAR 2026-11-19; arithmetic in §1A |
| Overboarding / staleness signs | **Overboarding: none.** Company policy caps directors at **three outside public company boards**; the actual maximum held is **two outside seats** (Hernandez: U.S. Bancorp + Fox). Every director sits on ≤3 listed boards in total, and the one executive (Zelnick) holds a single outside seat — inside the ISS/Glass Lewis ≤3-for-executives norm. The proxy names "Annual review of Director Time Commitments" as a standing practice. **Staleness: real and specific.** Four of nine independent directors are past ten years; three are at 19.7; the **audit-committee chair is at 12.7**. Average age 67 with two directors over 75 and **no retirement-age policy**. Cross-company committee caps are an India construct with no US equivalent, and committee seats at the other listed companies were **not assessed** — a stated coverage limit | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Director Time Commitments / Outside Board Policy / Director biographies` — EDGAR 2026-11-19 |
| Recent refreshment | **Five new independent directors in nine years = 50% of the board** (Srinivasan 2017, Viera 2018, Hernandez 2019, Gordon and Siminoff both May 2022). The most recent additions are **4.5 years old** — inside the five-year test, but nothing new since. Structural refreshment did happen in the same window: the **Lead Director role rotated (Sep 2023)** and a **Technology Risk Committee was created (Oct 2025)**. One nuance that matters for quality of refreshment: **Gordon's seat arrived with the Zynga acquisition** rather than from an independent search, so of the two most recent additions only one is a clean outside appointment | `DEF 14A 2026-07-27, Board Refreshment`; `07_people-integrity-dossiers.md §1 row 15` (Zynga director 2008–2022) |

**The blunt version.** This is a long-serving, stable, un-overboarded board that refreshes slowly and has never once lost a director in the three years on record. Stability of this kind is genuinely valuable — it is the opposite of the churn pattern the tests exist to catch — but at an average of 12.6 years, with the 2007 cohort still holding three seats and the audit chair at 12.7, the board that must police a $79.5m-a-year contract with the CEO's own firm is one that has sat alongside him for most of two decades. That is the entrenchment risk in this name, and it is a tenure risk, not a compliance breach: **Nasdaq imposes no tenure cap, so nothing here is a rule violation** — it is a substantive-independence judgement.

### Matched-basis check on every ratio quoted above (CLAUDE.md §15)

| Ratio quoted | Numerator + its basis | Denominator + its basis | Matched-basis version | Basis mismatch? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1.19% of revenue** | **$79.5m — cumulative amounts RECORDED for the full fiscal year** ended 2026-03-31, built as **$16.6m consulting expense + $62.9m share-based compensation on RSUs granted to ZMC = $79.5m**. Both components run through General and administrative expenses. **Mixed in KIND, same in basis**: one is a cash services fee, the other a non-cash equity charge — stated so the reader can rebuild the total and see what it is made of | **$6,656.4m — full-year FY2026 GAAP net revenue** (consolidated statements of operations) | **1.19% — already matched.** Both sides are full-year FY2026 flows measured the same way. The cash-only version, for readers who want the fee without the equity charge, is **$16.6m ÷ $6,656.4m = 0.25%**; the contracted base fee alone is **$3.3m ÷ $6,656.4m = 0.05%** | **No** |
| **2.26% of net worth** | Same **$79.5m full-year flow** | **$3,510.9m total stockholders' equity at 2026-03-31 — a point-in-time stock** | **Mismatched in kind and labelled inline every time it appears: a full-year FLOW over a period-end STOCK.** No matched version exists, because an annual services cost has no stock-basis equivalent. The honest bound: measured against prior-year equity of $2,137.7m the same flow is 3.72%, so the "share of net worth" sits **between roughly 2.3% and 3.7%** depending on which year-end you pick — which is exactly why it is not a monitoring metric | **Yes — flow ÷ stock** |
| **PAT percentage** | Same $79.5m | FY2026 GAAP net result was a **loss** | **Not computable.** A percentage of a negative denominator inverts sign and cannot be compared year to year; it is withheld rather than printed | **Yes — denominator is negative; ratio suppressed** |

**The monitoring threshold, stated so it can be measured the same way at the next reporting date.** The testable trigger is on the **matched basis**: *total ZMC cost — consulting expense plus the share-based charge on RSUs granted to ZMC, both as recorded in General and administrative expenses for the FULL fiscal year — rising above 1.5% of full-year GAAP net revenue*, or in plain currency, **above roughly $120m in FY2027** on the company's own FY2027 revenue guidance of $7,980–8,180m. Both forms are re-measurable from the FY2027 10-K's Note 3 and Note 16 exactly as FY2026 was. Any trigger expressed against net worth is **not** adopted, because the flow-over-stock basis cannot be measured the same way twice. A second, cleaner trigger: **ZMC RSU grants exceeding 517 thousand units in a year** (the FY2025 level; FY2026 was 373 thousand, i.e. falling).

**The counterparty's own position — recorded, not just the exposure.** The self-check requires this for a related **financial** counterparty, and ZMC Advisors, L.P. is one, so it is recorded even though no treasury exposure exists:
- **The company's equity interest in the counterparty: nil.** Take-Two owns no stake in ZMC Advisors, L.P. or ZelnickMedia Corporation; the flow runs one way, from the company to the CEO's firm.
- **Separately regulated, and by whom: yes — the SEC.** ZMC Advisors, L.P. is an SEC-registered investment adviser, **CRD 161274 / SEC file 801-73697**, with **no disciplinary disclosure on Form ADV** and approximately **$2.58bn of regulatory assets under management** [`07_people-integrity-dossiers.md §2.1 (A16-06) and §2B.2`, SEC IAPD record read 2026-11-19].
- **Approved cap and current utilisation:** the contractual cap is the agreement's own ceiling — **$3.3m annual management fee plus a maximum $13.2m annual bonus = $16.5m of cash consideration a year**. FY2026 cash consulting expense of **$16.6m** sits **at — marginally above — that stated cash ceiling** (0.6% over), which on the face of Note 3 means the bonus was earned at or near its maximum and the small excess is unexplained in the note. **That is a specific, named follow-up for `09`, not a finding here**, and it is the one number in this section a reader should want reconciled. The **equity** leg ($62.9m of RSU charges) sits outside that cash cap entirely and is governed instead by the shareholder-approved 2017 Stock Incentive Plan.
- **Independent-director / audit-committee and auditor review status:** the **Audit Committee** reviews related-person transactions [`DEF 14A filed 2025-07-28`, EDGAR 2026-11-19]; the **Lead Independent Director** specifically oversees this agreement [`DEF 14A 2026-07-27` and `2025-07-28`]; the amounts sit inside the audited financial statements covered by **Ernst & Young's unqualified FY2026 opinion** and by management's conclusion that internal control over financial reporting was effective, with the Section 404(b) auditor attestation box checked [`FY26 10-K, Item 9A` and cover page]; and the **clawback policy expressly names ZMC** [`DEF 14A 2026-07-27, executive compensation best practices`]. Omitting these facts would turn a disclosed, regulated, audit-committee-reviewed services contract into an implied red flag it does not earn.

**Materiality, recurrence and growth, judged against the module thresholds.** Aggregate disclosed RPTs = **$79.5m = 1.19% of revenue**, which sits in the **Medium** band (1–5%) of the RPT materiality matrix and nowhere near the High (5–10%) or Critical (>10%) lines. It is **recurring by contract** through 2029-03-31. **It is NOT growing materially faster than revenue, and the arithmetic has to be shown because the headline direction misleads.** Total ZMC cost rose $59.3m (FY2024: $6.5m + $52.8m) → $66.4m (FY2025: $10.2m + $56.2m) → **$79.5m (FY2026: $16.6m + $62.9m)**, i.e. **+19.7% year on year**. Full-year GAAP net revenue over the same years was $5,349.6m → $5,633.6m → **$6,656.4m**, i.e. **+18.2%** [`FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`]. So the ratio is **essentially flat: 1.11% (FY2024) → 1.18% (FY2025) → 1.19% (FY2026)** — up 8 basis points in two years, not a divergence. What HAS moved sharply is the **mix inside the cash leg**: consulting expense alone went $6.5m → $10.2m → $16.6m, **+155% in two years**, consistent with the performance bonus being earned at or near its maximum in FY2026 while revenue rose 24% over the same two years. That is the thing to watch, and it is why the monitoring trigger above is set on the combined matched-basis measure rather than on either leg alone.

**Minority-protection read on the approval process — the part this agent owns.** Three things are right and two are missing.
Right: (i) the arrangement is **disclosed in the audited notes with dated amounts** and again in the proxy's related-person section, so nothing is hidden; (ii) it is reviewed by a **100%-independent Audit Committee** and overseen by a **named, designated Lead Independent Director** who sits on no management payroll; (iii) the **equity leg runs through a shareholder-approved plan** and the **cash leg is embedded in the say-on-pay vote**, which drew **95.3% support in 2026** — so shareholders do get a vote on it, twice over, and they gave it.
Missing: (iv) there is **no majority-of-minority or disinterested-shareholder vote** on the management agreement itself, and no US rule requires one; (v) the **arm's-length substantiation is an assertion, not evidence** — no benchmarking methodology, no peer set, no disclosed performance thresholds, and the governing agreement is not in the pool. A minority holder can see what is paid and who signed off; they cannot see how the price was set.

**Disqualifier cross-reference.** RPTs at **1.19% of revenue** are an order of magnitude below the **>25% hard disqualifier** owned by `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan`, which recorded "**Any disqualifier triggered: N**" and "No lock applies". Nothing in this section changes that, and this agent does not re-decide it. Two corrections travel forward: triage `00` recorded RPT quantification as "not assessable" and `business-model/01` recorded the amount as "not quantified anywhere in this pool" — **both are narrower than the evidence**, because `FY26 10-K, Note 3` quantifies it, exactly as agent `01` found. **The core question — is economic value leaking to the controller? — answers "a knowable, disclosed, audit-committee-reviewed 1.19% of revenue is flowing to the CEO's own firm — a share that has been flat for three years, not escalating — priced by a process nobody outside the board can inspect."** The leakage is small; the pricing opacity is the exposure.

So the one resolution shareholders pushed back hardest on (apart from the exculpation amendment) is the one that funds the related-party arrangement. The board's disclosed response is a **programme, not a reply**: the FY2026 proxy describes year-round engagement reaching holders of about **56.4% of outstanding stock by direct contact, 31.8% in director-led discussions**, and credits that outreach with say-on-pay support reaching 95% in 2025 — but it **does not address the equity-plan outcome anywhere**. The engagement machinery is real and demonstrably worked on pay (86.2% → 95.1% → 95.3% support); on this specific vote there is no disclosed response. Hence **RF-SHR-001 fires at Medium severity with an Amber verdict**, not Red: the 20% line was crossed once, on one resolution, in a three-meeting record where everything else cleared 86% and the item that previously drew dissent was fixed.

## 5. Minority-Shareholder Protection Read

The board is a **real, structurally capable check in form** — nine of ten directors independent, all three key committees and the new technology-risk committee fully independent, a designated Lead Independent Director who convened eleven independent-only executive sessions in one year, eleven board meetings, a skills matrix with no uncovered competency, annual elections with majority voting and a resignation policy, no poison pill, no classified board, one share one vote, no supermajority provisions, and shareholders retaining both the right to call special meetings and to act by written consent. **Rights, on paper and in the one place it can be tested — the ballot — are strong**: every resolution across three annual meetings passed, no director fell below 90.1% support, and the one pay item that drew 13.9% dissent in 2024 was engaged on and fixed to 95% support by 2025.

What stops this being "strong protection" is the single structure everything else has to police. **The CEO and President are not employees — they are supplied to the company by ZMC Advisors, L.P., a firm the CEO founded and runs, under a contract paying $79.5m in FY2026 (1.19% of revenue; cash consulting expense of $16.6m sits marginally above the agreement's own $16.5m stated cash ceiling, unexplained in the note) and running only to 2029-03-31** — and the board doing the policing has an **average tenure of 12.6 years**, with three directors seated since March 2007 and the **audit-committee chair at 12.7 years**. Pricing of that contract is asserted arm's-length with **no benchmarking, no peer set and no disclosed performance thresholds**; there is **no majority-of-minority vote** on it; its equity leg runs through the one plan shareholders pushed back hardest on (**22.40% against, 2025**, with no disclosed board response to that vote); and the CEO personally carries an **unresolved, un-adjudicated civil fraud and California-securities claim** (24STCV20137, stayed to arbitration 2025-02-04) that `07` graded Minor concerns with RF-MGT-005 at High. **RF-OWN-004 does not apply** — there is no government control, no value-maximising parent and no sprawling conglomerate; `04`'s structurally-unaligned-owner filter is not engaged by a register that is ~85% index and institutional money, so the §24 Filter 6 floor is not imposed here.

**Verdict: adequate.** Not strong — a twelve-and-a-half-year-average board cannot be called an arm's-length counterparty to the man who has chaired it for eighteen of those years, and the price of the arrangement it approves is unverifiable from outside. Not weak or entrenched either — nothing is hidden, nothing is unvoted, the defences are absent rather than stacked, and the dissent that exists is small, declining and demonstrably listened to. **The single biggest risk to minority holders is not leakage but capture: a $79.5m-a-year related-party contract that supplies the company's two most senior executives, priced by a process no outside holder can inspect, renewed or replaced by 2029-03-31 by a board whose median independent director has sat alongside that counterparty for nearly a decade.**

# Candor & Disclosure Quality — TTWO

**Evidence binding.** Every read below resolved inside the single frozen generation `.extract-generations/0af638492ecb0521db2676c79d75e6940c7227bb9f192567527b8a57eb43203d/` plus its immutable raw snapshot. The live logical path `data/TTWO/` was **not** read and is a citation label only; `analyses/TTWO_2026-11-19/_pool_extracts/` was not read; the pool extractor was not run.

**Jurisdiction & basis (carried from triage `00` and agent `01`).** United States / SEC domestic large accelerated filer (10-K / 10-Q / 8-K / DEF 14A). **US GAAP**, **USD millions**, fiscal year ends **31 March** — "FY2026" = year ended 2026-03-31, "Q2 FY27" = quarter ended 2026-09-30. Every document in the pool is in English, so CLAUDE.md §27's language rule has nothing to apply to and **nothing here is marked missing, opaque, or capped on language grounds**.

**Numeric reading check — UNCHECKED (carried forward verbatim).** This generation's `manifest.json` carries **no `numeric_reading_check` field on any source or sheet**, and `corpus.txt` carries no labelled extractor reading-warning annotation. A missing check means **unchecked, not clean** — the absence of a warning is not proof of accuracy. There is therefore no literal warning token, no source/extract reference and no canonical LF-line/column span to preserve, and **no specific amount in this report is marked not-proven on reading-warning grounds**. Every load-bearing figure below was read directly out of the frozen extract named beside it. Any restating layer must carry this statement forward.

**Coverage limits that bind this agent, stated before any score (CLAUDE.md §11; MODULE_RULES Partial-Data Rules).**
1. **Only two verbatim transcripts exist in the pool** — Q1 FY2027 (2026-08-07) and Q2 FY2027 (2026-11-09), both inside the current fiscal year. There is **no call for the quarter in which *Grand Theft Auto VI* was pushed from 2026-05-26 to 2026-11-19** (the Q4 FY2026 call, ~May-2026), which is precisely the call at which that miss would naturally have been owned out loud. My tone and own-the-miss read is therefore built on a thin base and I **cap the Disclosure Candor Score at 70** and carry confidence 3 (not 4) on the two components that depend on the calls.
2. The pool's **DEF 14A export is an empty vendor file**, so the Summary Compensation Table, the audit-fee table and the AGM voting results are unreadable from the pool. Where agent `03` used a tier-10 web restatement of the proxy, I carry that qualifier exactly and do not harden it.
3. The pool's **"Key Developments" export belongs to Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), not TTWO**, so there is **no TTWO material-event / 8-K history in the pool at all**. Every 8-K and EDGAR filing-date fact below is referenced from agent `12`'s own sweep, labelled as such, and not re-derived here.
4. **No shareholder letter of any vintage exists in the pool.** A sell-side note or a company press release is not a substitute for either a letter or a transcript, and is not used as one.

## 1. Owning the Misses

The misses are taken from `01_management-and-track-record.md` §4.1–§4.3 and are not re-derived. What is assessed here is only **how each was communicated**.

I will not infer tone from a filing I have not read | **Insufficient Data — the explaining documents are absent** | Miss figures from `01_management-and-track-record.md §4.2`; pool manifest (no FY2022–FY2024 filings, no pre-FY2027 transcripts) |
| **The IBM / Zynga matter: a $44.9m adverse jury verdict (Sept-2024), disclosed by 8-K and then dropped out of every legal note** — the handoff from agent `12`, adjudicated in §3 below | Disclosed through the correct channel at the correct time (8-K, 2024-09-13, quoting the company's own litigation position). Then: **both the FY25 and FY26 10-Ks mention "the IBM case against Zynga" exactly once each, and in neither case in the legal note** — in FY25 as a reason G&A *rose*, in FY26 as a reason it *fell*. The verdict, the $44.9m, the forum and the settlement appear in **no** periodic filing | **Obscured as to outcome, not as to existence.** See §3 | `FY25 10-K, MD&A — General and administrative` (line 2346); `FY26 10-K, MD&A — General and administrative` (line 2460); `FY26 10-K, Note 14`; 8-K accession 0001193125-24-219235 filed 2024-09-13, via `12_regulatory-legal-and-compliance.md §8` |

**The pattern across eleven rows.** Where management speaks on a call, it owns the miss, names the driver and quantifies the variance — including in the one quarter where it could have led with three beats instead. Where management writes a press-release headline or a CEO quote, the miss disappears and the adjective outruns the number. Both channels are available to the same reader on the same day, so this is a framing failure rather than a concealment; but framing is what most of the market reads, and in Q1 FY27 it crossed from flattering into contradicted.

## 2. Non-GAAP / Adjustment Aggressiveness

Cross-checked against `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md` (score **48/100**, band 41–60, "material concerns — cash conversion weak OR recurring one-offs. Here, both"). The figures below are **read from that module, not re-derived** (MODULE_RULES Materiality Thresholds).

| Signal | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Recurring "one-off" addbacks** | Four lines appear in **every** period disclosed and none is a one-off. (a) **Acquisition / business-acquisition expenses** still added back **4.5 years after the Zynga deal closed** — $2.4m in Q2 FY27, $3.8m in the half, $7.5m in the year-ago half. (b) **Business reorganisation**: $104.6m (FY2024), $106.5m (FY2025), then a **$(4.4)m credit** in FY2026 — a release, not an absence. (c) **Impairment of software development costs and licenses**: $109.9m / $77.5m / $(1.0)m / $43.6m in H1 FY27 — the same "one-off" line in **four consecutive years**. (d) **Stock-based compensation**, every single quarter without exception. The two reversal lines moved from **$184.0m of combined charges in FY2025 to a $5.4m combined credit in FY2026 — a $189.4m swing that flattered FY2026 operating income with no operating cause** | `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §4, §5, §8`, resting on `Q2 FY27 earnings release, p.2`; `FY26 10-K, p.64 and Note 7` |
| **GAAP-to-adjusted gap (magnitude / trend)** | Four non-interchangeable columns for one quarter (Q2 FY27): **GAAP net loss $(54.0)m → non-GAAP EBITDA $92.2m → management-reporting EBITDA $277.1m → management-reporting EPS ≈$0.99** against GAAP $(0.29). The step from the first to the third is **$331.1m on $1,497.0m of revenue = 22.1% of the quarter's revenue**; the EBIT step is 23.2%. Forward: the company's own FY2027 outlook implies a **management-basis EBITDA midpoint of $1,565m** containing **$462m of guided stock compensation = 29.5%**. Trend: the *disclosure* of the gap has not narrowed and has not widened — the same five lines every quarter, fully built out each time | `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §4, §7`; `TTWO 2Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-11-09, p.2 and p.11`; `TTWO 1Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-08-06, FY2027 outlook table` |
| **Does adjusted framing flatter reality?** | **Yes, in two specific ways, and no in a third.** (1) **Stock compensation is a real cost of employing people and it is excluded from the number the market tracks** — $90.0m in Q2 FY27 = **32.5% of the $277.1m management-reporting EBITDA**; $176.0m in the half; $305.3m in FY2026; **$462m guided for FY2027**. It is not theoretical dilution: the share count rose from **177.1m (2025-03-31) to 187.2m (2026-09-30)**. (2) **The deferred-revenue add-back cuts both ways and in Q2 it cut the helpful way** — **+$104.3m for the three months** but **−$43.7m for the six months**, so the single largest non-amortisation add-back in the quarter's headline EBITDA was positive only because of where the quarter fell in the billing cycle. (3) **It does not flatter through concealment.** Amortisation of acquired intangibles, D&A and interest are standard EBITDA exclusions; the company prints the full line-by-line build of **both** adjusted layers every quarter, carries the standard caveat ("not intended to be considered in isolation from, as a substitute for, or **superior to**, GAAP results"), and `earnings/04` reconciled the vendor's "EBITDA" and "EPS Normalized" fields to those builds **to the cent on two consecutive quarters** | `earnings/06_earnings-quality.md §4, §7, §9`; `TTWO 2Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-11-09, p.11 and "Non-GAAP Financial Measure"`; `FY26 10-K, p.63 and p.66`; `earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md` |
| **Guidance reconciliation — the one place this company is better than most** | The outlook tables do not just give a non-GAAP number: for the full year **and** the coming quarter they print **four adjustment columns against every GAAP line** — change in deferred net revenue, stock-based compensation, amortisation of acquired intangibles, other — so a reader can rebuild the bridge forward, not only backward. Few issuers reconcile the *forecast*. Credit it, because the aggressive substance in the rows above is only measurable **because** of this | `TTWO 1Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-08-06, "Fiscal Year Ending March 31, 2027"`; `TTWO 2Q27 Earnings Release, 2026-11-09, same table` |

**RF-DISC-002 fires.** Recurring "one-off" add-backs plus a headline adjusted measure that is roughly **30% non-cash by construction** clears the trigger on evidence, not on existence.

## 3. Disclosure Transparency

**On the financial side, disclosure is more complete than the pool first suggests; on the legal side it is pure boilerplate, and that is where the candor question actually sits.** The company discloses its KPI set identically in both annual filings in the pool, each with a **three-year rolling column** — Net Bookings, recurrent consumer spending ($5,196.6m / 78.1%, $4,474.6m / 79.4%, $4,213.5m / 78.8%), full game and other, net revenue by platform (mobile / console / PC and other), by distribution channel (digital online 97.0% / 96.4% / 95.6%), by content, and by timing of recognition — and it quantifies the one related-party channel in the **third note of the financial statements**: ZMC Advisors' consulting expense of **$16.6m / $10.2m / $6.5m** and stock compensation on units granted to ZMC of **$62.9m / $56.2m / $52.8m** (FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024), with a risk factor naming the dependency outright ("Our continued success will depend to a significant extent on our senior management team and **our relationship with ZMC Advisors, L.P.** … Our Executive Chairman/Chief Executive Officer and President are **partners of ZMC**") and every amendment listed in the exhibit index. That is disclosed, not buried.

**Three genuine transparency limits, and one disclosure that is compliant and uninformative at the same time.** (1) **No segment economics exist to disclose.** The group reports **one** operating and reportable segment, the CODM is the CEO, and the filing states he "does not review segment assets at a level other than that presented on the Consolidated Balance Sheet" — so there is **no profitability split for Rockstar, 2K or Zynga**, in a business where mobile is **50.1% of net revenue at a structurally lower gross margin** than console or PC. That is a permitted ASC 280 judgment, not a breach; it is still the single biggest thing a reader cannot see. (2) **The presentation of the CEO's pay is technically complete and practically misleading**: the Summary Compensation Table reports him at **$403,019** (FY2026) while **$79.5m** went to his own firm for supplying him and the President — a **197×** gap between the two correct numbers, with ZMC's equity leg alone taking **20.6% of the company's entire $305.3m stock-compensation expense**; the $403,019 figure itself is tier-10/unverified because the pool's DEF 14A export is empty, and I carry agent `03`'s qualifier rather than hardening it. (3) **Group scope is unresolvable from the filings**: `09` records **145 entities with no published ownership chain**, ~20 subsidiaries with no identifiable purpose, **82.2% of cash offshore**, and an **unnamed counterparty** behind a **$62.1m non-cash purchase of non-voting shares** that quintupled the unconsolidated investment balance (18.5 → 93.0) in six months — the only material movement in that module whose counterparty nobody outside the company can identify, and the one structured in the share class that keeps a stake that size below significant influence.

**Did any disclosure get LESS transparent over time? One, and it is the handoff I was asked to adjudicate.** The legal note is **identical boilerplate across four consecutive filings** (FY25 10-K Note 14, FY26 10-K Note 14, Q1 FY27 10-Q Note 12, Q2 FY27 10-Q Note 12) and **names not one case**; a grep returns **zero** occurrences of "class action", "putative", "derivative action", "tribunal" or "subpoena". Over the same window the public record holds a **$44.9m adverse IBM jury verdict against Zynga** (Sept-2024), a **five-week UK blacklisting and union-victimisation trial against Rockstar with judgment pending as of today**, and **at least one apparent federal securities class action over the GTA VI delay disclosures**. My adjudication, and I keep agent `12`'s qualifiers exactly as it set them:

- **The securities class actions and the tribunal quantum stay unconfirmed.** `12` deliberately did not fire **RF-CMP-001** because the plaintiff-firm notices are not court records and no primary docket was reachable (Stanford's clearinghouse offline, PACER and Justia returning no TTWO securities docket). I do not harden either matter into a confirmed one, and I do not score candor against them. §3's rule cuts in the company's favour here exactly as it would cut against it.
- **The IBM verdict is confirmed, and it is a candor finding — but a narrow one, so size it rather than inflate it.** $44.9m = **1.28% of FY2026 net worth** ($3,510.9m) — **Medium** materiality, below the 2% High line — so treating it as not individually material is defensible on the threshold, and the material-event duty *was* discharged, on time, in the right form. What is not defensible is the shape of what followed. The FY25 10-K tells a reader that G&A rose partly on "legal fees and contingencies related to **the IBM case against Zynga**"; the FY26 10-K tells the same reader G&A fell "primarily driven by **lower** legal fees and contingencies related to the IBM case against Zynga". So the company names the case twice, in two years, as a driver big enough to explain its own expense line — while the legal note two hundred pages later says nothing in its litigation is worth naming. **A reader of the legal note learns there is no case; a reader of MD&A learns there is one case, with no amount, no forum and no outcome.** That is a self-inconsistency inside one document, and the verdict, the $44.9m and the settlement are nowhere in any periodic filing. **Amber, and the biggest single drag on the specificity component.** No registry tag fits it: A9-10 and RF-CMP-001 belong to `12`, which tested and declined them; A7-01 (timeliness) belongs to `12`, which graded it Green; RF-DISC-001 is about commentary contradicting the numbers, and this contradicts another note, not the numbers. I therefore record it as an owned Amber candor finding without inventing a flag for it.

## 4. Tone in Bad Times

**Q2 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-09-30, reported 2026-11-09) is the worst recent period for which a verbatim transcript exists, and the tone on the call is candid — measurably so.** Net Bookings came in below the guided range, recurrent consumer spending fell **9%** against a guided **5%** decline, Net Bookings were down **18%** year on year, the half was down **11.7%** ($2,987.2m vs $3,383.6m), and the GAAP result was a **$54.0m loss** — and both the CEO and the CFO opened with the miss, named NBA 2K as the cause, and quantified the RCS variance against their own forecast, in a quarter where they could instead have led with a GAAP revenue beat, an EPS beat and an EBITDA beat. The same CEO declined to monetise the one thing he could have: asked why extraordinary pre-orders were not being put into guidance, he answered "we're days away from the launch of GTA VI, and **we tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs** … There is really no need to update numbers right now", and earlier, "we haven't sold one unit yet. **You can cancel a preorder** … we're sort of **allergic to victory laps**". That is a management declining to raise guidance on good news it cannot yet bank — the opposite of promotional.

**Q&A was answered, but thinly, and one answer is a real ding.** Thirteen questions were taken in Q1 and fourteen in Q2, none cut off, with few deflections (three instances of "in the fullness of time", two of "I'm not going to", one "not going to comment"). But: asked directly whether he still stood by a prior public statement that the company could grow revenue and earnings in the year *after* the GTA VI launch — "is that a comment you still stand by? Or have things evolved such that you don't want to stand on that comment anymore?" — the CEO **neither reaffirmed nor retracted it**: "Tempting as it is, Doug, I'm not going to give you guidance for fiscal '28 today. We have said that we expect to set a new baseline for performance going forward." An unwillingness to guide FY2028 is legitimate; an unwillingness to say whether a statement already made in public still stands is not the same thing, and this is the clearest Q&A-transparency failure in either call. Asked about the reported GTA VI budget he answered with a riddle rather than a number ("someone saying something is not more than something does not mean it's close to something, half of something, 1/4 of something or 1/10 of something"), and the CFO's two substantive variance questions — full-year gross margin guided lower, Q4 operating expenses implied up ~10% — drew directionally honest but **wholly unquantified** answers ("it's due to the mix of the business, and it's being offset by some changes in the operating expenses"; "mostly being driven by increases in R&D as well as some modest growth in selling and marketing and also investment in IT expenses") while the company's **own outlook table on page 3 of the same release carried the figures** — cost of revenue guidance raised ~$141m and operating expenses cut ~$72m versus the Q1 outlook. The specificity in this company lives in the written tables, not in the spoken answers.

---

## 5. Candor Read

**Management can be trusted to tell the truth about a number it has already printed, and not to be trusted on the adjective it puts in front of it.** The strongest evidence for them is Q2 FY2027: in its worst reported quarter it led with the one line it missed rather than the three it beat, quantified the variance against its own forecast, refused to raise guidance on pre-orders it could not yet bank, disclosed both *Grand Theft Auto VI* slips against its own superseded dates with the old date left in the sentence, owned $5.9bn of goodwill write-offs as its **own acquisition's** consequence in its own risk factor, publishes the complete line-by-line build of both adjusted layers **and of the forward outlook**, and has filed 12 of 12 10-Qs and 4 of 4 10-Ks on time with zero late-filing notifications in the issuer's entire history (`12`, A7-01 Green). The strongest evidence against them is the written channel and the legal note: a Q1 FY2027 release that called a quarter with Net Bookings **−3%**, recurrent spending **−1%** and a GAAP loss **186.6% wider** "excellent … positive trends"; a Q2 release whose headline and CEO quote omit the guidance miss the call owned two hours later; a headline earnings measure that is roughly **30% non-cash by construction** and excludes **$462m of guided FY2027 stock compensation** while the share count rose 177.1m → 187.2m; and a legal note that has named **zero cases in four consecutive filings** while the same filings' MD&A twice names "the IBM case against Zynga" as a driver of its own expense line and never once mentions the **$44.9m** verdict behind it. **The single biggest candor signal is that split: candid where a number forces it, promotional where only an adjective is required — and, in Q1 FY2027, promotional past the point its own printed numbers supported.** Verdict: **mixed.**

**Weighing the unresolved integrity signal rather than setting it aside (CLAUDE.md §24, Filter 1).** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` routed nothing — "Integrity signal: none found, hard or soft" — and `01` correctly did not emit RF-MGT-005 on that basis. But agent `07` **did** fire **RF-MGT-005 at High** on a different item: *Marks Capital, Inc. & Steven Marks v. Harry Strauss Zelnick*, civil fraud and California securities claims against the Executive Chairman/CEO **personally** (LA Superior Court 24STCV20137, stayed pending arbitration 2025-02-04; sanctions motion denied 2026-01-27), plus a pro se derivative action in Delaware Chancery (2025-0816). Nothing is adjudicated, the primary dockets were not reached, and the dispute concerns his private investment activity — I re-fire nothing and add nothing to `07`'s grade. What I do is refuse to net it out: an unresolved personal-fraud claim against the chief executive, absent from every filing, sitting beside a legal note that names no case and a release channel that oversold a declining quarter, **compounds** the trust question rather than cancelling it. It is why this read is mixed rather than "candid / high-trust", and why the follow-up below is worth more than the rest of this report put together.

**Standalone red-flag tag emission (CLAUDE.md §13; MODULE_RULES; eval check AQ).** Emitted as literal lines so the module synthesis and the eval harness can detect them mechanically, independent of the Disclosure Candor Score that already absorbs them:

RF-DISC-002 (recurring "one-off" / aggressive non-GAAP add-backs)

RF-DISC-001 (commentary contradicting the numbers)

**Tested and NOT fired, recorded explicitly so a reader can see the test ran rather than was skipped:** **RF-REG-002 (delayed results / material-disclosure timeliness)** — agent `12` owns A7-01 and tested it across 12 quarters of primary EDGAR filing dates (12/12 on-time 10-Qs, 4/4 on-time 10-Ks, zero NT filings in the issuer's history, proxy filed 2026-07-27 against a stated 2026-07-29 deadline, no exchange nudge) and graded it **Green**; my own read of the pool adds nothing contradicting it, so **RF-REG-002 is not triggered by either specialist** and the tag is deliberately not emitted. **RF-CMP-001 (undisclosed material litigation)** belongs to `12`, which tested and declined it on the stated ground that no primary docket was reachable; I keep that qualifier and do not re-adjudicate it.

**The single highest-value next data request:** one paid primary-docket pull — the federal securities class actions over the GTA VI delay disclosures, and the Glasgow Employment Tribunal register for *IWGB v. Rockstar Games UK*. If a securities class action is on file, its total absence from a 10-Q filed **2026-11-09** moves the legal-note finding from Amber to Red, fires RF-CMP-001 in `12`, and caps Disclosure candor at 50 under the Score Cap Rules. One pull settles it.
