## Hard Self-Check (MODULE_RULES canonical — applied before returning)

- **Every material claim appears in the Universal Findings Table.** Yes — 24 rows; §1–§5 introduce no claim absent from the table.
- **Every non-NA finding has evidence; every citation has source, period, and page/section.** Yes — printed page numbers, named notes/items, named transcript speakers and dates; no PDF byte offsets. Line numbers are given only where they point into the frozen extract text and are labelled as such.
- **Every Amber or Red finding has a follow-up question.** Yes — 06-001, 002, 007, 008, 011, 012, 013, 014, 015, 017, 018, 019, 020, 021, 023, 024 all carry one.
- **Every Red finding has a red-flag decision and an ID where applicable.** 06-007 → RF-DISC-001 (fired). 06-013 and 06-014 → RF-DISC-002 (fired). 06-012 → Red with the explicit decision that no registry ID fits a note-vs-note inconsistency and that RF-CMP-001 belongs to `12`, which tested and declined it.
- **Every score is traceable to specific rows.** Yes — each Disclosure Candor component cites its finding IDs.
- **No vague verdicts without raw values.** Every verdict carries a number and a unit.
- **No US-only filing assumptions for a non-US company.** Not applicable — TTWO is a US domestic filer; the US form names are the correct local equivalents, as triage `00` established.
- **Missing data marked "Insufficient Data," not guessed.** 06-010 (no FY2026 transcript), 06-024 (two transcripts, no letters, no 8-K history), and the FY2022–FY2024 miss-communication rows in §1 are all marked Insufficient Data rather than inferred.
- **Narrative introduces no uncited claim.** Checked line by line.
- **Banned phrases.** None used in my own voice. "Disciplined execution" and "excellent" appear only inside quotation marks as the evidence for RF-DISC-001, paired in the same sentence with the contradicting figures; "accretive M&A" appears only inside the quoted CEO statement.
- **Upstream qualifiers preserved (CLAUDE.md §3).** `12`'s non-firing of RF-CMP-001 on the ground that no primary docket was reachable, `07`'s RF-MGT-005 at High, `03`'s tier-10 unverified label on $403,019 and $66.818m, and the unchecked numeric-reading status are each carried forward in the exact form the originating agent set them, and none is hardened.

# People & Network Integrity Dossiers — TTWO

**Reachability declaration (read this first).** Triage `00` recorded that *its* web/registry/trademark/address lookups were unreachable (sandbox `deniedHosts: ["*"]`) and told `07` and `12` to declare their own posture rather than inherit it. **This agent's posture is different and better.** Direct socket access is still denied (`curl` to sec.gov, efts.sec.gov, take2games.com and icis.corp.delaware.gov all returned `000` on 2026-11-19), but the managed search/fetch capability IS available, and a genuine external sweep ran through it. Reached: SEC EDGAR (company submissions API, Archives, litigation releases), the SEC Investment Adviser Public Disclosure register (IAPD), USPTO registration records (via registry mirrors), the OpenSanctions consolidated screen (OFAC SDN/CONS, EU, UN, UK, SAM exclusions, PEP), the company's own website, court-record aggregators, and dated media. **Not** reached: state corporate registries (Delaware Division of Corporations, New York DOS), primary court docket systems (PACER, LA Superior Court, Delaware Chancery File&ServeXpress), the OFAC search tool directly, professional-licence registers (state bar / AICPA), and any registered-address-cluster source. Every dossier below therefore says **coverage-limited** with the axes that did not run, and the Score Cap Rules are applied, not argued with.

**Numeric reading unchecked (travels forward).** This frozen generation carries **no `numeric_reading_check`** on any source or sheet, and `corpus.txt` carries no labelled extractor reading-warning annotation. A missing legacy check means **unchecked, not clean**. There is no literal warning token, source reference, or LF-line/column span to preserve, and no specific amount in this report is marked not-proven on reading-warning grounds. Any figure quoted here that becomes load-bearing should be eyeballed against its frozen extract before it anchors a verdict.

**Promoter-specific reads (kept inside the controller's dossier).**
- **A9-04 — track record elsewhere.** His other ventures show no defaults, no enforcement and no minority-squeeze history. ZMC runs **$2,575,358,490 of regulatory assets** as an SEC-registered adviser with a clean Form ADV; Starwood Property Trust is a live listed REIT where he has served as an independent director since 2009; the one failure in the set (Blockbuster) was a non-executive seat at a secularly destroyed business. **Green, with the coverage caveat that ZMC's individual portfolio companies were not swept one by one (Scope-Boundary #5).**
- **A13-01 — professional CEO vs promoter-run.** Unusual hybrid and worth naming precisely: he is not a founder-promoter (he owns no control block; the company is institutionally held with no promoter group) yet he is not a plain salaried CEO either, because he is supplied to the company *as a service* under a management agreement with a firm he owns. There is a real professional layer beneath him — President (Slatoff, 2008–), CFO (Goldstein, 2007–), Chief Legal Officer, General Counsel Americas. **Green on professional depth; the structural oddity is priced at A5-02 by `09`, not here.**
- **A13-02 — view on the CEO (operating record).** A long, continuous operating history across Fox, BMG, Crystal Dynamics and 19 years here; crises navigated (the 2007–08 post-backdating rebuild, the EA takeover defence, the Zynga integration). No trail of abandoned ventures dressed as pivots. **Green.**
- **A13-03 — vintage & involvement.** 19 years, executive, full-time Executive Chairman & CEO. Attention is genuinely split with ZMC, which he also runs as CEO and Managing Partner — a disclosed, paid, structural split rather than a hidden one. **Amber**, on the split, not on absence.
- **A13-06 — family dynamics / succession disputes.** **None.** No family member is on the board, the payroll or the register; there is no controlling family and therefore no succession dispute to have. **Green.**
- **A13-07 — promoter's other material businesses.** ZMC is a private media-focused PE firm that **transacts with the listco** — and it is disclosed, quantified ($275k/month base; $16.6m FY26 consulting expense) and overseen by the Lead Independent Director. No evidence it competes with Take-Two. **Amber and routed to A5/A11 (`09`)** — the correct destination is RPT pricing, not an integrity flag.
- **A13-08 — sensitive government dealings.** **None.** No government contracts, licences or discretionary allocations drive revenue; the business sells games to consumers through platform holders. The 2023 Senate letter and FTC commentary are political attention, not dependence. **Green.**
- **A13-09 — political connect.** Modest personal donations, no office, no party role, no donation-to-outcome coincidence evidenced. **Green.**

**Two sentences.** The man who founded this company was criminally convicted on his own guilty plea and permanently barred by the SEC from ever serving as an officer or director again, over backdating that ran from 1997 to 2003 — and none of it is disclosed anywhere in this evidence pool. The one thing the synthesis must know is the direction of that fact: it is the **base rate this board was built to correct**, it attaches to nobody currently in post, and it is the strongest available argument for reading the current roster's clean sweep as a real result rather than a formality.

## 3B. Lineage & Phoenix Read (A17-02, A17-03)

**Does a predecessor of the LEGAL ENTITY exist? No — and that answer is swept, not silent.** Three independent checks agree: the company was incorporated in Delaware in **1993** and claims **1993** as its founding year (they reconcile exactly, so D-2 raises no lead); EDGAR's `formerNames` array for CIK 0000946581 is **empty** (D-3); and the company's own website, fetched 2026-11-19, carries **no history page** (`/about` → HTTP 404) and no "formerly / erstwhile / part of" language anywhere on its home page (D-1). A17-02 is **Green**, and **RF-NET-001 does not fire**.

**Is the FRANCHISE lineage older than the group's ownership of it? Yes — and it is disclosed.** *Grand Theft Auto* originated at **DMA Design** and entered the group through the **BMG Interactive** acquisition dated **1998-03-12**; DMA Design Holdings Limited is named as a current subsidiary in the FY26 10-K's own subsidiary list. That is disclosed lineage, in the filings, not hidden lineage — the distinction A17-02 turns on.

**The phoenix test, answered limb by limb, on the one entity where the first limb is actually satisfied — THQ Inc.:**
1. **Did the predecessor fail?** Yes. THQ Inc. went through **Chapter 11** and its assets were sold in the bankruptcy.
2. **Did assets, brands, staff, address, products or customers continue into the current entity?** Partially and narrowly — Take-Two acquired the **"Evolve" asset line** on **2013-01-23**. No continuation of THQ's address, corporate identity, customers or wider business into Take-Two is evidenced.
3. **On what disclosed legal basis and for what consideration?** A **formal, court-supervised bankruptcy asset sale from an arm's-length third party**, dated and recorded in the group-structure record. **No Take-Two controller, director or officer sat on the seller's side**, so there is no related-party re-purchase and no round-trip. The per-transaction consideration is not in this evidence pool — named as a gap, and routed to `12`'s and `09`'s reading of the FY2013-era disclosures rather than guessed.

**Is a predecessor still live and still trading on the same brands?** No. There are **no two live entities trading the same brand** anywhere in this network: the core mark **GRAND THEFT AUTO (Reg. 4321159)** is registered to **Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc.** itself, and no unrelated live proprietor of it was found, so the D-4 corroboration test is not even reached. **A17-03 is Green and RF-NET-002 does not fire.** The 1998 BMG Interactive deal likewise fails the phoenix test on limb 1 — BMG was a solvent corporate seller divesting a unit, not a failed entity.

## 6. Provenance & Next Data Request

- **Provenance.** Of 54 register subjects, **46 were filing- or vendor-supplied, 8 were independently discovered by this sweep, and 0 were user-supplied** — and separately, **18 were invisible inside the frozen evidence pool** (the 8 above plus 10 the company discloses only in the proxy the pool was missing) — and after the A17-08 four-class test, **0 are `disclosable-and-omitted`**. That independently discovered set is where the value sits: the company's **own founder and two former officers, all three carrying permanent SEC officer-and-director bars**; four of the CEO's past board seats; the live civil claim against him personally; and — pulling the other way — the **actual, disclosed economics of the ZMC management agreement**, which the evidence pool could not show.
- **Nominee or independent directorships excluded from beneficial-interest scope:** none excluded. There is no promoter group, no nominee structure and no dual-class share, so nothing was carved out. For the avoidance of doubt, all nine independent directors — **Srinivasan, Dornemann, Moses, Sheresky, Tolson, Viera, Hernandez, Gordon, Siminoff** — were swept at Tier C in their own right, and their names are recorded here so a reader can check that none was quietly dropped.
- **Aggregator conflicts kept in scope and unresolved (A17-10).** Four, all named rather than resolved in the subject's favour:
  1. **The pool's vendor graph tags ZelnickMedia Corporation and ZMC Advisors, L.P. `affiliation: third_party`** while the same pool's board background says the CEO founds and manages both. The conflict is resolved **against** the vendor label — they are controller-linked, not arm's-length — and the shorter/benign reading is explicitly rejected.
  2. **"Butterfingers Limited (Out of Business)"**, listed by the vendor as a strategic alliance of 2K Games and Gearbox Software with industry "Restaurants". Kept in scope and flagged as a **probable vendor name-match error**; no registry was reachable to resolve it, and **nothing adverse is attributed to Take-Two on this row**.
  3. **The aggregator paraphrase of Chancery 2025-0816** — "principal owner of Belzberg & Co.", deliberately bounced employee paychecks, "a federal investigation into drug trafficking and money laundering at affiliated entities". Kept in scope, named, and **not attributed**: no primary or reputable secondary source corroborates any of it, and the one outlet that covered the related LA case expressly warned other media had over-stated it.
  4. **Two namesake collisions, both resolved on the primary source and not attributed**: the "SEC falsely accused me of fraud" item adjacent to **Lainie Goldstein** is **Gregory Law of Osiris Therapeutics** (*SEC v. Jacoby*, 17-cv-03230-CCB); the SAM debarment adjacent to **Daniel P. Emerson** is **"Daniel Emerson Norton"**, a different surname. Also noted: *SEC v. Hernandez* (M.D. Fla. 6:22-cv-02367) is not **Roland A. Hernandez**.
- **Single highest-value next data request:** **the complaint, first amended complaint and full docket in *Marks Capital, Inc. & Steven Marks v. Harry Strauss Zelnick*, LA Superior Court 24STCV20137 — plus the pro se complaint in *Marks v. Zelnick*, Delaware Chancery 2025-0816.** One paid docket pull. It is the only document set that can move the Executive Chairman & CEO's grade in either direction: it would show what is actually pleaded, whether the arbitration-stayed claim is a commercial dispute between investors or something that touches his conduct as a fiduciary, and whether the sensational collateral allegations circulating in aggregator summaries appear in the pleadings at all. Everything else outstanding (state registries, the address cluster, licence registers, the six overflow entities) is cheaper but cannot change a grade.

## 7. People & Network Integrity Read

The distribution is **15 of 16 current directors and officers Clean** (seven of them on a stated reduced-depth scope), **one — the Executive Chairman & CEO — Minor concerns on his own record**, and **three Disqualifying grades that belong entirely to the past**: the founder and two former officers, all three permanently barred by the SEC and gone since 2007. The riskiest live subject is **Strauss Zelnick**, and the reason is narrow and specific: an unresolved, un-adjudicated civil fraud and California-securities claim against him personally (LA Superior Court 24STCV20137, stayed into private arbitration on 2025-02-04, where no public outcome will ever appear) plus a pro se Delaware derivative action naming him and his firm — set against a completely clean criminal, securities-regulator, sanctions and disqualification record, and a management agreement with his own $2.6bn private-equity firm that the company **does** disclose with amounts ($275k a month; $16.6m of FY2026 consulting expense), contrary to the impression the empty proxy export in this evidence pool created. The discovery loop reached **hop 2** and stopped on **`breadth_budget`** with six named Tier-A-linked entities, the address-cluster recipe, every state registry and every primary court docket left on the table — so this is a **coverage-limited** read, and the §24 Filter 1 signal is **open**, which is why **RF-MGT-005** fires and conviction is capped rather than the finding being dressed up as either exoneration or indictment.

A rational minority holder should conclude this: the people now running Take-Two swept clean on every axis that could be reached, and that clean sweep is more meaningful here than at most companies, because this is a company that **did** suffer a real, adjudicated fraud — its founder pleaded guilty and is permanently barred, as are its then general counsel and its then accounting officer — and the board, the CFO and the audit-committee chair now in place all arrived **after** that conduct, with 19 years of unqualified E&Y opinions and effective internal controls since. The open item is not a pattern and not a regulator; it is one unresolved private lawsuit against the chief executive, in his personal investment capacity, whose pleadings nobody in this run could read. That justifies monitoring and a conviction cap — not a walk-away, and not a clean bill of health either.

# Related-Party & Group Forensics — TTWO

**Company:** Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NasdaqGS:TTWO) · **Date:** 2026-11-19
**Reporting standard US GAAP · currency USD, millions unless stated · fiscal year ends 31 March** (so "FY2026" = year ended 2026-03-31; "Q2 FY27" = quarter ended 2026-09-30). All pool documents are in English, so CLAUDE.md §27's language provisions have nothing to apply to here — and nothing below is recorded as a gap on language grounds.

**Evidence binding.** Every pool read resolved through the frozen generation `0af6384…3203d`; the extractor was not run; live `data/TTWO/` and `analyses/TTWO_2026-11-19/_pool_extracts/` were not read. `data/TTWO/` is a citation label only.

**Numeric reading — UNCHECKED, carried forward verbatim from `00_governance-data-triage.md` §5.** This generation's `manifest.json` carries **no `numeric_reading_check` field on any source or sheet**, and `corpus.txt` carries no labelled extractor reading-warning annotation. A missing check means **unchecked, not clean**. There is therefore no literal warning token, source reference or LF-line/column span to preserve, and **no amount below is marked not-proven on reading-warning grounds**. The duty that transfers: every load-bearing figure in this report was read directly from the frozen filing extract that reports it (`10K_2025_26_0001628280-26-037434.txt`, `10K_2024_25_0001628280-25-026694.txt`, `10Q_2Q_0001628280-26-072254.txt`); Capital IQ workbook tabs and `relationships.json` are used only as a tier-5 vendor read to reconcile against, never as the authority for a filing's own number (§5).

## 0. Two corrections to the inherited premise, made before anything else

**Correction 1 — the triage's "no related-party note" premise is wrong, and its caps do not bind.** `00_governance-data-triage.md` §5 set an **RPT & leakage risk floor of 40** and a **Confidence max of 80** on the stated premise that the pool contains no related-party note and that RPT quantification is "not assessable". Both layer-1 agents found that premise too pessimistic, and this agent confirms it directly from the frozen extract:

- **FY26 10-K Note 3 — MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT is a related-party note, in the audited financial statements, with amounts.** It names the counterparty (ZMC Advisors, L.P.), the two executives on the other side (Strauss Zelnick, Executive Chairman & CEO; Karl Slatoff, President), the term (effective 2022-05-23, running through 2029-03-31), the annual management fee ($3.3), the maximum annual bonus ($13.2), the consulting expense recognised ($16.6 / $10.2 / $6.5 for FY2026 / FY2025 / FY2024) and the stock-based compensation on restricted stock units granted to ZMC ($62.9 / $56.2 / $52.8) [`FY26 10-K, Note 3 — Management Agreement`]. The triage looked for a note titled "related party" (ASC 850's usual heading); the disclosure is there under its own heading, quantified, three years deep.
- **The real DEF 14A exists on EDGAR and was read this run** (it is absent from the pool, where the vendor export is an empty 4×4 stub). It discloses the arrangement by name in "Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions", confirms the $275,000-per-month base management fee, and states the written policy and the approval route [`FY2026 DEF 14A (EDGAR, filed 2026-07-27), Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions` — partial render, see Sweep Log].

So **A5 IS quantifiable**. The Score Cap row "No related-party note / RPT disclosure (A5 not quantifiable) → RPT & leakage risk floor 40; Confidence Score max 80" has **a false premise and is not applied**. Agent `07`'s conclusion is adopted: **the pool's apparent related-party non-disclosure is an evidence-pool gap, not a company gap.** The residual disclosure finding that does survive is narrower and is graded in §5 (A5-08) and §11: the *pool* could not show the amounts, which is a defect of this evidence set, not of Take-Two's filings.

**Correction 2 — `relationships.json` tags the two controller vehicles `third_party`, and that tag is wrong as a matter of substance.** The vendor graph lists **ZelnickMedia Corporation** (`affiliation: "third_party"`, sourced to the 2025 Form 10-K, Suppliers row) and **ZMC Advisors. L.P.** (`affiliation: "third_party"`, sourced to the 2026 Form 10-K, Suppliers row) as operating vendors, each with `link_strength` capped at 25 for the stated reason "the export names no listing for it" and each carrying an explicit `evidence_gap` that the size of the relationship is undisclosed [`relationships.json` (CIQ Suppliers/Customers export, tier 5), retrieved 2026-11-19]. **`third_party` here is a parsing artefact of how the export classifies counterparties — it has only `group` / `likely_group` / `third_party` to choose from and no field for "controlled by the registrant's own CEO". It is not a finding of arm's-length dealing.** The CEO founded and manages both entities [`CIQ Board Members export, Background field`; `FY26 10-K, Note 3`]. **Both are treated throughout this report as related parties.** The same caution applies in the other direction to the graph's `likely_group` tags on **Epic Games, Inc.**, **Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.** and **Prima Interactive (Pty) Ltd** — none is in Take-Two's group; Ex. 21.1 names none of them, and Epic is named as a *competitor* in the same filing [`FY26 10-K, Ex. 21.1`; `FY26 10-K, Item 1 — Competition`]. The vendor's own `link_strength_cap_reason` says so ("may be part of the anchor's own group"), i.e. it is a guess, not a determination.

**Correction 3 — the Management Agreement itself is obtainable, and was obtained.** The triage recorded Ex. 10.26 (Management Agreement dated 2022-05-03) as absent from the pool with "the fee, the term, and the performance conditions all unreadable". The governing instrument's full text was not rendered this run, but the filing's own Item 1.01 description of it was, and it carries the material terms verbatim — fee, bonus target and range, the three equity tranches with their metrics, the severance multiple, and who approved it [`8-K dated 2022-05-03 (filed 2022-05-05), Item 1.01`, read 2026-11-19]. Those terms are used below and cited to that source. What remains **"Not proven from available data"** is the clause-level detail of the executed agreement (full termination mechanics, change-of-control triggers, bonus performance thresholds by metric, and any indemnity) — the exhibit text itself was not rendered. That residual is priced in Confidence, not in the leakage score.

**What agent `07` found in history, used only as base-rate context and not re-adjudicated.** `07` established, by its own network sweep and outside the pool, that the company's **founder and former CEO/Chairman Ryan Ashley Brant**, the **then General Counsel (Kenneth Selterman)** and the **then Controller/Chief Accounting Officer (Patti Tay)** were each permanently barred by the SEC, all links terminated in **2007**; it tested **RF-NET-003 and recorded explicitly that it does not fire**, and classified all three `not-disclosable` because Regulation S-K Item 401(f) reaches only current directors and officers within a ten-year window [`07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` §2.4–2.6, §3, §4]. That is not re-opened here. Its only use in this report: the 2007 episode arose from backdated option grants and the then-management's own self-dealing, so this group has a historical reason to over-document controller pay — and the 2022 Management Agreement's approval trail (unanimous Compensation Committee **and** unanimous independent-director approval, a Lead Independent Director with named oversight of the agreement, a written $120,000 policy) is consistent with that. The present management is a different set of people; nothing adverse is attributed to them from 2007.

## 1. RPT Intensity & the Applicable Regime (A5-01)

**Applicable materiality rule, per period — named, because the wrong regime is a bad-extraction error (§20).** Take-Two is a **US / SEC domestic large accelerated filer** listed on NasdaqGS [`FY26 10-K, cover page`; triage §5A]. India's SEBI LODR Reg 23 regime — neither the Dec-2025 graded slabs (10% of turnover up to ₹20,000cr, tapering to a ₹5,000cr cap) nor the earlier lower-of-10%-of-turnover-or-₹1,000cr line — **has no application to this issuer in any period read, and is not used.** The rules that do govern, and they are the same in each of FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026:

| Rule | What it requires | Line |
|---|---|---|
| **Regulation S-K Item 404(a)** | Proxy disclosure of any transaction in which a related person has a direct or indirect material interest | **$120,000** per transaction / series |
| **ASC 850** | Related-party disclosure in the audited financial statements where material | No numeric floor — materiality judgment |
| **Nasdaq Listing Rule 5630** | Review and approval of related-party transactions by the audit committee or a comparable independent body | Review requirement, not a threshold |
| **Shareholder approval of an RPT** | **No US rule requires a majority-of-minority vote on a related-party transaction.** There is no Reg 23(1A)/23(4) analogue | **n/a — regime** |

That last row matters for how the bands below are read: the A5-01 and A5-02 Red limbs that turn on "without majority-of-minority approval" **cannot trip in this jurisdiction**, because no such vote exists to withhold. Per the Regime & structure nuance rule, the item is judged on conduct within the regime that applies — which here means the audit-committee / independent-director gate, and the advisory say-on-pay vote as the nearest shareholder check.

**The ledger is small and complete: there is exactly one related-party relationship with a dollar amount anywhere in three years of filings — the ZMC management agreement.** Both legs are summed below, because an aggregate must travel with its build (§15).

| FY | Aggregate RPTs ex-dividends (cash + equity legs) | % of revenue | % of PAT | % of total expenses | % of total assets | Material-RPT line that year | Above the line? | Minority-approved? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2024 | **59.3** = cash 6.5 + ZMC RSU SBC 52.8 | **1.11%** | **n/m — GAAP net loss $(3,744.2)** | **0.66%** (÷ 8,940.2) | not computed — FY2024 total assets not read in this pool | Item 404(a) **$0.12** disclosure floor; **no approval slab exists** | Yes — above the $0.12 *disclosure* floor, and disclosed | **n/a — no US majority-of-minority vote exists.** Approved by the independent directors | **Amber** | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `earnings/01` (revenue); `FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations` |
| FY2025 | **66.4** = cash 10.2 + SBC 56.2 | **1.18%** | **n/m — net loss $(4,478.9)** | **0.66%** (÷ 10,024.7) | **0.72%** (÷ 9,180.7) | same | Yes (disclosure floor), disclosed | same | **Amber** | same |
| FY2026 | **79.5** = cash 16.6 + SBC 62.9 | **1.19%** | **n/m — net loss $(298.2)** | **1.18%** (÷ 6,760.6) | **0.85%** (÷ 9,383.2) | same | Yes (disclosure floor), disclosed | same | **Amber** | same |
| **3-yr cumulative** | **205.2** | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | arithmetic on the three rows above |

*Denominators, each cited where it came from:* revenue 5,349.6 / 5,633.6 / 6,656.4 and the GAAP net losses $(3,744.2) / $(4,478.9) / $(298.2) are the filing's own [`FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`], and match `earnings/01_historical-financials.md` §1 exactly — they are not recomputed here. Total expenses are built, not quoted: FY2026 **6,760.6** = cost of revenue 2,846.7 + total operating expenses 3,913.9 [`business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` §1 row 3, same basis]; FY2025 **10,024.7** and FY2024 **8,940.2** are derived as revenue − EBIT using `earnings/01`'s EBIT of $(4,391.1) and $(3,590.6), so both include that year's large goodwill impairment and are **labelled derived, not filed**. Total assets 9,383.2 and 9,180.7 are the filing's [`FY26 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets`].

**Why "% of PAT" is recorded not-meaningful rather than computed.** Take-Two posted a GAAP net loss in each of the three years, so a ratio to PAT inverts its sign and its sense. For a reader who wants the magnitude anyway: $79.5 is **26.7%** of the absolute FY2026 net loss of $298.2 — a number that says more about the loss than about the leakage, which is exactly why it is not the headline. The useful comparators are the four below, all matched-basis (same fiscal year, same P&L, before tax):

| Matched-basis ratio (both sides FY2026, P&L charge before income tax) | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 | Build |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| ZMC total charge ÷ **General and administrative expense** (where all of it is booked) | **8.28%** | **7.52%** | **9.09%** | 59.3÷716.1 · 66.4÷883.3 · 79.5÷874.4 [`FY26 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Operations`; Note 3] |
| ZMC equity leg ÷ **total stock-based compensation expense before income taxes** | **15.73%** | **17.35%** | **20.60%** | 52.8÷335.6 · 56.2÷324.0 · 62.9÷305.3 [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`] |
| ZMC equity leg ÷ **G&A stock-based compensation** | **47.35%** | **45.62%** | **42.21%** | 52.8÷111.5 · 56.2÷123.2 · 62.9÷149.0 [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`] |
| ZMC **cash** leg ÷ total expenses (the proxy's own framing) | 0.07% | 0.10% | **0.25%** | 6.5 / 10.2 / 16.6 over the expense bases above |

**Verdict: Amber, not Green, and not Red — and the reasons are specific.**
- **Not Red.** The quantum is **1.19% of revenue**, inside A5-01's Green band (<1–5%) and inside the Materiality Thresholds' **Medium** band (1–5% of revenue/assets), nowhere near the 5–15%+ High/Critical line. It is quantified in an audited note, the counterparty is named, and the US regime's approval gate was used (§5). **RF-RPT-001 is tested and does not fire** (not above the High threshold). **RF-RPT-002 is tested and does not fire**: the registry trigger is "Promoter-linked RPT **above threshold**", and at 1.19% of revenue this is below the 5% High threshold. I state that reading explicitly because the Materiality Thresholds table's RPT row lists "promoter-linked" among its Critical qualifiers; read literally and alone, that would make every disclosed controller-pay arrangement Critical on existence, which the module's own ban on flagging Red for existence alone, and the Regime & structure nuance rule, both forbid. The quantum governs; the controller linkage sets the floor at Amber and drives the follow-ups.
- **Not Green.** A5-01's Green band requires "all at documented arm's length". This arrangement is **100% controller-linked, recurring, and rising** — every dollar of the three-year $205.2 ledger went to a vehicle founded and managed by the two most senior executives, the charge grew **+34.1%** over two years against **+24.4%** revenue growth, and its share of G&A rose to **9.09%** in a year when total G&A **fell 1.0%** ($883.3 → $874.4) [`FY26 10-K, MD&A — General and administrative`]. There is no peer benchmarking of the structure (§5, A5-05). "Recurring" and "promoter-linked" are two of the Red band's own qualitative disjuncts; what keeps the item off Red is the quantum plus the documented approval, not the absence of those features.

**The >25% hard lock: reported, not re-adjudicated.** At **1.19% of revenue** and **1.18% of total expenses**, the ratio is an order of magnitude below the 25% line. `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan.md` §1 row 3 recorded disqualifier 3 as **N**, with the bars computed at **$1,664.1** of related-party sales (25% of revenue) and **$1,690.2** of related-party purchases/expenses (25% of total expenses). **This agent defers to `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` (hard lock) and does not re-decide it.** One refinement is handed back, because that agent recorded the amount as "not quantified anywhere in this pool": it **is** quantified, at Note 3, and the correct figure to set against the $1,690.2 expense bar is **$79.5** — i.e. **4.7% of the bar**. The conclusion is unchanged; the evidence behind it is now numeric rather than absent.

| Component | FY2026 amount | What it is | Cash or non-cash | Where it is disclosed |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Annual management fee | **3.3** | $275,000 per month × 12 = $3.30m, contractually guaranteed not to decrease over the term | **Cash** | `FY26 10-K, Note 3` ($3.3 annual fee); `8-K 2022-05-03, Item 1.01` ("$275,000 per month in each year during the term"); `FY2026 DEF 14A` |
| Annual bonus earned | **≈13.3** (residual) | Target $6.6; range $0 at 80% of target to a **maximum $13.2** at ≥150% of target, on performance thresholds | **Cash** | `8-K 2022-05-03, Item 1.01`; `FY26 10-K, Note 3` (maximum 13.2) |
| **= Consulting expense recognised in G&A** | **16.6** | The **cash leg** — the line the proxy describes and the figure agent `07` reports as ~0.25% of FY2026 total expenses (this agent computes 16.6 ÷ 6,760.6 = **0.25%** ✔) | Cash | **`FY26 10-K, Note 3`** — the audited figure |
| Stock-based compensation on RSUs granted to ZMC | **62.9** | The **equity leg** — non-cash expense on time-, market- and performance-based restricted stock units granted to ZMC, also booked in G&A | **Non-cash, dilutive** | **`FY26 10-K, Note 3` and `Note 16`** |
| **= Total FY2026 P&L charge for the ZMC relationship** | **79.5** | What agent `01` and `business-model/11` report. **16.6 + 62.9 = 79.5 ✔** | Mixed basis — stated | Build is this agent's; both components are the filing's own |

**So the two figures do not conflict: $16.6 is the cash consulting expense and $79.5 is the total expense including the $62.9 non-cash equity leg.** Neither is wrong; each must carry its label. Two residuals are named rather than rounded away (§15): **(a)** the bonus component is a **residual of $13.3** (16.6 − 3.3), which sits **$0.1 above the disclosed $13.2 maximum** — the gap is not explained in the filing and is most likely rounding at one decimal across two disclosed figures, or reimbursable expenses inside the consulting line; it is **not** evidence of a bonus above the cap, and the honest statement is that the bonus was **at or within rounding of its maximum** in FY2026; **(b)** no component of the $79.5 is capitalised — the ZMC charge is expensed in G&A in full, unlike the $98.0 of company-wide stock compensation capitalised into software development costs [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`].

**What the equity leg costs minority holders, stated on its own basis.** Unvested ZMC units at 2026-03-31 were **1.3 million**, i.e. **0.70%** of the 185,666,663 shares outstanding net of treasury at 2026-05-11 [`FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY26 10-K, cover page`]. Valued at the FY2026 time-based **grant-date** price of $226.28, that is **≈$294** of unvested value — an **engine computation on a grant-date-price basis, not a filed figure and not a market value at any date**; the units' realisable value depends on three-year relative TSR and recurrent-consumer-spending outcomes that are not yet determined.

### 3A. Royalty / brand / technology fees (A5-02)

| Payee | What is provided | Amount | % of turnover | Basis disclosed? | Trend vs margins | Prior minority approval? | Verdict | Source |

| **No controller-linked payee** | — | **nil** | **0.00%** | n/a | n/a | n/a — no US vote exists | **Green** | Direct read of `FY26 10-K` Notes 1–21 and `FY25 10-K`: no royalty, brand, trademark, technology or licence fee to any related party appears in any note or caption |
| *(For completeness — the inbound licences that DO exist, all third-party)* | Minimum marketing support "primarily reflect our agreements with **major sports leagues and players' associations**" (i.e. the NBA licence); software development and licensing commitments include "obligations to **holders of intellectual property rights** for use of their trademarks, copyrights, technology" | **740.1** total minimum contractual commitments at 2026-03-31 (software development and licensing 175.8 + marketing 206.9 + purchase obligations 357.4) | 11.1% of FY2026 revenue | Yes — laddered by fiscal year, FY27 **323.7** | Arm's-length; counterparties are unrelated (NBA, leagues, IP holders) | n/a | **Green — not a related-party channel** | `FY26 10-K, Note 14`; quantified by `10_contingent-liabilities-and-commitments` / `balance-sheet-survival/05` (A7a) — **not counted here** |

**Brand ownership — priced, as required, even though the flag does not fire.** Agent `07` established that the group's core mark **GRAND THEFT AUTO (US Reg. 4321159) is registered to Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. itself**, found no unrelated live proprietor, and recorded **A17-04 Green with RF-NET-004 explicitly not firing** [`07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` §3B, §4]. Consistent with that, Ex. 21.1 shows the IP- and music-rights holders sitting **inside** the consolidated group — `Rockstar Games Songs/Sounds/Tunes LLC`, `2K Games Songs/Sounds/Tunes LLC`, `Take-Two Games Songs/Sounds/Tunes LLC`, `Rockstar Records, LLC`, `RDIP Limited` [`FY26 10-K, Ex. 21.1`]. **So the pricing answer is: there is no controller-side licence, and therefore no rate to disclose and no fee to benchmark — the brands the company trades under are owned by the company or a consolidated subsidiary, and nothing flows out of the group for their use.** RF-NET-004 does not propagate: none of its enumerated adverse conditions is present (no controller-linked owner, no undisclosed terms on a licence that does not exist, no mark in use without a licence, no dispute, no corroborated same-mark use by an unrelated proprietor). The RPT & leakage-risk floors of 55 / 50 / 45 attached to RF-NET-004 therefore **do not apply**.

Below every High/Critical threshold; quantified, named, independently approved. The channel is the executives' own pay, not a trading relationship | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `relationships.json` Suppliers row (tier 5, `third_party` tag corrected per §0) |

The revenue side is platform holders, retailers and distributors — all unrelated |

**The structural read on this row, stated plainly.** The margin-skimming pattern A5-04 exists to catch needs a controller entity standing between the listco and its market — buying its output cheap or selling it inputs dear. **That pattern is absent here.** Every dollar of Take-Two's $6,656.4 of FY2026 revenue was earned from unrelated counterparties, and the only controller-side purchase is the two most senior executives' own remuneration, routed through their firm rather than paid as salary. The conflict is real and is graded at A5-10 and A11-04; it is not a trading-margin conflict.

## 4. Round-Tripping Cross-Year Name Match (A5-04)

**The list was BUILT, not eyeballed.** One list of every named counterparty across every year the pool covers, from four sources: `relationships.json`'s 22 counterparty objects with their `orientation` field (customers vs suppliers) and their `source_ref` year; the FY26 10-K's and FY25 10-K's named platform partners and >10% customers; the FY26 10-K's related-party Note 3; and the CIQ Strategic Alliances and Direct Investments exports. Customer names were then matched against vendor names **across years**, not within one year. 22 counterparty names were matched; the matches that returned are below.

| Name | Years as customer | Years as vendor | Both roles? | Sales ≈ purchases (circular)? | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Microsoft Corporation** | FY2025, FY2026 (`orientation: customers`, roles **distributor + licensor**); named as a >10% customer in FY2024–FY2026 | FY2026 — platform-fee and publisher-agreement counterparty; the Xbox publisher agreement is filed as an exhibit | **YES** | **No.** Two legs of a published platform relationship: Take-Two sells games through the storefront (revenue) and pays a platform fee on those same sales (cost of revenue). No matched or mirrored amounts; no funds-flow circle | **Amber — resolved and closed.** A genuine two-way trade; the industry's standard structure | `FY26 10-K, Item 1 — Business`; `FY26 10-K, Note 1 — Concentration`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Exhibit — Xbox publisher agreement`; `relationships.json` |
| **Apple Inc.** | FY2026 (`customers`, distributor); named >10% customer FY2024–FY2026 | FY2026 — platform fees in cost of revenue; "Apple and Google generally have the **discretion to set** the amounts of their platform fees and change them" | **YES** | **No** — same reasoning | **Amber — resolved and closed** | `FY26 10-K, Item 1A / MD&A — platform fees`; `FY26 10-K, Note 1`; `relationships.json` |
| **Google LLC** | FY2026 (`customers`, distributor); named >10% customer | FY2026 — platform fees in cost of revenue, rate set at Google's discretion | **YES** | **No** — same reasoning | **Amber — resolved and closed** | same |
| **Sony Group Corporation / Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.** | FY2015 and FY2026 source refs (`customers`; SIE carries roles **distributor + licensor**); Sony named >10% customer | FY2026 — platform/licensor leg | **YES** | **No** — same reasoning. Note SIE's `likely_group` tag is a vendor artefact (§0): SIE is not in Ex. 21.1 | **Amber — resolved and closed** | `FY26 10-K, Item 1`; `relationships.json` |
| **Nintendo Co., Ltd.** | FY2026 (`customers`, customer role) | Not in the suppliers orientation | No | n/a | **Green** | `relationships.json` |
| **Valve Corporation · Meta Platforms · Snap Inc. · Epic Games · Thunderful Group AB · Alliance Entertainment · Prima Interactive** | FY2024–FY2026 (`customers`) | Not in the suppliers orientation | No | n/a | **Green** | `relationships.json` |
| **National Basketball Association, Inc. · Remedy Entertainment Oyj · Gaming Realms plc · ironSource Ltd. · Bidstack Group Plc · Punktid Technologies AS · Technicolor Creative Studios** | Not in the customers orientation | FY2022–FY2026 (`suppliers`: licensors and suppliers) | No | n/a | **Green** | `relationships.json` |
| **ZMC Advisors, L.P.** | **Never — zero years as a customer** | **FY2026** (`suppliers`, vendor); FY2024–FY2026 per Note 3 | **NO — vendor only** | **No — the question cannot even arise.** No related party appears anywhere on the revenue side, so there is no second leg for a circle to close through | **Green on the round-trip test** (the relationship itself is graded Amber at A5-01/A5-04/A5-10) | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `relationships.json` |
| **ZelnickMedia Corporation** | **Never** | FY2025 (`suppliers`, vendor) — historic | **NO — vendor only** | **No** | **Green on the round-trip test** | same |

**Result.** Four both-roles matches returned, all four with the same four names — **Microsoft, Apple, Google and Sony** — and all four are **Amber-resolved, not Red.** Per step 7, a both-roles match escalates to Red only on circularity **evidence**, and none of the four tests is met: (i) **no matched or mirrored amounts or timing** — the revenue leg is gross net revenue recognised on sell-through and the cost leg is a percentage platform fee expensed as incurred, disclosed on different bases in different captions [`FY26 10-K, Note 1 — Revenue Recognition`, MD&A]; (ii) **no off-market pricing favouring an insider** — the platform fee is set **unilaterally by the platform holder**, which the company discloses as a risk running *against* it, the precise opposite of an insider-favourable price; (iii) **no funds-flow circle** — nothing leaves as a purchase and returns as a sale, because the two legs are economically the same transaction seen from both sides of one storefront; (iv) **no unexplained material match** — the explanation is in the filing itself. None of the four is a related party, and none is controller-linked. **The lead is closed as Amber-resolved; no red flag fires, and the DHFL/Gensol pattern is absent.** One thing the match *does* say, and it belongs to another module: the same four names are simultaneously the company's largest customers (80.6% of FY2026 revenue in the top five, one at 24.9%) and the setters of its largest cost — a bargaining-power concentration, not a leakage channel, and already owned by `business-model`'s customer-concentration and external-dependency reads.

## 5. Approval & Disclosure Hygiene (A5-05, A5-06, A5-07, A5-08)

| ID | Test | Raw finding | Band | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A5-05** | Arm's-length substantiation | **No bare "arm's length" assertion is relied on anywhere — and none is made.** What IS documented: the fee is **contractual and specified** ($275,000 per month, guaranteed not to decrease over the term); the bonus has a **stated target ($6.6), a stated range ($0 at 80% of target to a maximum $13.2 at ≥150% of target) and stated performance thresholds**; the equity has **named metrics and curves** (time-based cliff vesting over two to three years; market-based on three-year Total Shareholder Return against the NASDAQ-100 constituents, target at the 50th percentile and maximum at the 75th; performance-based 25% on recurrent consumer spending and 75% on relative stock price, maximum 200% of target); and **approval is documented by name**: "the compensation committee of the Board of Directors of the Company… and the independent members of the Board have each unanimously approved". **What is NOT disclosed: any benchmarking of this structure against a peer set.** The arrangement has no obvious peer comparator — an externally contracted CEO-and-President through a private-equity vehicle is not a standard S&P 500 structure — and the company publishes no comparator analysis for it | Green limb (methodology + approval documented) **met on approval and on metrics**; **not met on benchmarking** | **Amber** | `8-K 2022-05-03 (filed 2022-05-05), Item 1.01`; `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY26 10-K, Note 16`; `FY2026 DEF 14A, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions` |
| **A5-06** | Minority dissent on RPT resolutions | **No RPT resolution exists to dissent against — the US regime has no majority-of-minority RPT vote** (§1). Judged on the nearest shareholder checks at the **2026 annual meeting, held 2026-09-17**, where the ZMC economics sit inside the compensation that was voted on: **advisory say-on-pay — For 137,394,611 / Against 6,717,451 / Abstain 196,603 / Broker non-votes 14,929,224 → 4.66% against** of for-plus-against (4.65% including abstentions). **Re-election of Strauss Zelnick — 4,588,247 against → 3.19%.** **Re-election of LaVerne Srinivasan**, the Lead Independent Director who holds named oversight of the ZMC agreement — **377,967 against → 0.26%**. Highest director dissent anywhere on the ballot: **Roland Hernandez 9,977,712 against → 6.93%**. **No resolution was defeated and none was restructured.** (Separately, and not an RPT item: the Certificate-of-Amendment proposal drew 23,574,236 against → **16.37%** — routed to `05`, which owns A10-03) | **<10% against = Green**; >20%, or a defeated resolution restructured to dodge the vote, would be Red | **Green** | `8-K dated 2026-09-17, Item 5.07 (EDGAR, read 2026-11-19)`; `FY2026 DEF 14A` (Srinivasan's oversight role) |
| **A5-07** | Pre-approval, only-ID voting, omnibus discipline, slab-slicing | **A written policy exists with a stated threshold and a named approver.** "Take-Two has adopted a written policy and procedures regarding related person transactions whereby the **Audit Committee** is generally responsible for reviewing and approving transactions involving amounts **in excess of $120,000** between the company or any of its subsidiaries and any related person." For FY2026 the proxy states the company "was not a participant in any financial transaction, arrangement or relationship in which a related person had or will have a direct or indirect material interest, in an amount exceeding $120,000, **except for the transactions described with ZMC, which the independent directors of the Board of Directors had previously reviewed, approved and ratified** in accordance with its policy on transactions with related persons." Two independent approval facts, from two documents: the **independent directors** reviewed and approved the ZMC transactions (not management, not the full board including the interested parties), and the underlying 2022 agreement was **unanimously approved by the Compensation Committee and by the independent members of the Board**. **Oversight is also personalised**: the Lead Independent Director's role explicitly includes "the oversight of our management agreement with ZMC". **No omnibus approval, no blanket pre-clearance and no post-facto-only ratification is disclosed** — the word "previously… approved" places approval before the year, with ratification alongside it, not instead of it | Green band: 100% pre-approved with only independent members voting; omnibus ≤1 year reviewed quarterly. Red band: post-facto ratifications, omnibus as a blank cheque, non-independent directors voting, or transactions split below thresholds | **Green** | `FY2026 DEF 14A, Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions` and `Review, Approval or Ratification of Transactions with Related Persons` (EDGAR, read 2026-11-19 — see Sweep Log for the render limit); `8-K 2022-05-03, Item 1.01`; corroborated for the prior year by the same language in the `FY2024 DEF 14A` |
| **A5-08** | Counterparty transparency | **Every related-party counterparty is named, with the relationship stated, in both the audited note and the proxy** — ZMC Advisors, L.P. by name, with both executives' partner status named, and ZelnickMedia Corporation named as predecessor by assignment. **Zero instances** of "entities where key management personnel exercise influence", "an affiliate of a director", or any aggregated unnamed related-party caption in four filings. **One unnamed counterparty exists in the group's disclosures and is not disclosed as related:** "During the six months ended September 30, 2026, we acquired **non-voting equity shares in a privately-held entity with an initial value of $62.1 in a non-cash transaction**" — no name, no description of the consideration given, no stated business purpose. It is **2.53%** of 2026-09-30 total equity of 3,673.6 (Medium materiality). Nothing in the filings suggests the counterparty is related, and the proxy's own $120,000 negative covers FY2026 — but the half-year to 2026-09-30 falls in FY2027, which no proxy yet covers | Green band: every counterparty named with the relationship stated. Red band: **material** transactions with unnamed KMP-influenced entities | **Amber** — Green on every disclosed related party; Amber on the one unnamed, unexplained $62.1 counterparty, which is not stated to be related and is not asserted here to be | `FY26 10-K, Note 3`; `FY2026 DEF 14A`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Note 4 — Fair Value Measurements, Nonrecurring`; equity denominator `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets` via `balance-sheet-survival/05` §4 |

**Slab-slicing result — the sums that were actually checked.** The test is whether same-counterparty transactions were split to stay under an approval threshold, so the **totals**, not the slices, were compared against the applicable slab. The applicable slab is Item 404(a)'s / the company's own policy threshold of **$120,000 per transaction or series**; there is **no higher approval slab in the US regime** and no shareholder-vote slab at all.

| Counterparty | FY2024 total | FY2025 total | FY2026 total | Policy slab | Total ÷ slab | Split into sub-threshold slices? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| **ZMC Advisors, L.P.** (all legs summed: management fee + bonus + RSU stock compensation) | **59.3** | **66.4** | **79.5** | **0.12** | **494× · 553× · 663×** | **No.** The arrangement is disclosed as **one** agreement with two expense legs, both named and both quantified in the same note. The cash leg **alone** ($16.6) clears the slab by **138×** — there is nothing to gain by slicing, and no sliced presentation exists |
| **ZelnickMedia Corporation** | nil | nil | nil | 0.12 | n/a | n/a |
| Every other counterparty in the pool | — | — | — | 0.12 | — | **No related-party slice found.** The proxy affirmatively states that **no** related-person transaction other than ZMC exceeded $120,000 in FY2026 — the only way slicing could hide here is if a series were disaggregated below $120,000 each, and the policy's own wording reaches a "series", not just a single transaction |

**Conclusion on A5-07: no slab-slicing.** The single related-party arrangement sits three orders of magnitude above the only threshold that applies, is presented as one agreement, and was approved by the independent directors before the year it covers.

**What the aborted-deal sweep actually covered, and where it stops.** Swept: both 10-Ks' acquisition, divestiture and subsequent-event disclosures; the FY26 10-K exhibit index in full (which lists every 8-K-filed agreement by date, including each ZelnickMedia and ZMC instrument from 2017 to 2025); the 2022-05-05 8-K's Item 1.01; the 2026-09-17 8-K's Item 5.07 ballot (a withdrawn-and-restructured related-party proposal would normally leave a trace there, and none appears); the CIQ Direct Investments merged-entity trail back to 1998; and a targeted web sweep for controller-linked or withdrawn Take-Two transactions. **The limit, stated rather than papered over: the pool contains no 8-K feed at all and no TTWO material-event history** — the Key Developments export in this pool resolves to **Alphabet Inc.**, a different issuer, and was not read as TTWO evidence [`00_governance-data-triage.md` §5]. A board-approved-then-withdrawn related-party proposal announced in an 8-K and never repeated in a 10-K could therefore escape this pool. The web sweep partly compensates and returned nothing (Sweep Log). **So: no related-party M&A found, including no aborted attempt, on a sweep whose 8-K leg is reconstructed from the exhibit index and the web rather than from a material-event feed.** **RF-CAP-004 does not propagate from this row** — the serial-acquirer cap that `business-model/11` set (acquisition-pattern score 75, §24 Filter 4) is owned by agent `02` and binds Capital allocation, not RPT leakage; deals are **not** the leakage channel here, because every seller was a third party.

- **The label tier (`Rockstar Games, Inc.`, `2K Games, Inc.`, `2K, Inc.`, `Zynga Inc.`, `The Gearbox Entertainment Company, Inc.`).** The publishing labels — the operating economics.
- **The studio tier (~24 named development entities across 21 countries).** Where games are made and where staff are employed; local incorporation is a labour and tax requirement, not a structuring choice.

- **The unexplained tier (~20 names above).** **No disclosed purpose.** This is the honest residual, and it is the reason A11-01 is Amber rather than Green.

## 9. Cash & Funding Topology (A11-02, A11-03)

**Matched-basis rule (CLAUDE.md §15) applied line by line.** The company's offshore-cash disclosure covers **cash and cash equivalents only** — not short-term investments — so both sides of every share below are **period-end cash and cash equivalents at the same date**. The broad-basis variant (cash + short-term investments) is shown **labelled**, with the mismatch named, and is **not** used as the headline, because the numerator's scope does not extend to it.

| Question | Raw value | Basis (both sides) | Matched ratio | Verdict | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where does consolidated cash sit (parent vs subs)? | Cash and cash equivalents **held outside the U.S. by foreign subsidiaries 1,359.7** of total cash and cash equivalents **1,545.5** at **2026-03-31**; **945.0** of **1,149.4** at **2026-09-30** | **Matched** — both numerator and denominator are period-end *cash and cash equivalents* at the same date, from the same two documents | **88.0%** offshore at 2026-03-31 (1,359.7 ÷ 1,545.5); **82.2%** at 2026-09-30 (945.0 ÷ 1,149.4) | **Amber** — the great majority of the group's cash sits in foreign subsidiaries, and the company does not disclose it as restricted | `FY26 10-K, MD&A — Liquidity`; `FY26 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, MD&A — Financial Condition`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets` |
| *Same question on a broad basis — shown only to prove the read is not basis-shopping* | Offshore cash 945.0 against cash + short-term investments **1,673.6** (1,149.4 + 524.2) at 2026-09-30 | **MISMATCHED and labelled as such** — the numerator's disclosure scope is cash and equivalents only; the denominator adds short-term investments whose geography is not disclosed | *56.5% — not a share of anything the company discloses; do not use* | **Not used** | same |
| Share held with a related **finance company or treasury vehicle** | **nil — 0.0%.** No related finance company, treasury vehicle, affiliated bank or related-party deposit exists anywhere in the group. Counterparties named for the group's cash and investments are **money market funds (512.3) and bank time deposits (229.7)** at 2026-09-30, plus short-term investments of 524.2 | Matched — all period-end 2026-09-30 | **0.0%** | **Green** | `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Note 4 — Fair Value Measurements`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Note 5 — Short-term Investments` |
| Parent borrowing while subs hold the cash? | **Yes, factually.** **All 2,500.0 of senior notes are obligations of the parent**, Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., as is the 1,000.0 revolver (997.9 available at 2026-09-30 after 2.1 of letters of credit); the only subsidiary-level borrowing is **29.4** of Zynga convertible notes, **1.2% of face borrowings**, which the parent guarantees. Against that, **82.2%** of cash sat offshore at 2026-09-30 | Matched where compared — debt at face from the debt note, cash at period-end, both 2026-09-30 | Parent-level debt **2,500.0** vs domestic cash **204.4** (1,149.4 − 945.0) at 2026-09-30 → domestic cash covers **8.2%** of parent senior-note principal. *Both sides period-end 2026-09-30; the domestic figure is a **derived residual** of two disclosed numbers, labelled* | **Amber** — this is the A11-02 pattern in form. What it is **not**: cash concentrated in **opaque** subsidiaries. The balances are "dispersed across various locations around the world", every holder is a consolidated Ex. 21.1 entity, **no dividend blocker or regulatory restriction is disclosed**, the company states it "expect[s] to have the ability to generate sufficient cash domestically to support ongoing operations", and the group generated **624.3** of operating cash flow in FY2026. The real cost is a **tax** cost, not a trapping: repatriation tax on undistributed foreign earnings is unprovided and **"it is not practicable to estimate"** it | `FY26 10-K, Note 11 (Debt)`; `Q2 FY27 10-Q, Note 10 (Debt)`; `FY26 10-K, Note 15 (Income Taxes)`; `balance-sheet-survival/01_capital-structure-and-leverage.md` §1, §3 (debt stack and offshore-cash flag — used, not re-derived); `balance-sheet-survival/05` §3 |
| **ICDs to group entities — amount, rate, tenor** | **No inter-corporate deposit or intra-group loan is disclosed in any filing read, and none to a related party exists.** Intra-group balances eliminate on consolidation and the notes disclose no related-party lending; `relationships.json` records **0 intragroup relationship rows (0.0% intragroup row share)** across its 28 disclosed rows | n/a | **nil** | **Green** | Direct read of `FY26 10-K` Notes 1–21 and `FY25 10-K`; `relationships.json` `concentration.intragroup_rows: 0` (tier-5 corroboration only) |
| **Evergreen / rolled-over ICDs?** | **None — nothing to roll** | n/a | **nil** | **Green** | same |

**No related financial counterparty exists, so the facts that row would require are recorded as nil rather than omitted.** The checklist requires that where a related **financial** entity holds group cash, the report state the company's own equity interest in it, its regulatory supervision, the approved cap and its utilisation, and the independent-director / auditor review status. **There is no such counterparty here**: Take-Two holds **no** equity interest in any bank, finance company or treasury vehicle, holds its cash in money market funds and bank time deposits with unrelated institutions, and discloses no approved related-party exposure cap because there is no related-party exposure to cap. The one adjacent fact, recorded for completeness: ZMC Advisors, L.P. **is** a financial entity — an SEC-registered investment adviser, CRD 161274, SEC file 801-73697, supervised by the SEC and verifiable on IAPD [`07_people-integrity-dossiers.md` §2B.2] — but **it is a service vendor, not a holder of any group cash or investments**, and the company holds no interest in it. Its own supervision status is recorded here because the counterparty's regulator is a fact that determines how the exposure reads; the exposure itself is a consulting expense, priced at §1–§2.

**Monitoring threshold, stated so it is measurable the same way at the next reporting date (§15/§17).** The testable share is **offshore cash and cash equivalents ÷ total cash and cash equivalents, both at period end, from the MD&A liquidity paragraph and the balance sheet of the same filing.** It read **88.0% at 2026-03-31** and **82.2% at 2026-09-30**. The comparable for the next print (Q3 FY27, quarter ending 2026-12-31) is the year-ago **Q3 FY26** figure on the same two lines — **which this pool does not contain**, so the honest trigger is stated against the two readings that do exist: a rise back **above 88.0%** on that exact basis, **combined** with either a drawn revolver or a new parent-level borrowing, would say the group is funding the parent with debt while cash accumulates where it cannot be used without a tax charge. Note what this trigger would have done on the last two reported periods: it would **not** have fired at either (88.0% is the bar, 82.2% the latest reading) — it is capable of failing, and it is currently failing, which is the correct state for a monitoring line rather than a finding.

| **A11-05** | Restructuring churn / associates held below consolidation thresholds | **Churn: two material years, then a reversal.** Business reorganization expense was **104.6 (FY2024)**, **106.5 (FY2025)** and **(4.4) (FY2026)** — a credit, i.e. a release, as the programme closed; the company attributes the FY2026 swing to the absence of the prior year's charges. In the same window it **acquired Gearbox (June 2024)**, **sold the Private Division label (October 2024)**, cancelled titles, and ran "several rounds of layoffs". **Associates below the threshold: the facts, stated without insinuation.** All unconsolidated equity investments are disclosed as "**less than a 20% ownership interest in each**" with "no significant influence over or control", measured at cost less impairment under the Topic 321 practical expedient — i.e. every one of them sits **below the equity-method line**, which is where the 20% figure comes from. **The coverage statistic, kept separate from the finding, because confusing the two manufactures a red flag.** `07` reported that **18 of 54 subjects were not visible anywhere in the frozen evidence pool** — the 8 it independently discovered plus 10 the company discloses only in the proxy this pool was missing. That is a statement about **this evidence set**, not about Take-Two's candor. On the specific question this agent owns: **the company disclosed its one related-party arrangement twice — in an audited note and in the proxy — with the counterparty named, the executives' interest named, three years of amounts, the contractual fee, the bonus range, the equity metrics, and the approval route.** Penalising it because the pool was missing the proxy would be the error the four-class test exists to prevent.

## 14. Read

**About $79.5m a year leaves Take-Two for the controller's own firm, and that is the entire related-party ledger.** The single largest channel is the ZMC Advisors management agreement — $16.6m of cash consulting expense plus $62.9m of non-cash stock compensation on units granted to ZMC, **$79.5m in FY2026, $205.2m cumulatively over three years, 1.19% of revenue and 9.09% of total G&A**, with the equity leg alone taking **20.6% of every dollar of stock compensation the company booked**. It is not a trading relationship and not a margin skim: it is how the Executive Chairman/CEO and the President are paid, routed through a private-equity firm they founded and run rather than onto the payroll, with a severance multiple of **3× (fee + target bonus) = $29.7m** and 1.3m unvested units (0.70% of shares) still to settle. Because every GAAP year since FY2024 was a net loss, the charge cannot be expressed as a share of profit at all — $8.52bn of cumulative GAAP losses were posted while $205.2m went to the controller's vehicle, which says more about goodwill impairment than about leakage but is the honest framing of what minority holders paid for.

**Would the structure let leakage hide? Partly — and the weakness is structural, not transactional.** The group runs **145 entities across 31 jurisdiction labels with no published ownership chain**, three serially numbered holding companies implying at least four layers, roughly 20 subsidiaries whose business purpose cannot be identified from anything disclosed, and **82.2% of cash sitting in foreign subsidiaries at 2026-09-30 while all $2,500m of senior notes sit at the parent** and the repatriation tax is "not practicable to estimate". Against that: there are no VIEs or structured-finance entities, no loans or guarantees to any related party, no inter-corporate deposits, no promoter-linked customer anywhere on a $6.66bn revenue line, no royalty or brand fee (the core marks are owned inside the group), no related-party M&A including nothing aborted, every related-party counterparty named, a written $120,000 policy with the **independent directors** doing the approving, a Lead Independent Director with the ZMC agreement explicitly in her remit, and **4.66% say-on-pay dissent**. So the honest answer is that this group has the *capacity* for opacity and no *evidence* of using it — and the disclosure of the one thing that does flow is better than the pool suggested, not worse.

**The one disclosure that would settle the biggest open question: name the counterparty to the $62.1m non-cash acquisition of non-voting shares in a privately held entity, and say what was given for it.** That transaction quintupled the group's unconsolidated investment balance in six months, is structured in the one share class that keeps a stake of that size below significant influence, and sits in a fiscal year no proxy has yet covered — so it is the only material movement in this entire report whose counterparty nobody outside the company can identify. Everything else is named.

RF-CAP-004's cap binds Capital allocation via agent `02`, **not** this score, because deals are not the leakage channel here (09-024).
- **Confidence Score for this agent's own read: 75.** Not capped at 80 by the false-premise row above, but set from this agent's actual coverage: the RPT quantification rests on an **audited note (confidence 5)**; the approval-hygiene items rest on a **primary proxy section that was not rendered verbatim (confidence 3)**; the agreement's clause-level terms are **"Not proven from available data"**; **layer depth is undisclosed** and the inference is labelled as such; **recipe D-5 and the state registries were unreachable**; the **aborted-deal sweep has no 8-K feed**; the **ZMC portfolio view is partial**; and **numeric reading is unchecked across all 73 extracts**. Those are seven named, specific limits on a read whose core number is audited — 75, not higher, and not lower.
- **Partial-data rule applied honestly in both directions.** No component is marked "Insufficient Data" at the component level, because every component had real evidence. Two **rows** are Insufficient Data (09-031 layer depth; 09-049 numeric reading) and both are **scored as risk, not as zero** — 09-031 carries 2 points precisely so that an undisclosed ownership chain is not rewarded for being undisclosed.

# Regulatory, Legal & Compliance — TTWO

**Reachability declaration (read this first — it changes the caps triage pre-applied).** Triage `00` recorded that *its own* web/registry lookups were unreachable and told `07` and `12` to declare their own posture rather than inherit it. **My posture matches `07`'s: the managed search/fetch path WORKED and a genuine company-level sweep ran.** Reached and read: SEC EDGAR (company submissions API for CIK 0000946581, the Archives, full-text search over the issuer's own 8-K/10-K/10-Q history, the 2026 DEF 14A and the Item 5.07 annual-meeting 8-K), SEC litigation releases (via `07`'s primary rows), the FTC's own case library, court-record aggregators and dated trade/general media, rating aggregators, and the frozen filings themselves. **NOT reached:** PACER and any primary federal docket, state court portals, the UK employment-tribunal register, the OFAC search tool directly, Moody's/S&P/Fitch own rating pages (cbonds returned HTTP 403, ratings.moodys.com rendered a shell), and state attorney-general registers. Every verdict below names the axes that did not run. The triage's blanket "sweep did not run" cap is therefore **not inherited as written** — the sweep ran and is logged — but the **primary court-docket axis, which is exactly what A9-10 turns on, is coverage-limited**, so the MODULE_RULES floor of 40 is applied conservatively and the arithmetic from the evidence rows (25) is shown alongside it so `99` can see both.

**Pool-integrity facts carried forward (they define what this sweep had to replace).** The pool's DEF 14A export is an **empty vendor file** ("This filing has no tabular data to export"), and the pool's "Key Developments" export belongs to **Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL)**, not TTWO. **There is therefore no TTWO material-event / 8-K history inside the frozen evidence pool at all.** This sweep is the module's only route to the issuer's event history, and I built that history directly from EDGAR: the 8-K/10-Q/10-K/DEF 14A filing-date series, the Item 5.07 vote results, the Microsoft publishing agreement 8-K, and an EDGAR full-text pass over every TTWO 8-K ever filed that mentions "class action". What that means for completeness: the *filing-timeliness* and *vote-result* records are now **primary and complete** (EDGAR is the system of record for both), while the *litigation* record remains **aggregator-and-media-derived** because no primary docket system was reachable — so A9-10 is answered on a weaker evidence base than A7-01 or A9-06, and is graded accordingly.

**Numeric reading unchecked (travels forward).** This frozen generation carries **no `numeric_reading_check`** on any source or sheet, and `corpus.txt` carries no labelled extractor reading-warning annotation. A missing legacy check means **unchecked, not clean**. There is no literal warning token, source/extract reference or LF-line/column span to preserve, and **no amount in this report is marked not-proven on reading-warning grounds**. Every figure quoted here that becomes load-bearing — above all total stockholders' equity of **$3,673.6** (Sep-30-2026) and **$3,510.9** (Mar-31-2026), which are the materiality denominators — should be eyeballed against its frozen extract before it anchors a verdict. A reading warning is not itself an adverse company finding.

**Disqualifier deference.** `business-model/01_disqualifier-scan` reports verbatim: "Any disqualifier triggered: **N**"; "No disqualifier triggered"; "No lock applies." The regulatory-enforcement hard lock is **not** fired and I do not re-adjudicate it. Everything below is the spectrum beneath that lock.

**Language.** Every source read for this report is in English; nothing is recorded as a gap on language grounds (CLAUDE.md §27).

**Materiality denominators used throughout.** Total stockholders' equity **$3,510.9** at Mar-31-2026 and **$3,673.6** at Sep-30-2026 [`Q2 FY27 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets`]. On the FY26 base, the MODULE_RULES legal/regulatory bands are: Low <$17.6 · Medium $17.6–$70.2 · High $70.2–$175.5 · Critical >$175.5 (or an adjudicated criminal/fraud finding). ## 1. Regulator & Enforcement Register (A9-01, A9-02)

**5-year lookback window: 2021-11-19 → 2026-11-19.** Within that window, **no securities-regulator, antitrust, criminal or consumer-regulator enforcement action, consent order, settlement scheme, formal order of investigation, or lender/regulator-ordered forensic audit against Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. was found** — swept and logged (Sweep Log rows 1–6, 9–12, 18, 20), not merely "not disclosed". The company-level register in the window is **empty of enforcement**. What the sweep did find is a dated enforcement history that matters as base rate, and live *private* litigation, which is Section 8's subject, not this one's.

**Coverage-limited axes behind the two Green verdicts (stated, not buried).** (a) **No primary federal or state docket system was reachable** (PACER, state portals), so "no formal SEC order of investigation" rests on the absence of any SEC litigation release, administrative proceeding or EDGAR-disclosed matter — a strong but not exhaustive read. (b) **State attorney-general registers were not swept.** (c) **The group has roughly 150 subsidiaries** [`FY26 10-K, Ex. 21.1`]; this sweep ran the parent plus the governance-relevant subsidiaries that the discovery loop surfaced (Zynga, Rockstar Games UK / Rockstar North, and the lineage names in Section 1A) — it is not a 150-entity sweep, and I say so rather than imply one. (d) **One SEC staff comment letter exists** in the issuer's EDGAR correspondence (an `UPLOAD`, FY2021); the PDF returned binary and could not be read, so its subject is **Insufficient Data**. A staff comment letter is routine review correspondence, **not** an enforcement action, and is recorded as such.

**Where the enforcement story actually sits.** Take-Two's enforcement record is an old, severe, *adjudicated* fraud whose participants were permanently barred and removed in 2007, followed by nineteen clean years at company level. That is the opposite shape from the pattern the A9 register is designed to catch (a clean-looking present with a live regulator behind it), and the direction matters for the read in Section 9.

## 1A. Predecessor / Lineage Sweep Register (structured handoff — `99` reads this table)

**The name list was built by filtering `entity_network.json` on `lineage_relation`, never on `discovery_method`.** The listco's own `former_names` array is **empty** — EDGAR's `formerNames` field for CIK 0000946581 returns `[]`, independently re-confirmed by me on 2026-11-20 (Sweep Log row 1), and the company has filed under "TAKE TWO INTERACTIVE SOFTWARE INC" throughout. **There is no `former_name_of_listco` subject in this network**, so no name carries the direct-scoring treatment; that is a checked fact with its source, not a silent absence. Two subjects carry `lineage_relation: "predecessor_entity"` (BMG Interactive; THQ Inc.), and neither has a populated `former_names` array of its own, so the predecessor's-own-former-names expansion adds nothing. One further subject — DMA Design Holdings Limited — carries `lineage_relation: "none"` yet `07` expressly handed its courts/enforcement leg to me ("courts/enforcement on this name handed to `12`"), so I resolved it rather than silently dropping it. **Correctly filtered out and NOT swept into this company's register: Commerce.com, Inc. (formerly BigCommerce Holdings)**, which carries `discovery_method: "name-change trail"` for *its own* rename and `lineage_relation: "none"` — sweeping a director's other company's former name into Take-Two's legal register would be the entity-level twin of the namesake error.

**Scoring treatment, stated so it cannot be mistaken.** BMG Interactive and THQ Inc. are **`predecessor_entity` (arm's-length succession)**: anything found against them is **lineage EXPOSURE, not enforcement against the listco**, it travels to `07`/`99` under RF-NET-003 and the banded cap, and it does **not** enter the A9-01/A9-02 register or fire RF-REG-001. Neither carries a Disqualifying- or Material-equivalent fact: the single matter found is a 29-year-old contract judgment against DMA Design (not against BMG, not against Take-Two), and THQ's Chapter 11 is a **resolved third-party insolvency** from which assets were bought through a formal court process — which the lineage rule records as a **legitimate outcome**, not a flag. **RF-NET-003 does not fire on either band**, and neither predecessor's banded cap binds. I did **not** treat either as an absorbed-by-merger predecessor with successor liability: the scheme/merger documents are not in this evidence pool, so asserting that liabilities transferred would be an unsupported claim against the company (§3) rather than a conservative one — both stay in the arm's-length row with the coverage-limited cap. **No row above reads `resolved-clean`, because no row reads Coverage `full`**: a partial sweep that found nothing has established "not found on the axes that ran", not "clean".

### Exchange-fine register — 8 quarters, ALL exchanges

**Exchanges the stock trades on: ONE — the Nasdaq Global Select Market, ticker TTWO, single class of common stock, $0.01 par** [`FY26 10-K, cover page, Securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b)`]. **Regime note (the US has no quarterly exchange fine register).** India's NSE/BSE publish quarterly LODR non-compliance-and-fine files; **Nasdaq publishes no equivalent**. The US evidence set for the same question is: (a) any **Item 3.01 8-K** (notice of failure to satisfy a continued-listing rule or standard), (b) any Listing Qualifications deficiency letter, and (c) the 10-K cover's listing representation.
