## 8. Litigation-Register Reconciliation (A9-10)

**Start with what the company's own register says, because it is the whole finding.** Item 3 of the FY26 10-K points to Note 14; Item 1 of each FY27 10-Q points to Note 12; and all three notes carry **identical boilerplate**, verbatim:

> "We are, or may become, subject to demands and claims (including intellectual property and employment related claims) and are involved in routine litigation in the ordinary course of business which we do not believe to be material to our business or financial condition or results of operations. We have appropriately accrued amounts related to certain of these claims and legal and other proceedings. While it is reasonably possible that a loss may be incurred in excess of the amounts accrued in our financial statements, we believe that such losses, unless otherwise disclosed, would not be material."

**Not one case is named, in any of the three filings.** A grep of the FY26 10-K and both FY27 10-Qs returns **zero** occurrences of "class action", "putative", "derivative action", "securities litigation", "tribunal" (in a litigation sense) or "subpoena". The only named legal matter anywhere in the FY26 10-K sits in the **MD&A expense discussion**, not in the legal note: operating-expense variance was helped "by lower legal fees and contingencies related to **the IBM case against Zynga**". An EDGAR full-text pass shows **15 TTWO 8-Ks have mentioned "class action" historically — the most recent in 2022**, and none since.

The two matters that are *confirmed* on primary or company sources were disclosed through the correct channel (the IBM/Zynga verdict by 8-K) or needed no disclosure (IBM v. Take-Two, filed and dismissed in 94 days). The two matters that are *unconfirmed on primary records* — the securities class actions and the tribunal's quantum — are exactly where the coverage gap is, and the honest consequence is Amber with a named follow-up, not a red flag built on a press release.

**But record the pattern, because the pattern is the decision-relevant part.** This issuer's periodic legal disclosure names **zero cases across three consecutive filings**, while the public record over the same period contains a **$44.9m adverse jury verdict** against its largest acquisition, a **five-week blacklisting trial** against its most important studio with judgment pending, **at least one apparent federal securities class action**, and a **civil fraud claim against its chief executive personally**. Every one of those is individually defensible as immaterial or ordinary-course or somebody else's. Collectively, the legal note tells a reader nothing they could not have guessed before opening it. That is a disclosure-quality finding, shared with `06`, and it is why the Section 9 read lands where it does.

## 9. Read

**The public record does not contradict the filings — but it is far better informed than they are.** On the things that can be checked completely, Take-Two is clean and the compliance machinery is real: twelve consecutive quarters of on-time 10-Qs with zero NT filings in the issuer's entire history, no Nasdaq deficiency or fine across eight quarters, no securities-regulator or consumer-regulator enforcement in the five-year window, a clean Section 16(a) year, a BBB rating affirmed with no notch movement and no non-cooperation or withdrawal behaviour, a top-tier JPMorgan/Wells Fargo consortium on an undrawn unsecured revolver, and a Whistleblower Policy owned and annually approved by an audit committee of three independent directors. **The single worst legal/regulatory fact is not an enforcement action at all — it is that the legal note of three consecutive filings names no case whatsoever while the public record holds a $44.9m adverse verdict against Zynga, a five-week UK blacklisting trial against Rockstar with judgment pending as of today, and at least one apparent federal securities class action over the GTA VI delay disclosures that appears nowhere in any filing or 8-K since 2022.** None of that is provably a non-disclosure breach: each item is individually defensible, and I decline to fire RF-CMP-001 on a plaintiff-firm press release when the primary docket could not be reached. **Verdict: hygiene lapses, watch** — the lapse being candor in the legal note rather than compliance in the filing calendar, and the watch items being the pending tribunal judgment and the unconfirmed securities class action. Two things belong in front of the synthesis as caps: the **coverage-limited primary-docket axis**, which is why this module's score sits at the MODULE_RULES floor of 40 rather than the 25 its own evidence rows build to; and the fact that the decisive unknown is **one paid docket pull away** — the same single highest-value request `07` named, now with a second item on it.
